subject: Purposive Communication
stem: Which kind of communication model treats communication as a one-way process from sender to receiver?
options: Interaction model with a feedback loop

explanation.correct: Linear models are one-way; Lasswell's and Shannon–Weaver are examples.

subject: Purposive Communication
stem: Which of the following is NOT an early linear model of communication?

explanation.correct: Barnlund's model (1970s) is transactional.

subject: Purposive Communication
stem: What feature distinguishes an interaction model from a linear one?
options: A feedback loop from the receiver
A longer message from the sender
The absence of any receiver at all
The use of written messages only

explanation.correct: Interaction models add a feedback loop.

subject: Purposive Communication
stem: Students recite the Panatang Makabayan word for word at the flag ceremony. In Joos's styles, this register is:

explanation.correct: Frozen style is unchanging printed language such as pledges.

wrong.1: Formal style is one-way but not fixed wording.
wrong.3: Casual is in-group talk with slang.

subject: Purposive Communication
stem: A patient explains symptoms while the doctor says "uh huh" and asks follow-up questions. Which Joos style is this?

explanation.correct: Two-way talk with background and back-channel responses is consultative.

wrong.2: Intimate style is among family and close friends.

subject: Purposive Communication
stem: Which Joos style uses ellipsis and slang within an in-group?

explanation.correct: Casual style is in-group, with ellipsis and slang.

wrong.1: Formal uses technical vocabulary without interruption.
wrong.3: Consultative gives background in two-way talk.

subject: Purposive Communication
stem: In Joos's intimate style, meaning is carried more by:
options: Fixed printed text than by speech

explanation.correct: Intimate style relies on intonation over wording.

subject: Purposive Communication
stem: A speaker on food safety shows data on how many children fell ill after eating unsafe street food. Which appeal is mainly used?

explanation.correct: Credible facts and evidence are logos.

wrong.3: Kairos is not among the appeals in our source.

subject: Purposive Communication
stem: A nutritionist begins, "As a registered dietitian for twenty years…" Which appeal is this?

explanation.correct: Establishing an authoritative, credible voice is ethos.

wrong.3: That is a figure of speech.

subject: Purposive Communication
stem: An advertisement shows a crying child and a hungry family to urge donations. Which appeal is used?

explanation.correct: Appeals to shared feelings and emotions are pathos.

subject: Purposive Communication
stem: According to Lloyd Bitzer (1968), a rhetorical situation consists of:
options: An exigence (issue), an audience and constraints
A sender, a channel and noise

explanation.correct: Bitzer named these three parts.

wrong.1: These are appeals, not Bitzer's parts.

subject: Purposive Communication
stem: Who answered Bitzer with "The Myth of the Rhetorical Situation"?

explanation.correct: Vatz wrote the reply.

subject: Purposive Communication
stem: Which sentence shows correct subject–verb agreement?
options: The price of these shoes at all stores is unbelievable.
The price of these shoes at all stores are unbelievable.
The prices of these shoe at all stores is unbelievable.
The price of these shoes at all stores were unbelievable.

explanation.correct: The subject "price" is singular, so the verb is "is".

wrong.1: Words between subject and verb do not change agreement.

subject: Purposive Communication
stem: Choose the correct verb: "Neither the students nor the teacher ___ ready."

explanation.correct: With nor, the verb agrees with the closer subject, "teacher".

wrong.1: "Are" would agree with "students", which is farther.

subject: Purposive Communication
stem: Choose the correct verb: "Either the teacher or the students ___ the room."

explanation.correct: With or, the verb agrees with the closer subject, "students".

wrong.1: "Cleans" would agree with "teacher", which is farther.

subject: Purposive Communication
stem: Which sentence is correct?
options: Everyone in the class has a recipe book.
Everyone in the class have a recipe book.
Everyone in the class are having recipe books.
Everyone in the class were given their books.

explanation.correct: "Everyone" takes a singular verb.

subject: Purposive Communication
stem: "The new canteen which opened last June serves fresh fruit." If the clause is nonessential, where do the commas go?

explanation.correct: A nonessential clause is set off by commas on both sides.

wrong.1: The clause needs a closing comma too.
wrong.2: The clause needs an opening comma too.
wrong.3: These positions split the main clause.

subject: Purposive Communication
stem: "Students who finish early may help clean up." The clause "who finish early" is:
options: Essential, so it takes no commas

explanation.correct: It identifies which students, so it is essential.

subject: Purposive Communication
stem: Combining "The cake fell. The oven was too hot." into "The cake fell because the oven was too hot." creates a:
options: Complex sentence with a dependent clause
Compound sentence with two independent clauses joined by a comma alone

explanation.correct: A dependent clause joined to an independent clause makes a complex sentence.

wrong.1: That would be a comma splice.

subject: Purposive Communication
stem: "Her voice was as sweet as honey" is an example of:

explanation.correct: A comparison using "as" is a simile.

wrong.1: A metaphor does not use like or as.
wrong.2: Personification gives human traits to non-human things.

subject: Purposive Communication
stem: "The moon smiled down on the sleeping town" is an example of:

explanation.correct: Giving the moon a human action is personification.

subject: Purposive Communication
stem: "I've told you a million times to wash your hands!" uses:

explanation.correct: Deliberate exaggeration is hyperbole.

wrong.1: There is no like or as comparison.
wrong.3: The speaker means the exaggeration for emphasis, not the opposite.

subject: Purposive Communication
stem: "Deafening silence" is an example of:

explanation.correct: A two-word paradox of opposite terms is an oxymoron.

wrong.2: That uses a part for the whole.

subject: Purposive Communication
stem: "Buzz", "sizzle" and "tik-tak" are examples of:

explanation.correct: Words imitating sounds are onomatopoeia.

wrong.2: Metaphor compares without like or as.

subject: Purposive Communication
stem: "All hands on deck" (meaning all sailors) uses which figure of speech?
options: Synecdoche, a part standing for the whole
Simile, a comparison with like or as
Onomatopoeia, a word imitating a sound

explanation.correct: Hands stand for the whole people.

subject: Purposive Communication
stem: "Peter Piper picked a peck of pickled peppers" mainly shows:

explanation.correct: Repetition of the initial "p" sound is alliteration.

subject: Purposive Communication
stem: A guest speaker delivers a prepared lecture with technical terms, and the audience listens without interrupting. Which Joos style is this?

explanation.correct: Formal style is one-way, without interruption, with technical vocabulary.

wrong.1: That is two-way with back-channel responses.
wrong.2: That is in-group talk with slang.
wrong.3: That is private talk among close people.

subject: Purposive Communication
stem: A register is best defined as:
options: A variety of language used for a particular purpose or situation
A type of figure of speech

explanation.correct: The source defines register this way.

subject: Purposive Communication
stem: Non-linear (transactional) communication models are:

explanation.correct: Non-linear models are multi-directional.

subject: Purposive Communication
stem: A rhetorical analysis addresses the rhetorical situation, which means:
options: The conditions of communication surrounding the rhetoric
The grammar errors in the text
The number of words in the essay

explanation.correct: The source defines it this way.

subject: Purposive Communication
stem: Which sentence is correct?
options: Each of the cooks has an apron.
Each of the cooks have an apron.
Each of the cooks are having aprons.
Each of the cooks were given aprons.

explanation.correct: "Each" takes a singular verb.

subject: Purposive Communication
stem: "The classroom was a zoo" is an example of:

explanation.correct: It compares without like or as.

wrong.1: A simile uses like or as.

subject: Malayuning Komunikasyon sa Wikang Filipino
stem: Ayon sa Artikulo XIV Seksiyon 6 ng Konstitusyon ng 1987, ano ang wikang pambansa ng Pilipinas?

explanation.correct: Tahasang sinasabi ng Sek. 6 na Filipino ang wikang pambansa.

wrong.1: Batayan lamang ng wikang pambansa ang Tagalog noong 1937.
wrong.2: Pilipino ang tawag mula 1959; Filipino na sa Konstitusyon ng 1987.
wrong.3: Ingles ay wikang opisyal, hindi wikang pambansa.

subject: Malayuning Komunikasyon sa Wikang Filipino
stem: Ayon sa Konstitusyon ng 1987, ano ang mga wikang opisyal ng Pilipinas para sa komunikasyon at pagtuturo?
options: Filipino at, hangga't walang ibang itinatadhana ang batas, Ingles
Lahat ng wikang panrehiyon nang pantay-pantay

explanation.correct: Ito ang itinakda ng Sek. 7.

wrong.1: Kasama rin ang Ingles hangga't walang ibang batas.
wrong.2: Ang Kastila ay isinasalin lamang, hindi wikang opisyal.
wrong.3: Pantulong lamang ang mga wikang panrehiyon.

subject: Malayuning Komunikasyon sa Wikang Filipino
stem: Ayon sa Konstitusyon, ano ang papel ng mga wikang panrehiyon sa mga rehiyon?
options: Pantulong na wikang opisyal at pantulong na midyum ng pagtuturo
Pangunahing wikang pambansa ng buong bansa

explanation.correct: Ito ang itinakda ng Sek. 7.

wrong.2: Hindi ito ipinagbabawal; pantulong ang papel nito.

subject: Malayuning Komunikasyon sa Wikang Filipino
stem: Sa anong mga wika ipalalaganap ang Konstitusyon ng 1987, ayon sa Sek. 8?
options: Filipino at Ingles, at isasalin sa mga pangunahing wikang panrehiyon, Arabe at Kastila
Ingles lamang, dahil ito ang wika ng batas

explanation.correct: Ito ang nakasaad sa Sek. 8.

subject: Malayuning Komunikasyon sa Wikang Filipino
stem: Ayon sa Sek. 9 ng Artikulo XIV, ano ang itatatag ng Kongreso?
options: Isang komisyon ng wikang pambansa na may kinatawan ng iba't ibang rehiyon at disiplina
Isang paaralan ng Ingles sa bawat lalawigan
Isang korte para sa mga usaping pangwika
Isang samahan ng mga manunulat sa Kastila

explanation.correct: Ito ang itinatadhana ng Sek. 9.

subject: Malayuning Komunikasyon sa Wikang Filipino
stem: Anong kautusan noong 1937 ang nagpahayag na batay sa Tagalog ang wikang pambansa?

explanation.correct: Ang EO 134 (1937) ang nagpahayag nito.

wrong.1: Ito ang nagtatag ng Surian ng Wikang Pambansa noong 1936.
wrong.2: Ito ang lumikha sa Komisyon sa Wikang Filipino noong 1991.
wrong.3: Ito ang nagtakda ng Buwan ng Wika noong 1997.

subject: Malayuning Komunikasyon sa Wikang Filipino
stem: Kailan unang tinawag na "Pilipino" ang wikang pambansa?

explanation.correct: Tinawag itong Pilipino noong 1959.

wrong.1: Noon sinimulan ang pagsisikap para sa wikang pambansa.
wrong.2: Filipino na ang tawag sa Konstitusyon ng 1987.
wrong.3: Ito ang taon ng Buwan ng Wika.

subject: Malayuning Komunikasyon sa Wikang Filipino
stem: Sinong pangulo ang namuno sa pagsisikap para sa wikang pambansa noong panahon ng Commonwealth?

explanation.correct: Sinimulan ito noong 1935 sa pamumuno ni Quezon.

wrong.1: Siya ang nagtakda ng Buwan ng Wika noong 1997.
wrong.2: Siya ang pangulo ng Unang Republika.

subject: Malayuning Komunikasyon sa Wikang Filipino
stem: Alin ang tamang pagkakasunod-sunod ng mga ahensiyang pangwika?
options: Surian ng Wikang Pambansa, Linangan ng mga Wika sa Pilipinas, Komisyon sa Wikang Filipino
Komisyon sa Wikang Filipino, Surian ng Wikang Pambansa, Linangan ng mga Wika
Linangan ng mga Wika, Komisyon sa Wikang Filipino, Surian ng Wikang Pambansa
Surian ng Wikang Pambansa, Komisyon sa Wikang Filipino, Linangan ng mga Wika

explanation.correct: Ito ang pagkakasunod mula 1936 hanggang 1991.

subject: Malayuning Komunikasyon sa Wikang Filipino
stem: Anong batas ang lumikha sa Komisyon sa Wikang Filipino?

explanation.correct: Nilikha ang KWF sa bisa ng RA 7104.

wrong.1: Ito ang lumikha sa Linangan ng mga Wika sa Pilipinas.
wrong.3: Ito ang nagpahayag ng wikang pambansa batay sa Tagalog.

subject: Malayuning Komunikasyon sa Wikang Filipino
stem: Sinong pangulo ang gumawa sa Linggo ng Wika na Buwan ng Wikang Pambansa tuwing Agosto?
options: Fidel V. Ramos, sa Proklamasyon Blg. 1041 (1997)

explanation.correct: Ito ang nakasaad sa sanggunian.

wrong.1: Ang EO 134 ay tungkol sa batayan ng wikang pambansa.
wrong.2: Ang EO 117 ay tungkol sa Linangan.
wrong.3: Iyon ay tungkol sa batas militar.

subject: Malayuning Komunikasyon sa Wikang Filipino
stem: Ilang titik mayroon ang Abakada?

explanation.correct: May 20 titik ang Abakada.

wrong.1: Iyan ang bilang ng titik ng alpabetong Latin.

subject: Malayuning Komunikasyon sa Wikang Filipino
stem: Saang aklat ipinakilala ang Abakada?
options: Ang Balarila ng Wikang Pambansa ni Lope K. Santos
Noli Me Tángere ni José Rizal
Kartilya ng Katipunan ni Emilio Jacinto

explanation.correct: Doon ipinakilala ang Abakada.

wrong.1: Nobela ito, hindi aklat ng balarila.
wrong.3: Hindi ito ang aklat na tinutukoy ng sanggunian.

subject: Malayuning Komunikasyon sa Wikang Filipino
stem: Ilang titik mayroon ang kasalukuyang alpabetong Filipino (1987)?

explanation.correct: Ang 26 na titik ng alpabetong Latin, ang Ñ at ang NG.

wrong.3: Kulang ito ng Ñ at NG.

subject: Malayuning Komunikasyon sa Wikang Filipino
stem: Bukod sa 26 na titik ng alpabetong Latin, aling dalawang titik ang kasama sa alpabetong Filipino?

explanation.correct: Kasama ang Ñ at ang digrapong NG.

wrong.3: Hindi hiwalay na titik ang mga ito.

subject: Malayuning Komunikasyon sa Wikang Filipino
stem: Sa anong mga taon ginamit ang Abakada?

explanation.correct: Ginamit ang Abakada mula 1940 hanggang 1987.

wrong.1: Iyan ang panahon ng pinagyamang alpabeto.

subject: Malayuning Komunikasyon sa Wikang Filipino
stem: Anong aspekto ng pandiwa ang "kumain"?

explanation.correct: Tapos na ang kilos.

wrong.3: Ang katatapos ay kilos na kagagawa lamang.

subject: Malayuning Komunikasyon sa Wikang Filipino
stem: Anong aspekto ng pandiwa ang "magluluto"?

explanation.correct: Hindi pa nasisimulan ang kilos.

wrong.3: Ang katatapos ay kilos na kagagawa lamang, hindi pa magaganap.

subject: Malayuning Komunikasyon sa Wikang Filipino
stem: Sa aspektong naganap, ano ang nangyayari sa unang "m" ng mga panlaping mag-, ma- at mang-?

explanation.correct: Halimbawa: magluto → nagluto.

subject: Malayuning Komunikasyon sa Wikang Filipino
stem: Ang pandiwa sa Filipino ay binabanghay pangunahin ayon sa:

explanation.correct: Ayon sa sanggunian, aspekto at hindi tense ang batayan.

subject: Malayuning Komunikasyon sa Wikang Filipino
stem: Anong kayarian ng salita ang "balat-sibuyas"?

explanation.correct: Pinagsamang dalawang salita.

wrong.3: Ang inuulit ay inuulit ang salita o bahagi nito.

subject: Malayuning Komunikasyon sa Wikang Filipino
stem: Anong kayarian ng salita ang "pulang-pula"?

explanation.correct: Inuulit ang salitang "pula".

wrong.1: Ang tambalan ay pinagsamang dalawang magkaibang salita.
wrong.3: Ang pag-uulit ang pangunahing katangian dito.

subject: Malayuning Komunikasyon sa Wikang Filipino
stem: Anong kayarian ng salita ang "hinog"?

explanation.correct: Salitang-ugat lamang ito.

subject: Malayuning Komunikasyon sa Wikang Filipino
stem: Anong uri ng pamilang ang "ikatlo"?

explanation.correct: Ipinakikita nito ang pagkakasunod.

subject: Malayuning Komunikasyon sa Wikang Filipino
stem: Anong uri ng pamilang ang "kalahati"?

explanation.correct: Bahagi ng kabuuan ang ipinakikita.

subject: Malayuning Komunikasyon sa Wikang Filipino
stem: Anong antas ng paghahambing ang "pinakamaliit"?

explanation.correct: Ginagamit ang pinaka- sa pasukdol.

wrong.2: Ginagamit dito ang sing-, kasing- o magsing-.
wrong.3: Ginagamit dito ang higit, lalo o mas.

subject: Malayuning Komunikasyon sa Wikang Filipino
stem: Sa pangungusap na "Di-gaanong mainit ang sabaw kaysa sa kape," anong uri ng paghahambing ang ginamit?

explanation.correct: Ginagamit ang di-gaano o di-gasino sa pasahol.

wrong.1: Ginagamit dito ang higit, lalo o mas.
wrong.2: Ginagamit dito ang pinaka-, ubod o saksakan.

subject: Malayuning Komunikasyon sa Wikang Filipino
stem: Anong uri ng pang-uri ang "Ingles" sa pariralang "wikang Ingles"?

explanation.correct: Tiyak na pangalan ang tinutukoy.

wrong.1: Naglalarawan ito ng laki, kulay, hugis o lasa.

subject: Malayuning Komunikasyon sa Wikang Filipino
stem: Aling pang-angkop ang ginagamit kapag nagtatapos sa katinig (maliban sa n) ang naunang salita, gaya ng "mapagmahal ___ tao"?

explanation.correct: Ginagamit ang "na" pagkatapos ng katinig maliban sa n.

wrong.1: Ginagamit ang -ng pagkatapos ng patinig o n.
wrong.2: Ginagamit ang -g sa salitang nagtatapos sa n.

subject: Malayuning Komunikasyon sa Wikang Filipino
stem: Alin ang tamang pagkakagamit ng pang-angkop?

explanation.correct: Nagtatapos sa patinig ang "mabuti", kaya -ng.

subject: Malayuning Komunikasyon sa Wikang Filipino
stem: Aling pangatnig ang nagpapahayag ng layunin?

explanation.correct: Ginagamit ang "upang" sa layunin.

subject: Malayuning Komunikasyon sa Wikang Filipino
stem: Sa pangungusap na "Mag-aaral ako nang mabuti, ngunit pagod na ako," ano ang gamit ng "ngunit"?

explanation.correct: Ang "ngunit" ay pangatnig na nagpapahayag ng pagsalungat.

subject: Malayuning Komunikasyon sa Wikang Filipino
stem: Ayon sa RA 12027 (2024), ano ang nangyari sa mother tongue bilang midyum ng pagtuturo mula Kindergarten hanggang Baitang 3?
options: Itinigil ito; bumalik sa Filipino at Ingles
Ginawang tanging wika sa lahat ng baitang

explanation.correct: Ito ang itinakda ng Sek. 1.

subject: Malayuning Komunikasyon sa Wikang Filipino
stem: Aling pangatnig ang nagpapahayag ng kondisyon?

explanation.correct: Ang "kung" ay pangatnig ng kondisyon.

subject: Malayuning Komunikasyon sa Wikang Filipino
stem: Alin ang tamang pang-angkop sa "huwaran ___ mamamayan"?

explanation.correct: Kapag nagtatapos sa n, -ng ang ginagamit: huwarang.

wrong.1: Ginagamit ang "na" sa katinig maliban sa n.
wrong.3: Ikinakabit ito sa salita, hindi hiwalay.

subject: Malayuning Komunikasyon sa Wikang Filipino
stem: Anong antas ng paghahambing ang "magsinggaling"?

explanation.correct: Ginagamit ang magsing- sa paghahambing na magkatulad.

subject: Malayuning Komunikasyon sa Wikang Filipino
stem: Ilang titik mayroon ang pinagyamang alpabeto na ginamit mula 1977 hanggang 1987?

explanation.correct: May 31 titik ito.

subject: Readings in Philippine History
stem: A student reads a 2015 textbook chapter that interprets Pigafetta's journal. The textbook chapter is a:

explanation.correct: It interprets a primary source.

wrong.1: Pigafetta's journal is the primary source.
wrong.2: A textbook chapter interpreting sources is secondary.

subject: Readings in Philippine History
stem: Which statement about primary sources is correct?
options: They are not necessarily more authoritative than secondary sources
They are always more reliable than any secondary source
They are always written by historians long after events
They cannot include diaries or letters

explanation.correct: The source makes this point.

wrong.3: Diaries and letters can be primary sources.

subject: Readings in Philippine History
stem: On what date was the Battle of Mactan fought?

explanation.correct: The battle took place on April 27, 1521.

wrong.1: That is not the battle date given.
wrong.2: That is the Declaration of Independence.

subject: Readings in Philippine History
stem: Whose account is the source of the troop figures for the Battle of Mactan?

explanation.correct: The figures come from Pigafetta's account.

wrong.3: He wrote the Declaration of Independence.

subject: Readings in Philippine History
stem: Where did the Cavite Mutiny of January 20, 1872 take place?

explanation.correct: The uprising was at Fort San Felipe.

wrong.2: That is linked to the Cry.
wrong.3: That is where independence was declared.

subject: Readings in Philippine History
stem: Which deductions from laborers' pay sparked the Cavite Mutiny?
options: Taxes and the falla, a fee for exemption from forced labor
The cédula and a church tithe only

explanation.correct: The source names these.

wrong.1: That is not the cause given.
wrong.2: That is not the cause given.
wrong.3: That is not the cause given.

subject: Readings in Philippine History
stem: Which three secular priests were implicated in the Cavite Mutiny and executed?
options: Mariano Gómez, José Burgos and Jacinto Zamora
Andrés Bonifacio, Emilio Jacinto and José Rizal
Emilio Aguinaldo, Apolinario Mabini and Antonio Luna
Lapulapu, Rajah Humabon and Rajah Sulayman

explanation.correct: These are the Gomburza priests.

wrong.1: These are revolutionary figures, not the priests.

subject: Readings in Philippine History
stem: According to modern consensus, when was the Katipunan founded?

explanation.correct: The source gives July 7, 1892, after Rizal's arrest.

wrong.1: That is a date given for the Cry.
wrong.2: That is the Declaration of Independence.
wrong.3: That is the Treaty of Paris.

subject: Readings in Philippine History
stem: Who wrote the first edition of the Kartilya ng Katipunan?

explanation.correct: The source credits Emilio Jacinto.

wrong.1: Bonifacio led the Katipunan, but Jacinto wrote the first Kartilya.

subject: Readings in Philippine History
stem: Why are the date and place of the Cry disputed?
options: Accounts differ; it was long held as August 26 in Balintawak, then August 23 was declared in 1963
No document mentions the Cry at all

explanation.correct: The source explains this history.

subject: Readings in Philippine History
stem: The Cry of 1896 is associated with tearing which documents?

explanation.correct: The Cry may refer to tearing the cédulas.

subject: Readings in Philippine History
stem: Who wrote the Philippine Declaration of Independence of June 12, 1898?

explanation.correct: The source credits Bautista.

subject: Readings in Philippine History
stem: Where was the Declaration of Independence proclaimed?

explanation.correct: The source gives Kawit, Cavite.

wrong.2: That is linked to the Cry.

subject: Readings in Philippine History
stem: The Malolos Constitution named the state the:

explanation.correct: It declared the state the Philippine Republic.

subject: Readings in Philippine History
stem: The Treaty of Paris, which ended the Spanish–American War, was signed on:

explanation.correct: The treaty was signed on December 10, 1898.

wrong.1: That is the Declaration of Independence.
wrong.2: That is not the treaty date.
wrong.3: That is not the treaty date given.

subject: Readings in Philippine History
stem: How much was paid to Spain in connection with the cession of the Philippines under the Treaty of Paris?

explanation.correct: The source gives US$20 million.

subject: Readings in Philippine History
stem: The Tydings–McDuffie Act (1934) provided for:
options: A ten-year transition to independence and a Commonwealth constitution
Return of the islands to Spain

explanation.correct: The Act set these.

subject: Readings in Philippine History
stem: When did Ferdinand Marcos announce Proclamation No. 1081 placing the country under martial law?

explanation.correct: The source gives September 23, 1972 as the announcement date.

wrong.1: That is the end of the EDSA revolution.
wrong.2: That is when martial law was formally lifted.
wrong.3: That is not the date given.

subject: Readings in Philippine History
stem: Martial law was formally lifted on January 17, 1981, by which proclamation?

explanation.correct: The source names Proclamation No. 2045.

subject: Readings in Philippine History
stem: The 1973 Constitution created which form of legislature?
options: A parliamentary-style National Assembly with a Prime Minister
A bicameral Congress of Senate and House

explanation.correct: The source describes this.

subject: Readings in Philippine History
stem: The People Power Revolution at EDSA took place on:

explanation.correct: The source gives these dates.

wrong.1: That is the start of martial law.
wrong.3: That is not the event in our source.

subject: Readings in Philippine History
stem: RA 10908 (Integrated History Act of 2016) integrates the history and culture of which groups into Philippine history?

explanation.correct: RA 10908 covers these groups.

wrong.1: That is not the law's focus.
wrong.2: That is not the law's focus.
wrong.3: That is not the law's focus.

subject: Readings in Philippine History
stem: Which article of the 1987 Constitution is the Bill of Rights?

explanation.correct: The Bill of Rights is Article III.

wrong.1: Article XIV covers education and culture.
wrong.3: Article II covers principles and state policies.

subject: Readings in Philippine History
stem: How many consecutive terms may a senator serve under the 1987 Constitution?
options: No more than two, of six years each
No more than three, of three years each

explanation.correct: Art. VI Sec. 4 sets this.

wrong.1: That is the rule for House members.

subject: Readings in Philippine History
stem: What is the term of the President under the 1987 Constitution?

explanation.correct: Art. VII Sec. 4 sets this.

wrong.2: The President is not eligible for re-election.

subject: Readings in Philippine History
stem: Judicial power under the 1987 Constitution is vested in:
options: One Supreme Court and lower courts

explanation.correct: Art. VIII Sec. 1 vests judicial power this way.

subject: Readings in Philippine History
stem: Which regions does the 1987 Constitution name as autonomous regions?

explanation.correct: Art. X names these.

wrong.1: These are not named as autonomous.
wrong.2: These are not named as autonomous.
wrong.3: These are not named as autonomous.

subject: Life and Works of Rizal
stem: Under RA 1425 (the Rizal Law), courses on Rizal's life and works must be included in the curricula of:
options: All schools, colleges and universities, public or private
Only public high schools in Laguna
Only state universities offering history degrees

explanation.correct: Sec. 1 covers all schools, public or private.

wrong.1: The law covers all schools nationwide.

subject: Life and Works of Rizal

stem: Under RA 9003, segregation and collection of biodegradable and reusable wastes is done at which level?
options: Household only, with no LGU role

explanation.correct: Sec. 10 assigns this to the barangay level.

wrong.1: The law assigns it to barangays.
wrong.2: The law assigns it to barangays.

subject: Science, Technology and Society
stem: Under RA 9003, each LGU had to divert at least what share of its solid waste within five years?

explanation.correct: Sec. 20 requires at least 25%.

subject: Science, Technology and Society
stem: Under RA 9003, where must a Materials Recovery Facility be established?
options: In every barangay or cluster of barangays

explanation.correct: Sec. 32 requires this.

wrong.2: The rule is per barangay or cluster.
wrong.3: The rule is per barangay or cluster.

subject: Science, Technology and Society
stem: What does RA 9003 say about open dumps?
options: No open dumps may be established or operated after the law took effect
Open dumps are allowed in rural areas
Open dumps are encouraged for biodegradables
Open dumps must be used for all hazardous waste

explanation.correct: Sec. 37 bans open dumps.

subject: Mathematics
stem: Evaluate 18 ÷ 3 × 2 + 4.

explanation.correct: Divide and multiply left to right: 18 ÷ 3 = 6, 6 × 2 = 12, then 12 + 4 = 16.

wrong.1: That multiplies 3 × 2 first and divides 18 by 6, then adds 4.
wrong.3: That is not the result of any correct order.

subject: Mathematics
stem: Evaluate 2 + 3² × 4.

explanation.correct: Exponent first (9), then 9 × 4 = 36, then 2 + 36 = 38.

subject: Mathematics
stem: Which number is prime?

explanation.correct: 29 has only two divisors, 1 and itself.

subject: Mathematics
stem: Which number is divisible by 3?

explanation.correct: Its digits sum to 15, which is divisible by 3.

subject: Mathematics
stem: A teacher has 24 eggs and 36 cupcakes to split into identical boxes with no leftovers. What is the greatest number of boxes possible?

explanation.correct: The GCD of 24 and 36 is 12.

wrong.1: 6 works but is not the greatest.
wrong.3: 4 works but is not the greatest.

subject: Mathematics
stem: One bell rings every 6 minutes and another every 8 minutes. If both ring now, after how many minutes will they ring together again?

explanation.correct: The LCM of 6 and 8 is 24.

wrong.1: 48 is a common multiple but not the least.
wrong.2: Adding the intervals does not give the LCM.

subject: Mathematics
stem: Simplify x⁵ · x³.

explanation.correct: Product rule: add exponents.

wrong.3: The bases are multiplied, not added.

subject: Mathematics
stem: What is the value of 125⁰?

explanation.correct: Any non-zero number to the zeroth power equals 1.

wrong.2: The zero exponent does not leave the base unchanged.

subject: Mathematics
stem: What is 2⁻³?

explanation.correct: A negative exponent means the reciprocal: 1/2³ = 1/8.

wrong.1: A negative exponent does not make the value negative.

subject: Mathematics
stem: What is the 10th term of the arithmetic sequence 4, 7, 10, 13, …?

subject: Mathematics
stem: What is the next term of the geometric sequence 5, 15, 45, …?

explanation.correct: The common ratio is 3: 45 × 3 = 135.

subject: Mathematics
stem: A recipe uses 3 cups of flour for 2 cakes. How many cups are needed for 8 cakes?

subject: Mathematics
stem: What are the solutions of x² − 5x + 6 = 0?

explanation.correct: Using the quadratic formula: [5 ± √(25 − 24)]/2 = 3 or 2.

wrong.2: These multiply to 6 but sum to 7.

subject: Mathematics
stem: The word "percent" comes from the Latin per centum, meaning:

explanation.correct: Percent means "by the hundred".

subject: Mathematics
stem: ₱8,000 is deposited at 3% simple interest per year for 4 years. How much interest is earned?

subject: Mathematics
stem: In the compound interest formula A = P(1 + r/n)^(nt), what does n stand for?
options: The number of compounding periods per year
The number of years of the loan

explanation.correct: n is the compounding frequency.

subject: Mathematics
stem: A blouse priced at ₱500 is sold at 20% off. What is the sale price?

wrong.2: That is the discount, not the price.

subject: Mathematics
stem: In how many ways can a president, secretary and treasurer be chosen from 6 club members?

explanation.correct: Order matters: 6P3 = 6 × 5 × 4 = 120.

wrong.3: That allows the same person to hold several posts.

subject: Mathematics
stem: In how many ways can a committee of 3 be chosen from 6 members?

explanation.correct: Order does not matter: 6C3 = 6!/(3!3!) = 20.

subject: Mathematics
stem: What is the value of 0!?

explanation.correct: By definition, 0! = 1.

subject: Mathematics
stem: A bag has 3 red, 5 blue and 2 green marbles. What is the probability of drawing a blue marble?

subject: Mathematics
stem: Which value CANNOT be a probability?

explanation.correct: Probabilities lie between 0 and 1 inclusive.

subject: Mathematics
stem: Two angles of a triangle measure 48° and 67°. What is the third angle?

wrong.3: Angles of a triangle sum to 180°.

subject: Mathematics
stem: A right triangle has legs of 6 cm and 8 cm. What is the hypotenuse?

subject: Mathematics
stem: What is the area of a triangle with base 10 m and height 7 m?

subject: Mathematics
stem: A circular table top has a radius of 7 dm. Using π ≈ 22/7, what is its area?

subject: Mathematics
stem: A rectangular prism has a base of 4 cm by 5 cm and a height of 3 cm. What is its volume?

wrong.2: That is not a correct computation.
wrong.3: That is only the base area.

subject: Mathematics
stem: In a class, 20 like adobo, 15 like sinigang and 8 like both. How many like at least one of the two?

wrong.1: That forgets to subtract the overlap.

subject: Mathematics
stem: If A = {1, 2, 3, 4} and B = {3, 4, 5}, what is A ∩ B?

explanation.correct: The intersection has elements in both sets.

subject: Mathematics
stem: When is the conditional statement "If p, then q" false?
options: Only when p is true and q is false
When both p and q are false

explanation.correct: A conditional is false only in this case.

wrong.1: A false hypothesis makes the conditional true.
wrong.2: A true conclusion makes it true.

subject: Mathematics
stem: What is the cardinal number of the set {a, e, i, o, u}?

explanation.correct: The cardinal number is the number of elements.

wrong.2: That is the number of letters in the alphabet.

subject: Ethics
stem: Someone argues, "People naturally compete, so competition is morally good." Which error does this commit?
options: The fallacy of the hypothetical imperative

explanation.correct: Deriving what ought to be from what is commits the naturalistic fallacy.

wrong.1: That is not the error described.
wrong.2: That is a moral theory, not an error.

subject: Ethics
stem: The naturalistic fallacy is closely related to which philosopher's problem?

explanation.correct: The source links them.

subject: Ethics
stem: Moral relativism is described in our source as:
options: An anti-realist position denying objective or universal justification for moral beliefs
A realist view that moral facts exist objectively
A form of consequentialism from China
A virtue theory based on habit

explanation.correct: The source describes it this way.

subject: Ethics
stem: Which philosopher first articulated the principle of utility?

explanation.correct: Bentham first articulated the principle of utility.

subject: Ethics
stem: A principal decides each case by asking which choice gives the greatest happiness to the greatest number in that situation. This is:

explanation.correct: Applying the principle case by case is act utilitarianism.

wrong.1: Rule utilitarians set general rules first.
wrong.2: Kant judges by duty, not results.

subject: Ethics
stem: A school adopts the rule "always tell parents the truth about grades" because following it generally produces the best results. This reflects:

explanation.correct: Using the greatest happiness principle to set moral rules is rule utilitarianism.

wrong.1: Act utilitarians judge each case separately.

subject: Ethics
stem: Mohism, founded by Mozi, is an early Chinese form of:

explanation.correct: The source calls Mohism an early form of consequentialism.

subject: Ethics
stem: The word "deontology" comes from Greek roots meaning:

explanation.correct: Deon means duty and logos means study.

subject: Ethics
stem: For Kant, the only thing of unconditional value is:

explanation.correct: Kant holds that only a good will has unconditional value.

subject: Ethics
stem: A student copies a classmate's work, thinking, "Would I want everyone to copy whenever it helps them?" Which Kantian test is he using?

explanation.correct: Asking whether a maxim could be a universal law is the universal law test.

wrong.1: That asks whether people are treated as ends.

subject: Ethics
stem: A vendor flatters a customer only to trick her into overpaying. Which Kantian principle does this violate most directly?
options: Treating humanity always as an end, never merely as a means

explanation.correct: Using someone merely as a means violates the humanity formulation.

subject: Ethics
stem: How does a categorical imperative differ from a hypothetical imperative?
options: It must be obeyed regardless of one's desires
It applies only if one wants a certain goal

explanation.correct: Categorical imperatives bind regardless of desires.

wrong.3: It applies to all rational agents.

subject: Ethics
stem: W. D. Ross held that a moral theory ignoring either duty or consequences:

explanation.correct: Ross said this; consequences matter in light of duties.

subject: Ethics
stem: For the ancient Greeks, the aim of life was eudaimonia, meaning:
options: A life of strict duty only

explanation.correct: Eudaimonia is a flourishing life.

subject: Ethics
stem: Courage lies between cowardice and recklessness. This illustrates Aristotle's idea that a virtue is:
options: A mean between two vices, deficiency and excess
A rule that must be obeyed regardless of desire
An action producing the greatest happiness

explanation.correct: Aristotle describes virtue as a mean.

subject: Ethics
stem: According to Aristotle, moral virtues come about as a result of:

explanation.correct: Moral virtues come from habit (Nicomachean Ethics II).

wrong.2: Laws are not the source named.
wrong.3: Luck is not the source named.

subject: Ethics
stem: Wu wei is central to which ethical tradition?

explanation.correct: Wu wei is central to Daoist ethics.

subject: Ethics
stem: Carol Gilligan (1982) found that, in her studies, men more often approached moral problems from justice and women from:

explanation.correct: Gilligan contrasted justice and care perspectives.

subject: Ethics
stem: Who wrote Caring (1984), developing the care perspective?

explanation.correct: Noddings wrote Caring.

wrong.1: Gilligan's 1982 work contrasted justice and care; Caring is by Noddings.

subject: Ethics
stem: Under RA 11476, what did GMRC and Values Education replace?

explanation.correct: RA 11476 replaces EsP with GMRC and Values Education.

subject: Ethics
stem: Under RA 11476, Values Education is a separate subject in:

explanation.correct: Values Education covers Grades 7–10; GMRC covers Grades 1–6.

subject: Ethics
stem: RA 11476 defines GMRC as:
options: Universally accepted basic social values and etiquette that convey respect to others

explanation.correct: Sec. 3(c) defines it this way.

wrong.3: It is not a reading test.

subject: Ethics
stem: The naturalistic fallacy is the error of:
options: Deriving what people ought to do from what is
Judging acts only by their consequences
Focusing on character instead of rules

explanation.correct: The source defines it this way.

wrong.1: That is moral realism, not a fallacy.

subject: Ethics
stem: A student says, "No moral belief is truly right or wrong for everyone; it depends on each culture." Which position is this?

explanation.correct: Denying universal justification for moral beliefs is relativism.

wrong.3: That sets general rules by utility.

subject: Ethics
stem: According to our source, moral debate challenges moral realism by:
options: Proving all moral claims are false
Showing that duty is the only value

explanation.correct: The source says debate challenges realism this way.

subject: Ethics
stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the three main approaches to normative moral theory in our source?

explanation.correct: The three approaches are consequentialist, deontological and virtue ethics.

wrong.1: This is one of the three.
wrong.2: This is one of the three.
wrong.3: This is one of the three.

subject: Ethics
stem: John Stuart Mill's greatest happiness principle holds that actions are right if they:
options: Produce the greatest happiness for the greatest number
Follow a universal law regardless of results
Hit the mean between two vices

explanation.correct: That is Mill's principle.

subject: Ethics
stem: What criticism of act utilitarianism does our source mention?
options: It can seem to justify actions far beyond ordinary moral standards
It forbids any rules at all

explanation.correct: The source notes this concern.

wrong.3: Rule utilitarians use rules; act utilitarians judge cases.

subject: Ethics
stem: A cashier returns extra change to a customer only because she wants a reputation for honesty. For Kant, her act lacks moral worth mainly because:
options: It is not done from a good will doing its duty
It is not a mean between two vices

explanation.correct: Kant values the good will acting from duty.

subject: Ethics
stem: "If you want to pass, study" is an example of which kind of imperative?

explanation.correct: It depends on a desire (wanting to pass).

wrong.1: Categorical imperatives bind regardless of desires.
wrong.2: That is a test of maxims.
wrong.3: That concerns treating people as ends.

subject: Ethics
stem: W. D. Ross is best described as a:

explanation.correct: Ross was a pluralist deontologist.

subject: Ethics
stem: Virtue ethics takes which kind of approach to morality?

explanation.correct: Virtue ethics focuses on character.

subject: Ethics
stem: Generosity lies between stinginess and wastefulness. According to Aristotle, which part is the vice of excess?

explanation.correct: Giving too much is the excess; stinginess is the deficiency.

wrong.3: That is not part of this triad.

subject: Ethics
stem: Which of the following is NOT named in our source among the ancient Greeks for whom the aim of life was eudaimonia?

explanation.correct: Kant was an 18th-century German philosopher.

subject: Ethics
stem: Who is regarded as the founder of Daoism in our source?

explanation.correct: Laozi (6th century BCE) is named as the founder.

wrong.2: Confucius is not named here as Daoism's founder.

subject: Ethics
stem: Daoism began during which period of Chinese history?

explanation.correct: The source places Daoism's beginnings there.

subject: Ethics
stem: A teacher decides how to handle a cheating case by focusing on her relationship with the student and his needs, rather than on abstract rules. Which approach is this?

explanation.correct: Care ethics focuses on relationships and care.

subject: Ethics
stem: Under RA 11476, GMRC in kindergarten is:

explanation.correct: GMRC is integrated in kindergarten and a separate subject in Grades 1–6.

subject: Ethics
stem: Under RA 11476, GMRC is a separate subject in which grades?

explanation.correct: GMRC is a separate subject in Grades 1–6.

subject: Understanding the Self
stem: In Descartes's dualism, the mind is a "thinking thing" called:

explanation.correct: The mind is res cogitans; the body is res extensa.

wrong.1: That is the extended, non-thinking body.
wrong.3: That term is not in our source here.

subject: Understanding the Self
stem: David Hume's bundle theory holds that the self is:
options: A bundle of perceptions in perpetual flux
An unchanging soul created at birth
A thinking thing separate from the body

explanation.correct: Hume described the self this way.

subject: Understanding the Self
stem: Which Buddhist concept denies a permanent self?

explanation.correct: Anatman denies a permanent self.

wrong.2: That is a Greek ethical goal.

subject: Understanding the Self
stem: John Locke described a person as a thinking being who can:
options: Consider itself as itself, the same thinking thing in different times and places
Exist only as a bundle without any continuity
Be fully defined by the body's extension

explanation.correct: Locke's definition stresses continuity of consciousness.

subject: Understanding the Self
stem: Charles Cooley's "looking glass self" means that:
options: Our self-understanding is built partly from how we think others see us
We are born with a complete self
The self is a bundle of perceptions

explanation.correct: Cooley's idea is about others' perceived views.

subject: Understanding the Self
stem: Which order follows Mead's stages of developing the self?

explanation.correct: Mead's path runs from imitation to the generalized other.

wrong.2: The game stage comes after play.

subject: Understanding the Self
stem: A child playing "teacher" acts out the role of one other person. Which Mead stage is this?
options: Game stage, many roles at once

explanation.correct: Taking the role of one other person is the play stage.

wrong.1: That stage is imitation without role-taking.

subject: Understanding the Self
stem: According to our sociology source, the first agent of socialization is:

explanation.correct: The family is the first agent of socialization.

subject: Understanding the Self
stem: In Carl Rogers's theory, congruence occurs when:
options: The real self and the ideal self are very similar
A person ignores how others see them

explanation.correct: Rogers defines congruence this way.

subject: Understanding the Self
stem: A parent says, "I love you no matter what, even when you make mistakes." In Rogers's terms, this is:

explanation.correct: Acceptance without conditions is unconditional positive regard.

subject: Understanding the Self
stem: Which trait is NOT part of the Big Five (Five Factor Model)?

explanation.correct: The Big Five are openness, conscientiousness, extroversion, agreeableness and neuroticism.

wrong.1: This is a Big Five trait.
wrong.2: This is a Big Five trait.
wrong.3: This is a Big Five trait.

subject: Understanding the Self
stem: How many personality factors did Raymond Cattell identify?

explanation.correct: Cattell identified 16 factors.

wrong.1: Five is the Big Five model.
wrong.3: That is the number of words Allport found.

subject: Understanding the Self
stem: Which neo-Freudian proposed the collective unconscious?

explanation.correct: Jung proposed the collective unconscious.

subject: Understanding the Self
stem: Alfred Adler's individual psychology emphasizes the drive to compensate for:

explanation.correct: Adler stressed compensating for inferiority.

subject: Understanding the Self
stem: Collectivist cultures tend to value:
options: Social harmony, respectfulness and group needs
Independence and personal achievement above the group

explanation.correct: Collectivist cultures put group needs first.

subject: Understanding the Self
stem: A student commits to becoming a nurse because her parents chose it, without exploring other options. In Marcia's model, she is in:

explanation.correct: Commitment without exploration is foreclosure.

wrong.3: Diffusion is low commitment and not seeking.

subject: Understanding the Self
stem: A college sophomore is actively trying different majors and has not decided. In Marcia's model, he is in:

explanation.correct: Exploring without commitment is moratorium.

subject: Understanding the Self
stem: After exploring several careers, a young adult firmly commits to teaching. Which identity status is this?

explanation.correct: Exploration followed by commitment is achievement.

subject: Understanding the Self
stem: Under RA 11036, mental health is a state of well-being in which a person:
options: Realizes own abilities, copes with normal stresses, works productively and contributes to the community
Never feels any stress at all
Agrees with everyone in the community

explanation.correct: Sec. 4(j) defines it this way.

wrong.1: The definition involves coping with stress.
wrong.2: The definition is about well-being, not only physical health.

subject: Understanding the Self
stem: In Descartes's dualism, the body is described as:

explanation.correct: Descartes called the body res extensa.

wrong.2: That is Hume's view of the self.

subject: Understanding the Self
stem: In Hindu traditions, the self is called:

explanation.correct: The Hindu self is atman.

wrong.1: That is the Buddhist denial of a permanent self.
wrong.3: That is a Greek ethical aim.

subject: Understanding the Self
stem: A student says, "When I look inside, I never find a 'self', only feelings, sights and thoughts that keep changing." Which philosopher's view does this echo?

explanation.correct: Hume saw the self as a changing bundle of perceptions.

subject: Understanding the Self
stem: A teenager decides she is a good cook because her family always praises her dishes. Which concept explains this?

explanation.correct: Self-understanding built from how we think others see us.

wrong.1: That is about perceptions in flux.

subject: Understanding the Self
stem: According to Mead, the ability to see oneself through others' eyes is:
options: Learned through social interaction, not inborn

explanation.correct: Mead held the self is learned.

subject: Understanding the Self
stem: In a basketball game, a child understands what each teammate and opponent is expected to do. Which Mead stage is this?

explanation.correct: Considering several roles at once is the game stage.

wrong.1: The play stage takes one other's role.

subject: Understanding the Self
stem: A toddler copies her father shaving without understanding the role. Which Mead stage is this?

explanation.correct: The preparatory stage is imitation only.

wrong.1: The play stage takes on a role.
wrong.2: The game stage handles several roles.
wrong.3: That is the final understanding of society's expectations.

subject: Understanding the Self
stem: Which of the following is NOT listed as an agent of socialization in our source?

explanation.correct: The listed agents are family, peer groups, media, schools, workplaces and government.

subject: Understanding the Self
stem: In Rogers's theory, self-concept means:
options: Our thoughts and feelings about ourselves
Our score on an IQ test
The opinions of our neighbors only

explanation.correct: Rogers defines self-concept this way.

subject: Understanding the Self
stem: Maslow developed his ideas about self-actualization by studying:

explanation.correct: The source says so.

subject: Understanding the Self
stem: The Eysencks proposed which two dimensions of personality?

explanation.correct: The Eysencks proposed these two dimensions.

subject: Understanding the Self
stem: About how many English words describing people did Gordon Allport find?

explanation.correct: Allport found about 4,500 words.

subject: Understanding the Self
stem: Karen Horney held that growth can be blocked by:

explanation.correct: Horney stressed basic anxiety.

subject: Understanding the Self
stem: Which of the following is NOT listed among the neo-Freudians in our source?

explanation.correct: Skinner was a behaviorist; the neo-Freudians named are Adler, Jung, Horney and Erikson.

subject: Understanding the Self
stem: Individualist cultures tend to value:
options: Respectfulness to elders above all else

explanation.correct: The source describes individualist cultures this way.

subject: Understanding the Self
stem: According to our psychology source, Asian cultures tend to be more:

explanation.correct: The source says Asian cultures tend to be more collectivist.

wrong.2: The source places them as more collectivist.

subject: Understanding the Self
stem: A 17-year-old has not thought about careers or values and is not trying to. In Marcia's model, he is in:

explanation.correct: Low commitment and not seeking is diffusion.

subject: Understanding the Self
stem: Marcia's identity statuses are formed by combining which two dimensions?

explanation.correct: Marcia's model crosses exploration and commitment.

subject: Industrial Arts (exploratory)
stem: Ohm's law states that:

explanation.correct: Voltage equals current times resistance.

wrong.1: Voltage is current times resistance, not divided.
wrong.2: Current is V divided by R.
wrong.3: Resistance is V divided by I.

subject: Industrial Arts (exploratory)
stem: A 220 V appliance has a resistance of 44 Ω. What current does it draw?

subject: Industrial Arts (exploratory)
stem: A rice cooker draws 4 A from a 220 V outlet. What is its power?

subject: Industrial Arts (exploratory)
stem: A current of 2 A flows through a 10 Ω resistor. How much power is dissipated?

wrong.1: That uses I × R, not I² × R.

subject: Industrial Arts (exploratory)
stem: A 1,000 W electric fan heater runs for 5 hours. How much energy does it use?

explanation.correct: E = Pt = 1 kW × 5 h = 5 kWh.

wrong.2: That forgets to convert watts to kilowatts.
wrong.3: Power and time are multiplied, not added.

subject: Industrial Arts (exploratory)
stem: A household uses 200 kWh in a month and electricity costs ₱12 per kWh. What is the energy cost?

explanation.correct: Cost = kWh × price = 200 × 12 = 2,400.

wrong.1: The values are multiplied, not added.

subject: Industrial Arts (exploratory)
stem: Electric bills charge for energy measured in:

explanation.correct: Bills use kilowatt-hours.

subject: Industrial Arts (exploratory)
stem: Three resistors of 10 Ω, 20 Ω and 30 Ω are connected in series. What is the total resistance?

explanation.correct: In series, Rs = R1 + R2 + R3 = 60 Ω.

subject: Industrial Arts (exploratory)
stem: When resistors are connected in parallel, the total resistance is:
options: Less than the smallest individual resistance
Equal to the sum of the resistances
Greater than the largest individual resistance
Always exactly half of the largest resistance

explanation.correct: Parallel total resistance is less than the smallest one.

wrong.2: Series totals exceed the largest; parallel totals are smaller.
wrong.3: There is no such fixed rule.

subject: Industrial Arts (exploratory)
stem: Why are a car's headlights wired in parallel rather than in series?
options: Each gets the full voltage and works independently
Parallel wiring uses more resistance per lamp
Series wiring gives each lamp more voltage
Parallel wiring makes current flow in only one path

explanation.correct: In parallel each device is connected directly to the source.

subject: Industrial Arts (exploratory)
stem: Two 12 Ω lamps are connected in parallel to a 12 V battery. What is the total resistance of the circuit?

explanation.correct: For two equal resistors in parallel, total = 12 ÷ 2 = 6 Ω, less than either one.

wrong.2: The total must be less than the smallest resistor.

subject: Industrial Arts (exploratory)
stem: In a series circuit, the current:
options: Passes through each resistor in sequence
Is zero in the last resistor

explanation.correct: In series the same current flows through each resistor in turn.

wrong.2: The current is the same throughout.
wrong.3: Current does not increase along a series path.

subject: Industrial Arts (exploratory)
stem: In the resistor color code, which color stands for the digit 4?

explanation.correct: Yellow = 4.

subject: Industrial Arts (exploratory)
stem: A gold tolerance band on a resistor means:

explanation.correct: Gold = ±5%.

wrong.3: Not given for gold in our source.

subject: Industrial Arts (exploratory)
stem: A resistor has bands brown–black–red–gold. What is its value?

explanation.correct: Brown 1, black 0, red multiplier = 2 zeros: 1,000 Ω; gold ±5%.

wrong.1: The third band is a multiplier, not a digit.
wrong.2: Red gives two zeros, and gold is ±5%.
wrong.3: Red adds two zeros to 10, giving 1,000.

subject: Industrial Arts (exploratory)
stem: Which band colors give 47,000 Ω (47 kΩ) on a four-band resistor?

explanation.correct: Yellow 4, violet 7, orange multiplier = 3 zeros.

subject: Industrial Arts (exploratory)
stem: A resistor with no tolerance band has a tolerance of:

explanation.correct: No band = ±20%.

subject: Industrial Arts (exploratory)
stem: Which order of strokes in a four-stroke engine is correct?

explanation.correct: These are the four strokes in order.

subject: Industrial Arts (exploratory)
stem: How many crankshaft revolutions does one complete four-stroke cycle take?

explanation.correct: The four strokes take two revolutions.

wrong.1: That is a two-stroke engine's cycle.
wrong.2: Each stroke is half a revolution, not one.

subject: Industrial Arts (exploratory)
stem: In which stroke is the air-fuel mixture drawn into the cylinder?

explanation.correct: The intake stroke draws in the mixture.

wrong.2: The power stroke is driven by combustion.
wrong.3: The exhaust stroke expels spent gases.

subject: Industrial Arts (exploratory)
stem: The four-stroke cycle is also called the Otto cycle after:

explanation.correct: The cycle is named after Nicolaus Otto.

wrong.1: Diesel is linked to the diesel engine.
wrong.2: Watt is linked to the steam engine.
wrong.3: Benz built early cars, but the cycle bears Otto's name.

subject: Industrial Arts (exploratory)
stem: Which set lists the four main components of a vapor-compression refrigeration system?

explanation.correct: These are the four components.

wrong.2: These are accessories, not the four core components.

subject: Industrial Arts (exploratory)
stem: What does refrigeration do with the heat removed from an enclosed space?
options: Rejects it at a higher temperature elsewhere
Stores it in the evaporator permanently

explanation.correct: Refrigeration removes heat and rejects it at a higher temperature.

wrong.2: The evaporator absorbs heat but it is moved out.
wrong.3: That is not what refrigeration does.

subject: Industrial Arts (exploratory)
stem: Which refrigeration method is the most widely used for air conditioning?

explanation.correct: Vapor-compression is the most widely used.

wrong.1: That exists but is not the most common.
wrong.3: That is not a refrigeration cycle.

subject: Industrial Arts (exploratory)
stem: Which is the correct order of the 5S?
options: Sort, set in order, shine, standardize, sustain
Shine, sort, sustain, set in order, standardize
Set in order, sort, standardize, shine, sustain

stem: A teacher logs into her bank account using free café Wi-Fi. What does our source advise?
options: Avoid logging in on open networks
It is always safe on public Wi-Fi
Share the password with the café staff

explanation.correct: The source lists this protective strategy.

subject: Introduction to ICT
stem: Encryption is listed in our source as:

explanation.correct: Encryption is among the listed strategies.

subject: Introduction to ICT
stem: What do the source's password rules say about reuse?
options: Use one password everywhere for easy memory
Reuse is fine if the password is long

explanation.correct: The source says do not reuse.

wrong.2: The source says do not reuse.

subject: Introduction to ICT
stem: Under RA 10173, "personal information" is information from which a person's identity:
options: Is apparent or can be reasonably and directly ascertained

explanation.correct: Sec. 3(g) defines it this way.

wrong.1: That would not be personal information.

subject: Introduction to ICT
stem: A company collected a learner's data unlawfully. Which right under RA 10173 lets her have it removed or destroyed?
options: The right to have data blocked, removed or destroyed
The right to change her birthday
No right exists once data are collected

explanation.correct: Sec. 16 gives this right for unlawfully obtained data.

wrong.1: That is not a data-subject right.

subject: Introduction to ICT
stem: A learner suffered damages because a school leaked his health records. Which RA 10173 right applies?
options: The right to be indemnified for damages
No right, because schools are exempt

explanation.correct: Sec. 16 includes indemnity.

wrong.2: Disputing errors does not cover damages.

subject: Introduction to ICT
stem: Someone opens a teacher's email account without permission. Under RA 10175 this is:

explanation.correct: Accessing a system without right is illegal access.

subject: Introduction to ICT
stem: A person uses a stolen identity to open an online account in another's name. Under RA 10175 this is:

explanation.correct: Identity theft is a computer-related offense.

subject: Introduction to ICT
stem: Which RA 10175 offense covers libel committed through a computer system?

explanation.correct: Libel under the RPC done through a computer is a content offense.

wrong.2: That is about tools for crimes.

subject: Introduction to ICT
stem: Under RA 8293, computer programs are protected as:

explanation.correct: Sec. 172.1(n) lists computer programs.

wrong.2: The source treats them under copyright.

subject: Agri-Fishery Arts (exploratory)
stem: Under RA 10068, organic agriculture dramatically reduces external inputs mainly by:
options: Refraining from chemical fertilizers, pesticides and pharmaceuticals
Using only imported hybrid seeds every season
Growing only one crop on the same land each year
Doubling the amount of irrigation water

explanation.correct: Sec. 3(b) defines organic agriculture this way.

subject: Agri-Fishery Arts (exploratory)
stem: Which of the following is NOT an aim of an organic production system under RA 10068?

explanation.correct: Organic systems refrain from chemical fertilizers.

subject: Agri-Fishery Arts (exploratory)
stem: The time between the start of organic management and certification of the products as organic is the:

explanation.correct: Sec. 3(d) defines the conversion period.

wrong.1: A closed season is a fishing ban period.
wrong.2: A fallow period is resting land, not this definition.

subject: Agri-Fishery Arts (exploratory)
stem: An independent certifying body inspects a farm to check that it follows organic standards. This is:

explanation.correct: An independent body checking compliance is third-party certification.

wrong.1: First party means the producer checks itself.
wrong.2: Second party means buyers or industry set and check rules.
wrong.3: A PGS is run locally by people engaged in organic farming.

subject: Agri-Fishery Arts (exploratory)
stem: What did RA 11511 (2020) add to the organic agriculture law?
options: A ban on all fish farming

explanation.correct: RA 11511 adds the PGS as a recognized quality-assurance system.

subject: Agri-Fishery Arts (exploratory)
stem: Under the amended organic law, which products may be labelled and sold as "organic"?
options: Those certified by a third party or through a PGS
Any product the farmer believes is natural
Only imported products with foreign labels
Any product sold in a public market

explanation.correct: The amended Sec. 18 allows labeling for third-party or PGS certification.

wrong.3: Market location does not decide it.

subject: Agri-Fishery Arts (exploratory)
stem: Who chairs the National Organic Agricultural Board (NOAB)?

explanation.correct: The NOAB, attached to the DA, is chaired by the Secretary of Agriculture.

wrong.3: The President does not chair it.

subject: Agri-Fishery Arts (exploratory)
stem: Crop rotation helps farmers mainly because it:
options: Reduces pest and weed pressure and reliance on one set of nutrients
Lets the same crop be grown on the same land every season
Removes the need for any soil management
Increases the number of resistant pests

explanation.correct: The source lists these benefits.

subject: Agri-Fishery Arts (exploratory)
stem: A farmer plants mung beans after rice to improve the soil. Which rotation goal does this mainly serve?
options: Speeding up erosion of the topsoil
Making the soil more acidic on purpose

explanation.correct: Rotations may aim to increase soil nitrogen with legumes.

wrong.1: Rotation can control erosion, not speed it up.
wrong.2: That is a problem of monocropping.
wrong.3: That is not a rotation goal named.

subject: Agri-Fishery Arts (exploratory)
stem: Growing the same crop on the same land year after year tends to:
options: Deplete nutrients and build up specialized pests
Add nitrogen to the soil naturally

explanation.correct: The source says monocropping does this.

subject: Agri-Fishery Arts (exploratory)
stem: Under the Fisheries Code, aquaculture covers fish culture in which waters?

explanation.correct: Sec. 4(3) covers all three.

subject: Agri-Fishery Arts (exploratory)
stem: Which fish can be grown in fresh, brackish and salt water in the Philippines?

explanation.correct: Milkfish grows in all three.

subject: Agri-Fishery Arts (exploratory)
stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the top five Philippine aquaculture commodities named in our source?

explanation.correct: The top five are milkfish, tilapia, jumbo tiger shrimp, seaweed and mud crab.

wrong.1: Milkfish is in the top five.
wrong.2: Seaweed is in the top five.
wrong.3: Mud crab is in the top five.

subject: Agri-Fishery Arts (exploratory)
stem: How does a fish cage differ from a fish pen?
options: A cage has an artificial bottom; a pen uses the lake or sea bed
A pen floats; a cage sits on dry land
A cage is only for seaweed

explanation.correct: Pens use the bed as the floor; cages have an artificial bottom.

subject: Agri-Fishery Arts (exploratory)
stem: Compared with pens, fish cages:
options: Cost less to build but need more feeding
Cost more to build and need no feeding
Need no water quality control at all
Are banned under the Fisheries Code

explanation.correct: The source says so.

wrong.2: All aquaculture needs water quality control.

subject: Agri-Fishery Arts (exploratory)
stem: Mussels and oysters in the Philippines are commonly grown on:

explanation.correct: The source names bamboo stakes.

wrong.1: That is not the method named.
wrong.2: That is not the method named.
wrong.3: That is not the method named.

subject: Agri-Fishery Arts (exploratory)
stem: Which natural event threatens the sale of farmed mussels and oysters?
options: El Niño drought in rice fields

explanation.correct: Red tide threatens the sale of bivalves.

wrong.1: That is not the threat named.
wrong.2: That is not the threat named.
wrong.3: That is not a threat in Philippine waters.

subject: Agri-Fishery Arts (exploratory)
stem: Under the Fisheries Code, how long does a Fishpond Lease Agreement run?

explanation.correct: Sec. 45 sets this term.

subject: Agri-Fishery Arts (exploratory)
stem: In onshore aquaculture, which living condition do farmers control?
options: The weather and the tides only

explanation.correct: The source names these.

wrong.2: Price is not a living condition.

subject: Agri-Fishery Arts (exploratory)
stem: Which order of hatchery steps is correct?
options: Broodstock conditioning, spawning, fertilization, larval rearing
Spawning, broodstock conditioning, larval rearing, fertilization
Larval rearing, fertilization, spawning, broodstock conditioning
Fertilization, spawning, broodstock conditioning, larval rearing

explanation.correct: These are the production steps in order.

subject: Agri-Fishery Arts (exploratory)
stem: Which of the following is NOT a benefit of hatcheries in our source?
options: Removing the need for any water quality management

explanation.correct: Benefits are out-of-season supply, genetic improvement and less dependence on wild fry.

subject: Agri-Fishery Arts (exploratory)
stem: Which is a method of inducing spawning named in our source?
options: Starving the broodstock for a month

explanation.correct: Spawning may be induced by stripping, thermal shock or hormone injection.

wrong.1: That is not a spawning method named.

subject: Agri-Fishery Arts (exploratory)
stem: Under the Fisheries Code, municipal waters extend how far from the coastline?

explanation.correct: Sec. 4(58) sets 15 km.

wrong.3: That is the exclusive economic zone.

subject: Agri-Fishery Arts (exploratory)
stem: Municipal fishing uses vessels of how many gross tons or less?

explanation.correct: Sec. 4(57) sets 3 gross tons or less.

subject: Agri-Fishery Arts (exploratory)
stem: Fishermen use a dynamite blast to stun fish near a reef. Under the Fisheries Code this is:
options: Allowed during the closed season only

explanation.correct: Sec. 92 prohibits fishing with explosives, poison or electricity.

subject: Agri-Fishery Arts (exploratory)
stem: Muro-ami fishing is banned mainly because it:
options: Is too slow to be profitable

explanation.correct: Sec. 97 bans muro-ami and methods that pound coral.

subject: Agri-Fishery Arts (exploratory)
stem: Under the Fisheries Code, converting mangroves into fishponds is:

explanation.correct: Sec. 99 makes it unlawful.

subject: Agri-Fishery Arts (exploratory)
stem: "Sabalo" refers to:

explanation.correct: Sec. 103 protects sabalo and other breeders.

subject: Agri-Fishery Arts (exploratory)
stem: A closed season under the Fisheries Code is:
options: A period when taking specified species with specified gear is prohibited
The time when fishponds are drained for cleaning
A holiday when markets are closed

explanation.correct: Sec. 4(8) defines it this way.

subject: Agri-Fishery Arts (exploratory)
stem: According to the FAO Code of Conduct, which gear should be given priority?
options: Gear that catches every species at once

explanation.correct: Art. 6.6 gives priority to selective, environmentally safe gear.

subject: Agri-Fishery Arts (exploratory)
stem: IPM, as defined by FAO, integrates which kinds of pest-control measures?
options: Chemical only, at the highest doses

explanation.correct: IPM integrates all these to minimize pesticide use.

subject: Agri-Fishery Arts (exploratory)
stem: In IPM, what is the first line of defense?
options: Cultural practices such as resistant varieties and rotation
Spraying pesticides on a fixed calendar

explanation.correct: Cultural practices come first.

wrong.1: Calendar spraying is not IPM's first step.

subject: Agri-Fishery Arts (exploratory)
stem: A farmer counts pests in traps each week and sprays only when the count reaches a level where losses would cost more than treatment. This level is the:

explanation.correct: Controls are used only when pests exceed the action threshold.

subject: Agri-Fishery Arts (exploratory)
stem: Which order follows the six IPM steps?
options: Monitor, identify, learn biology, set threshold, choose tactics, evaluate
Choose tactics, monitor, evaluate, identify, set threshold, learn biology
Identify, evaluate, monitor, choose tactics, learn biology, set threshold
Set threshold, choose tactics, monitor, identify, evaluate, learn biology

explanation.correct: These are the repeating steps.

wrong.3: The threshold is set after learning biology.

subject: Agri-Fishery Arts (exploratory)
stem: In Southeast Asian rice, early pesticide spraying made brown planthopper outbreaks worse because it:

wrong.1: That is not the reason given.
wrong.2: That is not the reason given.
wrong.3: That is not the reason given.

subject: Agri-Fishery Arts (exploratory)
stem: Under IPM, biopesticides such as Bt are counted as:

wrong.1: Cultural controls are practices like rotation.

subject: Agri-Fishery Arts (exploratory)
stem: The Philippine carabao is a:
options: Swamp-type water buffalo used as a draft animal in rice farming
River-type buffalo used mainly for racing
Breed of cattle imported from Europe
Wild animal never used on farms

explanation.correct: The source describes it this way.

wrong.2: The carabao is a water buffalo.

subject: Agri-Fishery Arts (exploratory)

wrong.2: Bantams are a small breed type.
wrong.3: Capons are a specific kind of male chicken.

subject: Agri-Fishery Arts (exploratory)
stem: Which is NOT a housing system for laying hens named in our source?

explanation.correct: The source names free-range, barns and battery cages.

subject: Agri-Fishery Arts (exploratory)
stem: A farmer composts animal manure and crop residues to return nutrients to the soil. Which aim of organic production does this serve?
options: Recycling plant and animal wastes to return nutrients to the land
Using more synthetic fertilizer each season
Spraying pesticides on a fixed schedule

wrong.1: Organic systems refrain from chemical fertilizers.
wrong.2: That is not an organic aim.
wrong.3: Organic systems refrain from chemical pesticides.

subject: Agri-Fishery Arts (exploratory)
stem: A buyers' cooperative writes its own organic rules and checks its suppliers against them. This is:

wrong.1: First party is the producer checking itself.
wrong.2: Third party is an independent body.

subject: Agri-Fishery Arts (exploratory)
stem: A farmer writes her own organic standards and declares her own farm compliant. This is:

explanation.correct: The producer sets and checks its own rules.

wrong.3: A PGS involves a local network of people.

subject: Agri-Fishery Arts (exploratory)
stem: A Participatory Guarantee System (PGS) is built mainly on:

explanation.correct: RA 11511 defines PGS this way.

subject: Agri-Fishery Arts (exploratory)
stem: Besides nitrogen, crop rotations may aim at which other goals?
options: Weed control, erosion control or soil structure

explanation.correct: The source lists these.

subject: Agri-Fishery Arts (exploratory)
stem: Which aquaculture species in the Philippines are usually raised in brackish water?

explanation.correct: The source lists shrimp and crab as brackish.

subject: Agri-Fishery Arts (exploratory)
stem: Which is described as the traditional aquaculture method in the Philippines, often multi-pond for milkfish?

explanation.correct: The source names brackish fishponds as traditional.

wrong.1: These are not described as traditional.
wrong.3: These are not described as traditional.

subject: Agri-Fishery Arts (exploratory)
stem: About how long after planting is the first seaweed harvest, per our source?

explanation.correct: The source gives about 105–135 days.

subject: Agri-Fishery Arts (exploratory)
stem: Which seaweeds are named as farmed in the Philippines?
options: Kelp and giant sea oak only

explanation.correct: The source names these.

subject: Agri-Fishery Arts (exploratory)
stem: Under the Fisheries Code, public lands such as mangroves and tidal swamps suitable for fishery:
options: May be sold to any private buyer
Are free for anyone to claim

explanation.correct: Sec. 45 says they may not be disposed of.

wrong.1: They may not be disposed of.

subject: Agri-Fishery Arts (exploratory)
stem: Fishpond Lease Agreements under the Fisheries Code are granted primarily to:

explanation.correct: Sec. 45 gives priority to qualified fisherfolk cooperatives.

wrong.3: Priority is given to fisherfolk cooperatives.

subject: Agri-Fishery Arts (exploratory)
