explanation.correct: Conditioning sets optimal conditions for breeders.

wrong.3: That is at the grow-out farm.

subject: Agri-Fishery Arts (exploratory)
stem: After hatching and early rearing in a hatchery, juveniles are usually moved to:

explanation.correct: Juveniles go to on-growing farms.

subject: Agri-Fishery Arts (exploratory)
stem: A fisherman uses a net with mesh smaller than the size set by the DA for that fishery. Under the Fisheries Code this is:
options: Unlawful, except in allowed cases such as gathering fry
Allowed, if he fishes at night

explanation.correct: Sec. 93 prohibits undersized mesh.

wrong.1: Time does not change the rule.

subject: Agri-Fishery Arts (exploratory)
stem: Fishermen use a cyanide solution to stun reef fish for the aquarium trade. This is:
options: Unlawful fishing with noxious or poisonous substances
Legal if the fish are sold alive

explanation.correct: Sec. 92 prohibits this.

wrong.2: IPM is pest management in crops.

subject: Agri-Fishery Arts (exploratory)
stem: Under the amended Fisheries Code, owners and operators using muro-ami face a fine of:
options: Five times the catch value or ₱2 million, whichever is higher

explanation.correct: Sec. 97 sets this fine.

subject: Agri-Fishery Arts (exploratory)
stem: Catching or possessing sabalo (mature milkfish) is allowed only for:
options: Local breeding or research, as permitted

explanation.correct: Sec. 103 allows these exceptions.

subject: Agri-Fishery Arts (exploratory)
stem: Which is a MECHANICAL pest control in IPM?

explanation.correct: Mechanical controls include hand-picking, barriers and traps.

subject: Agri-Fishery Arts (exploratory)
stem: A farmer releases more of a pest's natural predators into her vegetable garden to boost their numbers. This is:

explanation.correct: Increasing natural enemies is augmentative biocontrol.

subject: Agri-Fishery Arts (exploratory)
stem: IRRI encourages farmers to plant flowers and vegetables on rice paddy banks. Why?
options: To attract natural enemies of pests
To shade the rice from the sun
To sell flowers for extra income only

explanation.correct: The source says this attracts natural enemies.

wrong.1: That is not the reason given.
wrong.3: The reason given is pest control.

subject: Agri-Fishery Arts (exploratory)
stem: Besides draft work, the Philippine carabao is used for:

explanation.correct: The source lists these uses.

subject: Common Competencies
stem: A new worker in a food plant is put on the line without any safety orientation. Which employer duty under RA 11058 is being ignored?
options: Giving complete job safety instructions or orientation
Paying wages on a fixed day of the week
Giving every worker a written job promotion plan
Providing free meals to workers during breaks

explanation.correct: Sec. 4(a) requires complete safety instructions, especially for new workers.

wrong.1: Pay day rules are not the OSH duty described here.
wrong.2: Promotion plans are not part of the OSH duty described.
wrong.3: Meals are not the OSH duty described here.

subject: Common Competencies
stem: Under RA 11058, a worker may refuse unsafe work without reprisal when:
options: DOLE determines an imminent danger exists and the employer has not corrected it
The worker simply dislikes the assigned task for that day
A coworker says the job is boring and tiring
The shift falls on a holiday and pay is regular

explanation.correct: Sec. 6 sets this condition.

wrong.1: Dislike is not the legal ground.
wrong.2: That is not the legal ground.
wrong.3: That is not the legal ground.

subject: Common Competencies
stem: Under RA 11058, who pays for workers' personal protective equipment?
options: The employer, free of charge to workers
The workers, through salary deductions each month
DOLE, through a yearly voucher sent to each worker
The local barangay, from its development fund

explanation.correct: Sec. 8 requires PPE free of charge.

wrong.1: The law says free of charge.

subject: Common Competencies
stem: The "right to know" under RA 11058 means workers must be:
options: Informed of all workplace hazards and trained on safety
Told the company's profits and shareholder names
Shown the personal records of all other workers
Given the employer's home address and phone number

explanation.correct: Sec. 5 gives this right.

wrong.1: That is not the right to know under OSH.
wrong.3: That is not the right to know.

subject: Common Competencies
stem: Under RA 11058, safety signage must be:
options: Posted prominently in a language understandable to all
Written only in English, in small print, near the exit
Kept in the manager's office for reference only
Posted only during DOLE inspections, then removed

explanation.correct: Sec. 9 requires this.

wrong.1: It must be understandable to all and prominent.
wrong.3: It must be posted at all times.

subject: Common Competencies
stem: Under RA 11058, the cost of an approved safety and health program is treated as:
options: A fine to be paid by the workers each quarter
A donation that the employer may skip if busy
A tax credit claimed only by government offices

explanation.correct: Sec. 20 treats it as part of operating cost.

wrong.1: The cost is not charged to workers.
wrong.3: That is not what the law says.

subject: Common Competencies
stem: Under RA 11058, to whom may workers report accidents and hazards?
options: The employer, DOLE and other concerned authorities
Only to coworkers, never to outside offices
Only to the media, after the accident is over
No one; reporting hazards is not allowed

explanation.correct: Sec. 7 gives the right to report to these.

wrong.1: Workers may report to DOLE and others.
wrong.2: The law names employer and authorities.

subject: Common Competencies
stem: Which order follows the elements of the TESDA unit "Practice occupational health and safety procedures"?
options: Identify, evaluate, control hazards; maintain awareness; perform first aid
Control hazards, identify hazards, perform first aid, evaluate hazards
Perform first aid, evaluate, identify, control hazards and risks
Evaluate hazards, perform first aid, control hazards, identify hazards

explanation.correct: These are the five elements in order.

wrong.2: First aid is the last element.

subject: Common Competencies
stem: Loud noise from a grinder in a workshop is which type of hazard?
options: Biological, like bacteria, molds and parasites
Chemical, like fumes, gases and vapors
Ergonomic, like awkward or static postures

explanation.correct: Noise is a physical hazard.

subject: Common Competencies
stem: Mold growing on stored flour in a bakery is which type of hazard?
options: Physical, like heat, noise and vibration
Chemical, like dusts and smoke from burning

explanation.correct: Molds and fungi are biological hazards.

subject: Common Competencies
stem: A cook lifts heavy pots repeatedly with a bent back. This exposes the cook to which hazard type?
options: Chemical, from fumes of cooking oil
Biological, from bacteria on the pots
Physical radiation from the stove light

explanation.correct: Over-exertion and awkward postures are ergonomic hazards.

wrong.1: The issue here is body strain.
wrong.2: The issue here is body strain.
wrong.3: The issue here is body strain.

subject: Common Competencies
stem: Fumes from cleaning products in a closed salon are which type of hazard?

explanation.correct: Fumes, gases and vapors are chemical hazards.

subject: Common Competencies
stem: In evaluating hazards, the OHS unit uses maximum tolerable limits based on:
options: The worker's own comfort level that day
The cost of the materials being used
The number of years the shop has operated

explanation.correct: Element 2.1 uses TLVs.

wrong.2: Cost does not set exposure limits.
wrong.3: Age of the shop does not set limits.

subject: Common Competencies
stem: Which of the following is NOT listed as a contingency measure in the OHS unit?
options: Hiding the incident from the supervisor

explanation.correct: Contingency measures are evacuation, isolation, decontamination and calling emergency personnel.

subject: Common Competencies
stem: Which of the following is NOT an example of PPE in the OHS unit?

explanation.correct: The PPE listed includes masks, gloves, goggles, hairnets, face shields, ear muffs, aprons and coveralls.

subject: Common Competencies
stem: In selecting measuring instruments, the mensuration unit says alternative tools may be used:
options: Only if they are cheaper, whatever the quality
Only when the supervisor is absent

explanation.correct: Element 1 allows alternatives without sacrificing cost and quality.

subject: Common Competencies
stem: According to the mensuration unit, after computing, the worker should:
options: Round every answer to the nearest hundred
Ask the client to do the arithmetic

explanation.correct: Element 2 requires self-checking.

subject: Common Competencies
stem: A rectangular kitchen counter top is 2.4 m long and 0.6 m wide. What is its area?

explanation.correct: Area = length × width = 2.4 × 0.6 = 1.44 m².

subject: Common Competencies
stem: A recipe for 4 servings uses 300 g of flour. How much flour is needed for 10 servings?

explanation.correct: Ratio and proportion: 300 × 10/4 = 750 g.

subject: Common Competencies
stem: How many centimeters are in 1.75 meters?

wrong.1: The decimal is off by one place.

subject: Common Competencies
stem: During tool checking, a worker finds a drill with a frayed cord. What does the TESDA unit require?
options: Segregate and label it as non-functional
Put it back on the rack for the next user
Wrap it with tape and keep using it
Throw it in the general waste bin at once

explanation.correct: Element 1 requires segregating and labeling non-functional tools.

wrong.2: That is unsafe and not the rule.
wrong.3: The rule is to segregate and label.

subject: Common Competencies
stem: Underpinning knowledge for maintaining tools includes the types and uses of:

explanation.correct: The unit lists these.

wrong.2: These are not in the unit.
wrong.3: These are not in the unit.

subject: Common Competencies
stem: When interpreting a technical drawing, the worker should:

Guess the dimensions by looking at the picture
Ignore symbols and abbreviations in the plan
Redraw the plan freehand before reading it

explanation.correct: Element 2 lists these.

subject: Common Competencies
stem: Which type of drawing shows an object in separate views, such as front, top and side?
options: A pie chart of materials used in the project
A freehand mood board of colors and textures
A family tree of the project team

explanation.correct: Orthographic drawing is in the unit's underpinning knowledge.

wrong.1: That is a chart, not a technical view.
wrong.2: That is not a technical drawing type.
wrong.3: That is not a technical drawing.

subject: Common Competencies
stem: Which is NOT one of the plan types named under blueprint reading in the technical-drawing unit?

explanation.correct: The unit names architectural, electrical, electronic and mechanical plans.

subject: Common Competencies
stem: Under RA 11058, which of these is a type of PPE the employer must provide where needed?

wrong.2: Style items are not the listed PPE.

subject: Common Competencies
stem: Under RA 11058's right to know, workers must be trained on which kinds of safety?

Only traffic safety on the way to work

explanation.correct: Sec. 5 lists these.

wrong.1: The list is broader and ongoing.

subject: Common Competencies
stem: Under RA 11058, employers must use only devices and equipment that are:

Imported from a single foreign country
Older than ten years, to save money

subject: Common Competencies
stem: A worker in a bakery is exposed to fine flour dust all day. Which hazard type is this?

Physical, like noise from the mixers

subject: Common Competencies
stem: Which is the last element of the TESDA OHS procedures unit?

Control hazards and risks with measures

subject: Common Competencies
stem: Required trade mathematics in the mensuration unit includes:

explanation.correct: The unit lists these.

subject: Common Competencies
stem: A sewing project needs 3/4 meter of fabric for each of 6 aprons. How much fabric is needed?
options: 6 3/4 meters, adding the fraction to six
3 meters, using only half a meter each
8 meters, rounding each apron up to a whole meter

wrong.1: Fractions must be multiplied, not added.

subject: Common Competencies
stem: When checking tools, the TESDA unit requires observing:
options: The opinions of passing customers about the tools
The color of the tool handles only
No instructions, since workers know best

explanation.correct: Element 1 requires this.

subject: Common Competencies
stem: The first element of "Prepare and interpret technical drawing" is to:
options: Identify the right technical drawing for the job
Build the structure before reading the plan
Change all dimensions to suit the worker
Throw away drawings after one use

explanation.correct: Element 1 is identifying and sorting drawings.

subject: Entrepreneurship
stem: According to our entrepreneurship source, an idea becomes an entrepreneurial opportunity when:
options: Identifiable consumer demand meets the feasibility of satisfying it
The owner likes the idea and has some savings to spend
A relative agrees to buy the first batch of products
The product is new and has never been sold anywhere

explanation.correct: The source defines opportunity this way.

wrong.1: Liking an idea does not make it an opportunity.
wrong.2: One buyer does not show demand and feasibility.
wrong.3: Novelty alone is not the test.

subject: Entrepreneurship
stem: Corporate social responsibility (CSR) means a business:
options: Sees itself as a member of society with social and environmental obligations
Only obeys the law and does nothing beyond it
Gives all its profits away to charity every year
Avoids paying taxes to help the community directly

explanation.correct: The source defines CSR this way.

subject: Entrepreneurship
stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the three primary financial statements?

explanation.correct: The three statements are the balance sheet, income statement and statement of cash flows.

wrong.1: This is one of the three.
wrong.2: This is one of the three.
wrong.3: This is one of the three.

subject: Entrepreneurship
stem: Which financial statement bridges the income statement and the balance sheet?
options: Executive summary of the business plan

explanation.correct: The source says the statement of cash flows bridges the other two.

wrong.1: That is part of the plan, not a statement.
wrong.2: That is not a financial statement.
wrong.3: That is not a financial statement.

subject: Entrepreneurship
stem: A turon stall sells each piece for ₱15; the variable cost per piece is ₱5; monthly stall rent is ₱3,000. How many pieces must it sell monthly to break even?

explanation.correct: Contribution margin = 15 − 5 = 10; break-even = 3,000 ÷ 10 = 300.

wrong.1: That divides by the price (15) instead of the margin.
wrong.2: That divides by the variable cost (5).
wrong.3: That divides by 20, adding price and cost.

subject: Entrepreneurship
stem: A cupcake sells for ₱40 and its variable cost is ₱25. What is the contribution margin per cupcake?

explanation.correct: Contribution margin = price − variable cost = 40 − 25.

wrong.1: Price and cost are subtracted, not added.

subject: Entrepreneurship
stem: Under RA 9178, a Barangay Micro Business Enterprise (BMBE) has total assets, excluding land, of not more than:

explanation.correct: Sec. 3(a) sets the BMBE ceiling at ₱3 million.

wrong.2: That is the upper limit for small enterprises under RA 9501.

subject: Entrepreneurship
stem: Under RA 9501, a small enterprise has assets of:

explanation.correct: Small enterprises fall in this range.

subject: Entrepreneurship
stem: Under the Revised Corporation Code, how many incorporators may organize a corporation?

explanation.correct: Sec. 10 allows not more than 15; a One Person Corporation is also allowed.

wrong.1: The Code sets a maximum of 15.
wrong.2: The Code no longer requires exactly 5.
wrong.3: The Code sets not more than 15.

subject: Entrepreneurship
stem: Under the Revised Corporation Code, a corporation's term of existence is:
options: Perpetual, unless the articles provide otherwise
Only as long as the founder lives

explanation.correct: Sec. 11 grants perpetual existence by default.

wrong.1: The term is now perpetual by default.
wrong.3: A corporation is separate from its founder.

subject: Entrepreneurship
stem: In a primary cooperative, voting follows which rule?
options: One vote per peso of capital

explanation.correct: Democratic member control means one member, one vote.

wrong.1: Capital does not decide votes in primary cooperatives.

subject: Entrepreneurship
stem: A home-baker decides to sell her ensaymada at a coffee shop and through an online delivery app. Which P of the marketing mix is she deciding?

explanation.correct: Place is where the product is purchased.

wrong.1: Price is what the buyer pays.

subject: Entrepreneurship
stem: A tailoring shop posts photos of its work on social media with a weekend discount offer. Which P is this?

explanation.correct: Advertising and sales offers are promotion.

wrong.1: Place is where the customer buys.
wrong.3: Price is what is paid, though a discount touches price, the posting is communication.

subject: Entrepreneurship
stem: Why is the executive summary of a business plan usually written last?
options: It summarizes the whole plan, so the other parts must be done first
It is the least important part and may be skipped
Investors never read it, so it can wait
It contains only the owner's biography

explanation.correct: The source says write it last though it comes first.

wrong.1: It is placed first and read first.

subject: Entrepreneurship
stem: According to our source, legal compliance and ethical responsibility differ because:
options: The law does not settle every ethical dilemma
Laws always demand more than ethics
Ethics only matter for large corporations
Legal compliance is optional for small businesses

explanation.correct: The source makes this point about CSR.

subject: Entrepreneurship
stem: Under RA 9501, MSMEs may take which forms?
options: Single proprietorships, cooperatives, partnerships or corporations

explanation.correct: Sec. 3 lists these.

subject: Technology for Teaching and Learning
stem: TPACK describes the intersection of which three kinds of knowledge?

explanation.correct: TPACK stands for these three.

wrong.1: These are not the three domains.
wrong.2: These are not the three domains.
wrong.3: These are not the three domains.

subject: Technology for Teaching and Learning
stem: TPACK builds on which earlier idea?

explanation.correct: TPACK extends Shulman's PCK.

subject: Technology for Teaching and Learning
stem: Who developed the TPACK framework?

explanation.correct: The source credits Mishra and Koehler.

wrong.1: Dale proposed the Cone of Experience.
wrong.3: They are linked to source evaluation.

subject: Technology for Teaching and Learning
stem: A teacher knows how a spreadsheet works and knows nutrition well, but cannot plan a lesson where students use the spreadsheet to analyze their diets. Which TPACK area is weakest?
options: Context (XK) only, which is not a knowledge domain

explanation.correct: She has TK and CK but lacks integration of all three.

subject: Technology for Teaching and Learning
stem: According to Seifert and Sutton, more classroom technology makes it easier to move from:
options: Small groups to whole-class lecture only

explanation.correct: The source describes this shift.

wrong.3: That is not the shift described.

subject: Technology for Teaching and Learning
stem: What does CRAAP stand for?

explanation.correct: These are the five CRAAP criteria.

subject: Technology for Teaching and Learning
stem: Who created the CRAAP test, and when?

explanation.correct: The source credits librarian Sarah Blakeslee (2004).

wrong.2: Dale proposed the Cone of Experience.

subject: Technology for Teaching and Learning
stem: What are the four moves of Mike Caulfield's SIFT?
options: Stop; Investigate the source; Find better coverage; Trace claims to the original
Search; Index; File; Type the summary
Scan; Ignore ads; Follow links; Trust logos
Save; Insert; Format; Tag the article

explanation.correct: These are the SIFT moves.

wrong.2: Trusting logos is what fools readers.

subject: Technology for Teaching and Learning
stem: According to studies cited in our source, what often fools students and even historians online?

explanation.correct: The source reports this finding.

wrong.1: That is not the finding reported.
wrong.2: That is not the finding reported.
wrong.3: That is not the finding reported.

subject: Technology for Teaching and Learning
stem: How does gamification differ from game-based learning?
options: Gamification adds game elements to learning; game-based learning has students play or make games
They are two names for exactly the same practice
Gamification uses only board games, never digital tools
Game-based learning uses only points and badges

explanation.correct: The source draws this distinction.

wrong.3: Points and badges are gamification elements.

subject: Technology for Teaching and Learning
stem: What do the letters in "PBLs" stand for in gamification?

explanation.correct: PBLs are points, badges and leaderboards.

subject: Technology for Teaching and Learning
stem: A teacher adds badges to a weekly quiz. Participation rises but scores do not improve. What does our source suggest?
options: Surface rewards must be tied meaningfully to learning goals
Badges always raise achievement, so wait longer
Remove all feedback to make the game harder
Replace the quiz with a lecture only

explanation.correct: The source warns surface rewards may raise participation without improving achievement.

wrong.1: The source says they may not.

subject: Technology for Teaching and Learning
stem: Adaptive learning platforms work by:
options: Using algorithms and AI to deliver resources customized to each learner
Giving every learner the same worksheet at the same time
Removing all teachers from the classroom
Showing only videos with no practice

explanation.correct: The source defines adaptive learning this way.

subject: Technology for Teaching and Learning
stem: Adaptive learning grew out of which research in the 1970s?

explanation.correct: The source traces it to intelligent tutoring research.

subject: Technology for Teaching and Learning
stem: What does our source say about the "we remember 10% of what we read" percentages often attached to Dale's Cone?
options: They are not Dale's; he included no numbers
Dale measured them in a 1946 experiment
They come from the Philippine K to 12 curriculum
They were added by Dale in his 1969 revision

explanation.correct: The source says the percentages are not Dale's.

subject: Technology for Teaching and Learning
stem: Under RA 8293, which of the following uses can count as fair use?
options: Teaching, including multiple copies for classroom use
Uploading a whole film to sell online
Claiming another's program as one's own

explanation.correct: Sec. 185 includes teaching and classroom copies.

wrong.1: Commercial copying weighs against fair use.

subject: Technology for Teaching and Learning
stem: In TPACK, the overlap of technology and content knowledge alone is called:

explanation.correct: Technology + content = TCK.

subject: Technology for Teaching and Learning
stem: What surrounds the TPACK domains in the framework's diagram?

explanation.correct: Context surrounds the domains.

wrong.1: That is not part of the model.
wrong.2: That is not part of the model.

subject: Technology for Teaching and Learning
stem: Before trusting a viral post about a "miracle" diet, a learner first pauses, then checks who runs the website. Which SIFT moves is she using?
options: Find better coverage and Trace claims only
Trusting the logo because it looks official

explanation.correct: These are the first two SIFT moves.

wrong.1: She has not yet done these.

subject: Technology for Teaching and Learning
stem: Games built with learning goals inside the gameplay are called:

explanation.correct: The source defines serious games this way.

subject: Technology for Teaching and Learning
stem: Under RA 8293, one factor in judging fair use is:
options: The purpose and character of the use, such as non-profit educational use
The color of the copied pages
Whether the copier owns a printer

explanation.correct: Sec. 185 lists this factor.

subject: Home Management
stem: Which law is the Consumer Act of the Philippines?

explanation.correct: RA 7394 is the Consumer Act.

wrong.1: RA 11967 is the Internet Transactions Act.
wrong.3: RA 10611 is the Food Safety Act.

subject: Home Management
stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the objectives of the Consumer Act (Art. 2)?
options: Guaranteeing the lowest possible price for every product
Protection against hazards to health and safety
Protection against deceptive and unfair sales acts
Adequate rights and means of redress

explanation.correct: The objectives are health and safety, protection from deceptive and unfair sales, information and education, redress, and consumer representation.

subject: Home Management
stem: Under the Consumer Act, which agency sets product standards for food, drugs and cosmetics?

explanation.correct: Art. 6 assigns food, drugs, cosmetics and devices to DOH.

wrong.3: DepEd runs consumer education, not product standards.

subject: Home Management
stem: A consumer complains about a defective electric fan. Under Art. 6, which agency handles standards for this product?

explanation.correct: DTI covers consumer products other than food, drugs, cosmetics and agricultural goods.

wrong.1: DOH covers food, drugs, cosmetics and devices.
wrong.3: DOLE is not an implementing agency here.

subject: Home Management
stem: Which body does the Consumer Act create to improve coordination of consumer programs?
options: Consumer Price Board of the Senate

explanation.correct: Art. 148 creates the Council.

wrong.2: The Act does not create a special court.

subject: Home Management
stem: Under the Consumer Act, consumer education must be integrated into the curricula of:
options: All public and private schools from primary to secondary level

explanation.correct: Art. 154 requires this.

wrong.1: The requirement covers basic education schools.
wrong.3: The requirement covers primary and secondary schools.

subject: Home Management
stem: A shopper reads the label, compares prices and asks about the quality of a rice cooker before buying. Which consumer responsibility is shown?

explanation.correct: Being alert and questioning about use, price and quality is critical awareness.

wrong.1: Assertiveness is acting to get a fair deal.
wrong.2: Social concern is about the effect of consumption on others.

subject: Home Management
stem: A buyer returns a spoiled can of sardines to the store and insists on a replacement. Which responsibility is this?

explanation.correct: Acting to get a fair deal is assertiveness.

wrong.1: Critical awareness is questioning before buying.

subject: Home Management
stem: A family chooses products in refillable containers to cut plastic waste. Which responsibility is this?

explanation.correct: Understanding the environmental effects of consumption is environmental awareness.

wrong.1: Assertiveness is getting a fair deal.
wrong.2: Critical awareness is questioning price and quality.
wrong.3: Social concern is about effects on other people, especially the disadvantaged.

subject: Home Management
stem: According to the Consumer Act's education program, what happens to a passive consumer?
options: They save more money than an active one
They are protected automatically by DTI

explanation.correct: The program explains assertiveness by noting that a passive consumer continues to be exploited.

wrong.1: The law does not say this.
wrong.3: Passivity is the opposite of assertiveness.

subject: Home Management
stem: Under Art. 159, how may a consumer start a complaint with the concerned department?
options: By filing a petition or letter-complaint
Only by hiring a lawyer to file a case in court
Only by posting on social media

explanation.correct: Art. 159 allows a petition or letter-complaint.

wrong.2: The Act provides a formal complaint route.
wrong.3: The complaint is filed with the concerned department.

subject: Home Management
stem: A seller falsely says a used phone is brand-new to get a customer to buy it. Under the Consumer Act this is:

explanation.correct: Inducing a transaction through false representation is deceptive (Art. 50).

wrong.1: Unconscionable acts exploit infirmity or ignorance to get a one-sided deal.
wrong.3: A warranty is a promise about the product.

subject: Home Management
stem: A vendor sees that an elderly buyer cannot read and charges her five times the usual price for a loan of goods. Under the Consumer Act this is:
options: An unfair or unconscionable sales act
A deceptive act only, because a lie was told
A legal transaction because she agreed

explanation.correct: Taking advantage of illiteracy to get a grossly one-sided deal is unconscionable (Art. 52).

wrong.1: No false statement is described; the exploitation is the key.
wrong.3: That is a pyramid selling scheme.

subject: Home Management
stem: What does the Consumer Act say about pyramid sales schemes for consumer products?
options: They are allowed if registered with DTI
They are encouraged for small businesses

explanation.correct: Art. 53 prohibits chain distribution plans and pyramid sales schemes.

subject: Home Management
stem: Under the Consumer Act, false or misleading advertising to induce purchases is unlawful:
options: Only if the product is imported

explanation.correct: Art. 110 makes it unlawful in any medium.

wrong.3: The rule applies to all products.

subject: Home Management
stem: What is the official system of weights and measures for products under the Consumer Act?

explanation.correct: Art. 63 adopts the metric system.

wrong.1: The Act adopts the metric system.
wrong.2: The Act adopts the metric system.
wrong.3: The Act sets one official system.

subject: Home Management
stem: Which of the following is NOT among the minimum label contents required by Art. 77?
options: The retail price in five different stores
Philippine address of the manufacturer, importer or repacker

explanation.correct: The label lists brand name, trademark, business name, Philippine address, ingredients, net quantity and country of manufacture.

subject: Home Management
stem: A sari-sari store sells shampoo above the price printed on its tag. Under Art. 81 this is:
options: Not allowed; products may not be sold above the tagged price
Allowed if the buyer agrees to pay

explanation.correct: Art. 81 forbids selling above the price tag.

wrong.2: The rule applies to all retailers.

subject: Home Management
stem: Under Art. 81, a retailer's price for a product must be:
options: Set by bargaining with each buyer

explanation.correct: The same price applies to all buyers.

wrong.1: The same price applies to everyone.
wrong.2: The same price applies to everyone.

subject: Home Management
stem: When does a written warranty become operative under the Consumer Act?
options: Only after the product breaks for the first time
Only after the warranty card is mailed

explanation.correct: Art. 68(b) makes written warranties operative from the moment of sale.

wrong.1: It is operative from the sale.
wrong.2: It is operative from the sale.
wrong.3: The Act says from the moment of sale.

subject: Home Management
stem: Which of the following must an express warranty state, according to Art. 68(a)?
options: Who the warrantor is and what it will do, at whose expense
The names of other buyers of the same product
The product's price in other countries

explanation.correct: The warranty must state the warrantor, coverage, what will be done and at whose expense, and the period.

subject: Home Management
stem: Under Art. 97, manufacturers and importers are liable for damage from defective products:
options: Only if the consumer proves negligence
Only if the product is imported
Only during the first week after sale

explanation.correct: Liability is independent of fault.

subject: Home Management
stem: Under the Consumer Act, a product is "defective" when it:
options: Does not offer the safety rightfully expected of it
Costs more than a similar product
Is not the newest model available

explanation.correct: Art. 97 defines defectiveness this way.

wrong.3: Packaging style is not the test.

subject: Home Management
stem: A blender explodes because its manual gave no warning about overheating. Can the manufacturer be liable?
options: Yes; inadequate information on use and hazards is a ground of liability
No, because the blender itself was well built
No, because the buyer read the manual
Only if the store also agrees to pay

explanation.correct: Art. 97 covers defects including inadequate information.

wrong.3: Manufacturer liability stands on its own.

subject: Home Management
stem: Which transaction is NOT covered by the Internet Transactions Act (RA 11967)?
options: A consumer-to-consumer (C2C) sale between two private persons
A foreign platform targeting Philippine buyers

explanation.correct: C2C transactions and online media content are excluded.

wrong.3: Platforms targeting the Philippine market are covered.

subject: Home Management
stem: Which agency administers the Internet Transactions Act?
options: Department of Information and Communications Technology

explanation.correct: The Act covers B2B and B2C internet transactions under DTI.

wrong.1: That is not the agency named.

subject: Home Management
stem: Under RA 11765, a "financial consumer" is a person who:
options: Buys, leases or receives, or may do so, financial products from a provider
Owns a bank or lending company
Works as a teller in a bank

explanation.correct: Sec. 3 defines financial consumers this way, including prospective ones.

wrong.1: That is a provider, not a consumer.
wrong.2: An employee is not the definition.
wrong.3: The definition covers financial service providers.

subject: Home Management
stem: A family's income is ₱30,000 a month. Under the 50-30-20 guide, how much goes to savings and debt payments?

wrong.1: That is 30%, the share for wants.
wrong.2: That is 50%, the share for needs.

subject: Home Management
stem: Which of the following is a FIXED expense?
options: Electricity used for an air conditioner in summer

explanation.correct: Fixed expenses such as rent do not change over time.

subject: Home Management
stem: A family pays ₱6,000 for insurance once a year. How should it appear in the monthly budget?
options: ₱6,000 in one month and nothing after
It should be left out of the budget

explanation.correct: Divide the bill by the number of months it covers: 6,000 ÷ 12 = 500.

wrong.1: The source says spread it monthly.

subject: Home Management
stem: In budgeting, what should a family do if total monthly expenses are higher than income?
options: Adjust the budget after comparing income and expenses
Ignore it until the end of the year
Borrow every month to cover the gap

explanation.correct: The budget steps say total, compare, and adjust if expenses are higher.

wrong.3: The source says to adjust the budget.

subject: Home Management
stem: Simple interest is computed on the:
options: Principal, using the annual rate and the term in years
Interest already earned in earlier years
Price of the item bought with the loan only

explanation.correct: Simple interest uses the principal, rate and time.

wrong.2: Income is not part of the formula.
wrong.3: The principal is the amount borrowed or deposited.

subject: Home Management
stem: ₱10,000 is deposited at 5% simple interest per year for 3 years. How much interest is earned?

wrong.1: That is one year's interest only.
wrong.3: That is roughly compound interest, not simple.

subject: Home Management
stem: Which of the following is a unit of competency in TESDA Housekeeping NC II?
options: Clean and prepare rooms for incoming guests
Prepare hot and cold sauces for the menu
Draft and cut patterns for casual apparel
Install electrical wiring in a residential building

explanation.correct: This is one of the listed core units.

subject: Home Management
stem: Under the Consumer Act, which agency sets standards for agricultural products?

explanation.correct: Art. 6 assigns agricultural products to DA.

wrong.1: DOH covers food, drugs, cosmetics and devices.

subject: Home Management
stem: The Consumer Act's state policy aims to protect consumers' interests and:
options: Set standards of conduct for business and industry
Fix the price of every product

explanation.correct: Art. 2 includes this.

subject: Home Management
stem: A buyer chooses fair-trade products to support poor farmers. Which consumer responsibility is this?
options: Assertiveness in getting a fair deal
Critical awareness of price and quality

explanation.correct: Awareness of the effect of consumption on others, especially the disadvantaged, is social concern.

subject: Home Management
stem: The Consumer Act also requires a consumer education program for:

explanation.correct: Art. 154 includes them.

subject: Home Management
stem: Under Art. 159, departments must set up complaint procedures that are:

explanation.correct: The law requires simple, accessible procedures.

subject: Home Management
stem: A store displays canned goods with no price tag, label or marking. Under Art. 81 this is:
options: Not allowed; products for retail need a displayed price
Allowed if the cashier knows the price

explanation.correct: Art. 81 requires a price tag, label or marking.

subject: Home Management
stem: An imported jar of jam has no country of manufacture on its label. Which rule is broken?

explanation.correct: Country of manufacture is required for imports.

wrong.3: The missing item is the country.

subject: Home Management
stem: A rice cooker's warranty card does not say who the warrantor is or how long the coverage lasts. Which rule does this break?
options: Art. 68(a), requiring clear terms of express warranties

explanation.correct: The warranty must state the warrantor and period.

subject: Home Management
stem: A person in Cebu buys shoes from an online shop that targets Philippine buyers. Is the transaction covered by RA 11967?
options: Yes; it is a B2C internet transaction targeting the Philippine market
No; only government purchases are covered
No; only purchases above ₱1 million are covered
No; online shoes are online media content

explanation.correct: Such transactions are covered.

subject: Home Management
stem: A family earns ₱25,000 a month. Under the 50-30-20 guide, how much is for needs?

wrong.2: That is 20%, for savings and debt.

subject: Home Management
stem: Which of the following is a VARIABLE expense?

explanation.correct: Groceries change month to month.

wrong.3: The source lists internet as fixed.

subject: Home Management
stem: A quarterly water bill is ₱900. How much should be set aside each month?

explanation.correct: Divide the bill by the months it covers: 900 ÷ 3.

subject: Home Management
stem: Which of the following is a common competency in Housekeeping NC II?

explanation.correct: This is among the listed units.

subject: Food Science and Nutrition
stem: How many classes of nutrients are there?

explanation.correct: Carbohydrates, lipids, proteins, water, vitamins and minerals.

wrong.1: Four leaves out two classes, such as water and minerals.
wrong.2: Five leaves out one class; water is often forgotten.
wrong.3: Fiber is not counted as a separate class in our source.

subject: Food Science and Nutrition
stem: Which of the following is NOT a macronutrient?

explanation.correct: Vitamins are micronutrients, needed in small amounts.

subject: Food Science and Nutrition
stem: How many essential minerals and vitamins does our source list as micronutrients?

explanation.correct: Micronutrients are the 16 essential minerals and 13 vitamins.

subject: Food Science and Nutrition
stem: A snack has 10 g carbohydrate, 5 g protein and 4 g fat. About how many kilocalories does it provide?

wrong.1: This counts fat at 4 kcal/g instead of 9.
wrong.2: This counts every gram at 9 kcal.

subject: Food Science and Nutrition
stem: According to our nutrition source, what is protein's MOST important job?
options: Building body structures and running chemical reactions
Supplying most of the body's daily energy needs for work and exercise

explanation.correct: Proteins build bones, muscles and skin and run most chemical reactions; energy is not their main job.

wrong.1: The source says energy is not protein's most important job.
wrong.2: Insulation is a role of lipids.
wrong.3: Iron, a mineral, helps red blood cells carry oxygen.

subject: Food Science and Nutrition
stem: Which nutrient class forms cell membranes, protects organs and helps regulate body temperature?

explanation.correct: Lipids form membranes, protect organs and insulate the body.

wrong.2: Minerals are micronutrients with other roles.

subject: Food Science and Nutrition
stem: Why is a daily source of vitamin C needed?
options: It is not stored in significant amounts; excess is excreted
It is stored in body fat for years, so a large dose lasts a long time
It is made in the skin from sunlight
It is a mineral used up in sweat

explanation.correct: The source says vitamin C is not stored much and higher intake means more is excreted.

wrong.1: That describes fat-soluble vitamins more closely.
wrong.3: Vitamin C is a vitamin, not a mineral.

subject: Food Science and Nutrition
stem: Which of the following is NOT a B vitamin?

explanation.correct: Vitamin K is fat-soluble, not a B vitamin.

subject: Food Science and Nutrition
stem: A sailor on a long voyage without fresh fruit develops bleeding gums and slow-healing wounds. Which nutrient is lacking?

explanation.correct: Bleeding gums and poor healing are signs of scurvy, from lack of vitamin C, which is needed for collagen.

wrong.3: Vitamin A deficiency causes night blindness.

subject: Food Science and Nutrition
stem: Vitamin C is essential for making which structural protein?

explanation.correct: The source links vitamin C to collagen synthesis, which is why scurvy affects gums and skin.

wrong.1: Keratin is the protein in hair and wool, not linked here.
wrong.3: Albumin is linked to edema in kwashiorkor.

subject: Food Science and Nutrition
stem: In adults, vitamin D deficiency causes which condition?

explanation.correct: Vitamin D deficiency gives rickets in children and osteomalacia in adults.

subject: Food Science and Nutrition
stem: In a community whose staple is polished white rice, a nurse sees leg pain, swelling and signs of heart failure. Which deficiency fits?

explanation.correct: Beriberi is common where the staple is milled white rice, because milling removes the bran.

subject: Food Science and Nutrition
stem: Why is beriberi common where milled white rice is the main food?
options: White rice contains a vitamin C blocker
Rice is too high in iodine

explanation.correct: The source says milling removes the bran.

wrong.1: The source gives no such cause.

subject: Food Science and Nutrition
stem: Which set lists the "four D's" of pellagra given in our source?
options: Diarrhea, dermatitis, dementia and sometimes death
Diarrhea, diabetes, dehydration, dementia and depression

explanation.correct: Niacin deficiency leads to diarrhea, dermatitis, dementia and sometimes death.

wrong.1: These are not the four D's.
wrong.2: Diabetes and dehydration are not part of the list.
wrong.3: These are not the four D's.

subject: Food Science and Nutrition
stem: Dry eyes with Bitot's spots that can progress to corneal ulcers and blindness describe:
options: Xerophthalmia from severe vitamin A deficiency
Scurvy from a long-term lack of vitamin C in the diet

explanation.correct: Severe vitamin A deficiency causes xerophthalmia.

wrong.1: Scurvy affects gums, skin and joints.

subject: Food Science and Nutrition
stem: Low iron intake causes anemia mainly because it:
options: Reduces the oxygen-carrying capacity of red blood cells
Causes edema because the blood cannot hold enough water and albumin

explanation.correct: The source explains anemia this way.

wrong.1: That is goiter, from iodine deficiency.

subject: Food Science and Nutrition
stem: Iodine is essential for making which hormone?

explanation.correct: Iodine is needed to make thyroid hormone, which regulates basal metabolism, growth and development.

wrong.1: Insulin is not made from iodine.
wrong.2: Adrenaline is not made from iodine.
wrong.3: Thyroid hormone affects growth, but iodine is used for thyroid hormone.

subject: Food Science and Nutrition
stem: Why does a child with kwashiorkor show swelling (edema)?
options: Too little protein means too little albumin to hold water in the blood vessels
Too much salt in the diet makes the body hold water in every tissue
Lack of vitamin C weakens vessels

explanation.correct: The source explains edema through low albumin.

wrong.1: The source does not give salt as the cause.

subject: Food Science and Nutrition
stem: A recently weaned toddler fed mostly thin rice porridge has a pot belly, swollen feet and thinning, light-colored hair. The most likely condition is:

explanation.correct: Recently weaned children on low-protein porridge with edema and light, thin hair fit kwashiorkor.

wrong.1: Marasmus shows extreme thinness without edema.

subject: Food Science and Nutrition
stem: The word "marasmus" comes from Greek and means:

explanation.correct: The source says marasmus is Greek for starvation.

wrong.1: "Rejected one" is the meaning of kwashiorkor (from Ghana).

subject: Food Science and Nutrition
stem: The name "kwashiorkor" comes from a language of which country?

explanation.correct: The source says the name comes from a language in Ghana, meaning "rejected one".

wrong.2: Not the source of the name.
wrong.3: Not the source of the name.

subject: Food Science and Nutrition
stem: Which list gives the four steps of safe food handling?

explanation.correct: These are the four steps in the source.

wrong.1: These are not the four named steps.
wrong.2: These are not the four named steps.

subject: Food Science and Nutrition
stem: Within how many hours should leftovers be refrigerated?
options: Only after they cool completely overnight

explanation.correct: The Chill step says refrigerate leftovers within two hours.

wrong.2: Twelve hours is far too long.
wrong.3: Waiting overnight leaves food in unsafe temperatures.

subject: Food Science and Nutrition
stem: At what temperature or colder should a refrigerator be kept?

explanation.correct: The source says 40 °F (4 °C) or colder.

subject: Food Science and Nutrition
stem: Where in the refrigerator should raw meat be stored?

explanation.correct: Storing raw meat at the bottom keeps its juices from dripping onto other foods.

wrong.1: Juices could drip onto foods below.
wrong.2: The door is the warmest part.

subject: Food Science and Nutrition
stem: Why should eggs be kept on a shelf rather than in the refrigerator door?
options: The door is the warmest part of the refrigerator
Light from the door bulb damages the shells

explanation.correct: The source says the door is warmest.

wrong.2: Cleanliness is not the reason given.
wrong.3: That is not the reason given.

subject: Food Science and Nutrition
stem: Hot food that is being held for serving should be kept above about:

explanation.correct: Hot food should be kept above 140 °F.

wrong.1: That is in the danger range.
wrong.3: Food need not be kept boiling.

subject: Food Science and Nutrition
stem: A foodborne illness caused by toxins (for example, produced by molds) rather than by live microbes is called:

explanation.correct: Foodborne illnesses are infections (microbes) or intoxications (toxins).

wrong.1: Infections are caused by the microbes themselves.
wrong.2: Allergies are immune reactions, not this category.

subject: Food Science and Nutrition
stem: Salmonellosis symptoms usually appear within:

explanation.correct: The source gives fever, diarrhea and cramps within 12–72 hours.

subject: Food Science and Nutrition
stem: Salmonella is found mainly in the intestines of:
options: Molds, yeasts and other fungi on bread

explanation.correct: The source says Salmonella lives in these animals' intestines.

wrong.1: Salmonella is linked to animal sources.
wrong.2: It is not limited to fish.
wrong.3: Those are fungi, not hosts of Salmonella.

subject: Food Science and Nutrition
stem: Molds grow best on food kept in which conditions?

explanation.correct: Molds are fungi that grow in warm, humid or damp conditions.

wrong.1: Cold, dry conditions slow mold growth.

subject: Food Science and Nutrition
stem: When an egg white turns from clear to white while cooking, what is happening to its proteins?

explanation.correct: Cooking denatures proteins and changes their functional qualities.

subject: Food Science and Nutrition
stem: Which of the following is a MODERN rather than traditional preservation method in our source?

explanation.correct: Modern methods include drying, vacuum packing, pasteurization, freezing and refrigeration.

subject: Food Science and Nutrition
stem: Besides preventing foodborne illness, food preservation also protects:
options: Flavor, color, moisture and nutritive value
Only the calorie count and the weight of the food

explanation.correct: The source lists these benefits.

wrong.1: Price is not the listed benefit.
wrong.2: Weight is not the listed benefit.

subject: Food Science and Nutrition
stem: Under the Food Fortification Act, "fortification" means adding nutrients to processed foods at levels:

explanation.correct: RA 8976 Sec. 3 defines fortification this way.

wrong.3: The law defines the term; the choice is not free.

subject: Food Science and Nutrition
stem: A carinderia owner asks what salt the ASIN law lets her offer customers. What is the answer?

explanation.correct: RA 8172 requires food outlets and restaurants to make only iodized salt available.

wrong.2: The law does not require rock salt.
wrong.3: The law regulates salt; it does not ban it.

subject: Food Science and Nutrition
stem: The Food Safety Act of 2013 (RA 10611) aims to protect the public from:
options: Food-borne and water-borne illness and unsafe or misbranded food
Imported foods of all kinds, which the Act bans from local markets

explanation.correct: Sec. 3(a) states these aims.

wrong.1: Price control is not its aim.
wrong.3: Its aim is food safety broadly.

subject: Food Science and Nutrition
stem: Poaching differs from boiling and simmering mainly because it uses:
options: Dry oven air at a high, steady temperature

explanation.correct: Poaching uses a gentler, lower temperature than simmering or boiling.

subject: Food Science and Nutrition
stem: In blanching, plunging vegetables into iced water right after boiling is called:

explanation.correct: The cold plunge that stops cooking is known as shocking or refreshing.

wrong.1: Searing is browning at high heat.
wrong.2: Basting is spooning liquid over food.

subject: Food Science and Nutrition
stem: The word "sauté" comes from French and refers to:
options: Jumping or tossing the food in the pan
Marinating the food overnight before cooking it

explanation.correct: Sauté means "jumped", from tossing while cooking.

subject: Food Science and Nutrition
stem: A cook browns beef chunks in a hot pan, then adds a little broth, covers the pot and cooks it slowly. Which method is this, and why is it NOT poaching?
options: Braising, because it starts with dry-heat browning before covered simmering
Sautéing, because the beef was browned
Steaming, because the pot is covered and the liquid makes steam around the beef

explanation.correct: Braising combines dry and wet heat; poaching only uses gentle liquid heat.

wrong.1: Poaching does not begin with browning.
wrong.2: Sautéing is quick cooking in fat only.
wrong.3: Steaming cooks with steam, not in liquid after browning.

subject: Food Science and Nutrition
stem: Pan-frying differs from deep-frying because in pan-frying the food is:

explanation.correct: Deep-frying submerges food in hot fat; shallow (pan) frying does not.

subject: Food Science and Nutrition
stem: A cook soaks pork in vinegar, soy sauce and garlic for an hour before grilling. This step is called:

explanation.correct: Soaking food in a seasoned, often acidic liquid before cooking is marinating.

wrong.1: Blanching is brief boiling then shocking.
wrong.2: Braising is a cooking method, not a soak.
wrong.3: Creaming is beating fat with sugar.

subject: Food Science and Nutrition
stem: Why are vegetables often diced into uniform cubes?
options: To make them float in oil

explanation.correct: Uniform dice ensure even cooking.

wrong.1: Dicing is not for removing vitamins.

subject: Food Service Management
stem: Under PD 856, utensils are washed in warm water at what temperature?

explanation.correct: Sec. 24 sets 49 °C for washing.

wrong.2: 77 °C is for hot-water sanitizing, not washing.
wrong.3: Boiling is not the washing temperature.

subject: Food Service Management
stem: For hot-water sanitizing under PD 856, utensils are immersed for at least 30 seconds in water at:
options: 82 °C in a hot-air cabinet for only 20 seconds

explanation.correct: Sec. 25 sets at least 30 seconds at 77 °C.

wrong.2: That is below the required temperature.
wrong.3: That is the hot-air cabinet option.

subject: Food Service Management
stem: If chlorine is used to sanitize utensils, PD 856 calls for immersion for at least:
options: 1 minute in a lukewarm 50 ppm chlorine solution
30 minutes in a 500 ppm chlorine solution at boiling point

explanation.correct: Sec. 25 gives this option.

wrong.3: Water alone is not a chlorine treatment.

subject: Food Service Management
stem: Which order of steps follows PD 856 for washing utensils?
options: Scrape and pre-rinse, wash in warm detergent water, sanitize, drain-dry
Sanitize, scrape and pre-rinse, wash in cold water, towel-dry

explanation.correct: These follow Secs. 24–26.

wrong.1: Scraping and washing come before sanitizing; drying cloths are not used.

subject: Food Service Management
stem: After sanitizing, a canteen worker wipes each plate dry with a cloth. What does PD 856 say?
options: Utensils should drain-dry on racks without drying cloths
Cloth drying is required so that no chlorine taste remains on plates
Any cloth is fine if it is new
Plates must be dried with paper only

explanation.correct: Sec. 26(a) requires drain-drying without cloths.

wrong.1: The law says no drying cloths.
wrong.2: The law says no drying cloths.
wrong.3: The law says drain-dry or air-dry.

subject: Food Service Management
stem: Under PD 856, which materials must NOT be used in food equipment?
options: Food-grade plastic containers with tight-fitting lids

explanation.correct: Sec. 23 bans these.

wrong.2: This is not banned in the law's text.

subject: Food Service Management
stem: Under PD 856, perishable foods are kept at or below what temperature, except during preparation or serving?

explanation.correct: Sec. 29(a) sets 7 °C.

wrong.3: The rule is at or below 7 °C.

subject: Food Service Management
stem: PD 856 recommends storing meat and fish at:

explanation.correct: Sec. 29(c) gives 0–3 °C for meat and fish.

wrong.1: That is for milk and milk products.
wrong.2: That is for fruits and vegetables.

subject: Food Service Management
stem: Under PD 856, fruits and vegetables are best stored at:

explanation.correct: Sec. 29(d) gives 7–10 °C.

wrong.1: That is for meat and fish.

subject: Food Service Management
stem: What does PD 856 recommend for storing dry, non-perishable foods?
options: Metal containers with tight covers, at about 10–15 °C
The same shelf as cleaning chemicals
Any container at room temperature, as long as it is labeled

explanation.correct: Sec. 28 gives these rules.

wrong.1: Designated shelves and covered containers are required.
wrong.2: That is unsafe and not the rule.

subject: Food Service Management
stem: Under PD 856, refrigerators used for food must have:
options: Thermometers and enough shelving for ventilation
A lock on every shelf and a glass door for display

explanation.correct: Sec. 29(e) requires these.

subject: Food Service Management
stem: How should cups and glasses be stored under PD 856?
options: Inverted, in a clean, dry place protected from vermin
Upright on the bottom shelf of the open cabinet below the work top

explanation.correct: Sec. 27 says cups, bowls and glasses are inverted.

wrong.1: Bottom shelves below the work top are not allowed.
wrong.3: They are stored in a clean, dry place.

subject: Food Service Management
stem: A server picks up ice for a drink with bare fingers. Under PD 856 this is:
options: Not allowed; hand contact with food must be avoided
Allowed if the server's hands look clean and dry

explanation.correct: Sec. 30(a) says fingers are not used for butter, ice and similar items.

wrong.3: Consent does not change the rule.

subject: Food Service Management
stem: Under PD 856, how should sugar be served in a food establishment?
options: In covered dispensers or single-service packets
In open bowls shared by all tables, refilled from a sack
Only on request, from the kitchen floor

explanation.correct: Sec. 30(a) requires this.

wrong.1: Open bowls are not the rule.

subject: Food Service Management
stem: Where do soiled linens go under PD 856?
options: On the dining chairs until closing

explanation.correct: Sec. 30(d) requires a closed, marked bin.

wrong.2: Clean and soiled linens are separated.

subject: Food Service Management
stem: Under PD 856, between uses, ice cream dippers and scoops are kept:
options: In running water or water at 77 °C, or washed and dried after each use
In a dry cup on the counter
In a drawer with the cleaning cloths, dried by hand each morning

explanation.correct: Sec. 30(e) gives these options.

wrong.1: That is not an option given.
wrong.2: That is not an option given.
wrong.3: That is not an option given.

subject: Food Service Management
stem: In which service style is food plated in the kitchen and brought to each guest?

explanation.correct: American service is plate service.

wrong.2: Guests serve themselves at a buffet.
wrong.3: That is not one of the three styles listed.

subject: Food Service Management
stem: Which order follows the F&B Services NC II sequence of service?
options: Greet, seat, take beverage orders, present menu, take food orders
Present the bill, greet, seat, take orders
Take food orders, greet, seat, present menu, take beverage orders
Serve food, present menu, greet, seat

explanation.correct: This is the start of the listed sequence.

wrong.3: The menu is presented before food is served.

subject: Food Service Management
stem: What is the purpose of the "3-minute check"?
options: To confirm guest satisfaction soon after serving
To time how fast the kitchen cooks each order for the manager
To count the cutlery before service

explanation.correct: The check confirms satisfaction and replenishes items.

subject: Food Service Management
stem: In the sequence of service, crumbing the table comes:
options: After serving food, before coffee or tea
After presenting the bill and collecting payment

explanation.correct: The sequence is serve food, crumb, then coffee/tea, then the bill.

subject: Food Service Management
stem: Which of the following is NOT part of closing down the dining area in the TR?
options: Handling food scraps according to hygiene rules

explanation.correct: The TR says turn off electrical equipment.

subject: Food Service Management
stem: When preparing the dining area, what does the TR say about condiment bottles?
options: Fill them only after guests arrive

explanation.correct: The TR lists wiping necks and tops of condiment bottles.

wrong.2: That is not in the TR.
wrong.3: That is not in the TR.

subject: Food Service Management
stem: A bakery learns that a batch of bread may be contaminated and some loaves were already sold. Under RA 10611, what must it do?
options: Withdraw the bread, inform authorities and consumers, and recall it
Keep selling and hope no one gets sick
Lower the price to sell it faster
Wait for a customer complaint before removing any bread from the shelves

explanation.correct: Sec. 14 requires withdrawal, notice and recall.

wrong.3: The duty to act is immediate.

subject: Food Service Management
stem: Under the Food Safety Act, who is responsible for food safety in school canteens?

explanation.correct: Sec. 15 assigns food businesses such as school canteens to LGUs.

wrong.2: DOH covers processed and prepackaged foods.

subject: Food Service Management
stem: Under RA 10611, which agency covers food safety in primary production (farms)?

explanation.correct: Sec. 15 assigns primary production to the DA.

wrong.1: LGUs cover food businesses like markets and canteens.

subject: Food Service Management
stem: Under RA 11037, which agency runs the school-based feeding program for undernourished public school children?
options: Department of Health (DOH) through rural health units

explanation.correct: DepEd runs the program from kindergarten to Grade 6.

wrong.1: DSWD runs supplemental feeding in day care centers.
wrong.2: DOH is not named as the operator here.

subject: Food Service Management
stem: RA 11037 feeding programs give at least one fortified meal for not less than how many days a year?

explanation.correct: Sec. 4 sets at least 120 days.

wrong.1: The law says not less than 120.

subject: Food Service Management
stem: Under RA 11037, a fortified meal supplies at least what share of the daily requirement?

explanation.correct: Sec. 3(a) says at least one-third, based on the PDRI.

subject: Food Service Management
stem: The DSWD supplemental feeding under RA 11037 covers children aged:

explanation.correct: Sec. 4(b) covers ages 3 to 5.

wrong.2: The law does not cover this group here.
wrong.3: The law names ages 3 to 5 in day care.

subject: Food Service Management
stem: Which is NOT a component of the feeding program under RA 11037?

explanation.correct: The components include milk feeding, supplements, deworming, Gulayan sa Paaralan, WASH and nutrition education.

subject: Food Service Management
stem: HACCP addresses which kinds of food hazards?
options: Only those found after the food is served

explanation.correct: HACCP covers all three.

wrong.1: Chemical and physical hazards are included.

subject: Food Service Management
stem: By 1997, how many HACCP principles had become the standard?

explanation.correct: Seven principles became the standard.

subject: Food Service Management
stem: A canteen stores milk at 12 °C. Under PD 856's recommended range, what is wrong?
options: It is too warm; milk should be kept at 5–7 °C
It is too cold; milk should be kept at 20 °C
Nothing; 12 °C is the milk range in PD 856
Milk must always be frozen solid

explanation.correct: Sec. 29 recommends 5–7 °C for milk products.

subject: Food Service Management
stem: Under PD 856, food-contact surfaces of equipment must be:
options: Impervious, corrosion-resistant, non-toxic, easy to clean and durable
Porous so that they absorb cleaning water

explanation.correct: Sec. 23 lists these.

subject: Food Service Management
stem: Single-service items such as paper cups should be:
options: Stored in sanitary cartons and handled without touching food-contact surfaces
Reused after rinsing with cold water
Stored loose on the floor near the sink
Handled by the rim to show cleanliness

explanation.correct: Sec. 30 requires this.

subject: Food Service Management
stem: In Russian service, food is served from:

explanation.correct: Russian service is platter service.

wrong.3: That is not a listed style.

subject: Food Service Management
stem: Under RA 11037, the cycle menus are standardized by:
options: The National Nutrition Council and FNRI

explanation.correct: Sec. 3 names them.

subject: Food Service Management
stem: Under RA 11037, the school gardens program is called:

explanation.correct: The law names Gulayan sa Paaralan.

subject: Family Life and Child Development
stem: Under the Family Code, what is the minimum age at which a person may contract marriage?

explanation.correct: Art. 5 sets the minimum marrying age at 18.

wrong.1: Below 18 the marriage is void even with parental consent (Art. 35).
wrong.2: 21 matters only for the parental-consent rule; it is not the minimum age.
wrong.3: 25 is not the Family Code's minimum age.

subject: Family Life and Child Development
stem: Which of the following is an ESSENTIAL (not formal) requisite of marriage under the Family Code?
options: Consent freely given before the solemnizing officer
A ceremony with two adult witnesses

explanation.correct: Art. 2 lists legal capacity and freely given consent as the essential requisites.

wrong.1: The license is a formal requisite (Art. 3).
wrong.2: Officer's authority is a formal requisite (Art. 3).
wrong.3: The ceremony is a formal requisite (Art. 3).

subject: Family Life and Child Development
stem: Which of the following is a FORMAL requisite of marriage under the Family Code?
options: A valid marriage license, unless exempt
Approval of both sets of parents

explanation.correct: Art. 3 lists the officer's authority, a valid license and the ceremony as formal requisites.

wrong.1: Legal capacity is an essential requisite (Art. 2).
wrong.3: Parental approval is not a general requisite.

subject: Family Life and Child Development
stem: How many witnesses of legal age must be present at the marriage ceremony under the Family Code?
options: None, if a license was issued

explanation.correct: Art. 3 requires the declaration before at least two witnesses of legal age.

wrong.1: One witness is not enough under Art. 3.
wrong.2: The Code says at least two, not three.
wrong.3: The license does not remove the witness requirement.

subject: Family Life and Child Development
stem: The Family Code defines marriage as which of the following?
options: A special contract of permanent union between a man and a woman
A civil partnership that may be ended by mutual agreement
A religious sacrament recognized only by the Church
A temporary contract renewed every ten years

explanation.correct: Art. 1 uses these words and calls marriage the foundation of the family.

wrong.1: The Code calls it a permanent union, not a dissolvable partnership.
wrong.2: The Code treats it as a special contract under law.

subject: Family Life and Child Development
stem: Ana, 17, marries with her parents' written consent. What is the status of the marriage?
options: Void, because a party is below 18

explanation.correct: Art. 35 makes marriages of persons below 18 void even with parental consent.

wrong.1: Parental consent cannot cure being below 18.
wrong.2: The voidable rule covers ages 18 to below 21 without consent.
wrong.3: A void marriage is not cured by reaching 18.

subject: Family Life and Child Development
stem: Ben, 19, marries without his parents' consent and leaves his wife before turning 21. What is the status of the marriage?
options: Valid only if a church wedding was held

explanation.correct: Art. 45 makes a marriage of a party aged 18 to below 21 without parental consent voidable.

wrong.1: Lack of parental consent at 18–20 gives a voidable, not void, marriage.
wrong.2: Art. 45 allows annulment in this case.
wrong.3: The type of ceremony does not decide this.

subject: Family Life and Child Development
stem: A party aged 20 married without parental consent, then freely lived with the spouse as husband and wife after turning 21. What follows?
options: The ground for annulment is lost by the free cohabitation
The parents may still annul it at any time

explanation.correct: Art. 45 excepts cases where the party freely cohabited after reaching 21.

wrong.1: Free cohabitation after 21 cures the defect; it does not make it void.
wrong.2: The Code does not require a new ceremony.
wrong.3: Free cohabitation after 21 removes this ground.

subject: Family Life and Child Development
stem: Under the Family Code, a marriage in which one party was psychologically incapacitated to comply with essential marital obligations is:
options: Valid if the couple has children

explanation.correct: Art. 36 makes such a marriage void, even if the incapacity shows only after the wedding.

wrong.1: Psychological incapacity falls under Art. 36 (void), not Art. 45.
wrong.2: Civil status is governed by the Family Code.
wrong.3: Having children does not change Art. 36.

subject: Family Life and Child Development
stem: Which of the following marriages is NOT void under Art. 35 of the Family Code?
options: One where a 19-year-old married without parental consent
One solemnized without a license, not exempt

explanation.correct: That case is voidable under Art. 45, not void.

wrong.1: Below 18 is void even with consent.
wrong.2: Bigamous and polygamous marriages are void.
wrong.3: Lack of a license (unless exempt) makes it void.

subject: Family Life and Child Development
stem: What is the effect of the absence of any essential or formal requisite of marriage, as a general rule?
options: The marriage is void from the beginning
The marriage is voidable for five years
The marriage is valid but the officer is fined
The marriage becomes a legal separation

explanation.correct: Art. 4 says absence of any requisite makes it void ab initio (subject to Art. 35(2)).

wrong.1: Absence of a requisite gives a void marriage.
wrong.2: The Code treats absence as voiding the marriage.
wrong.3: Legal separation is a different remedy.

subject: Family Life and Child Development
stem: Under the Family Code, who exercises parental authority over the common children of a married couple?
options: The father and the mother jointly

explanation.correct: Art. 211 gives parental authority to both parents jointly.

wrong.1: Authority is joint; the father's view prevails only when they disagree.
wrong.3: Grandparents exercise substitute authority only in specific cases.

subject: Family Life and Child Development
stem: A couple disagrees about which school their son should attend, and no court order exists. Under Art. 211, whose decision prevails?
options: The father's, unless a court orders otherwise
The child's, if aged 12 or above

explanation.correct: Art. 211 says the father's decision prevails in case of disagreement, unless a court orders otherwise.

wrong.1: The Code gives the father's decision priority here.
wrong.2: Art. 211 does not give the child the deciding vote.
wrong.3: The school has no authority to decide.

subject: Family Life and Child Development
stem: A 12-year-old living with his parents breaks a neighbor's window. Who is civilly liable for the damage?
options: His parents, subject to the defenses allowed by law
Only the child, from his future earnings
No one, because he is a minor

explanation.correct: Art. 221 makes parents civilly liable for damage by unemancipated children living with them.

wrong.1: Art. 221 places liability on the parents.
wrong.2: The barangay is not liable under Art. 221.
wrong.3: Minority shifts civil liability to the parents.

subject: Family Life and Child Development
stem: Under RA 7610, a "child" generally refers to a person:

explanation.correct: RA 7610 Sec. 3(a) defines children as persons below 18, or older but unable to protect themselves.

subject: Family Life and Child Development
stem: The Responsible Parenthood and Reproductive Health Act (RA 10354) defines adolescents as young people aged:

explanation.correct: RA 10354 Sec. 4(b) defines adolescents as ages 10 to 19.

wrong.1: The RH Law's range is 10 to 19.
wrong.2: The RH Law's range is 10 to 19.
wrong.3: The RH Law's range is 10 to 19.

subject: Family Life and Child Development
stem: Under RA 9262, which of the following is a form of violence against women and their children?
options: Economic abuse by a former husband
A stranger's theft of a woman's phone
A teacher's low grade given fairly

explanation.correct: RA 9262 covers physical, sexual, psychological harm and economic abuse by a husband, former husband or partner.

wrong.1: RA 9262 concerns persons in an intimate or family relationship.
wrong.2: That is a civil matter, not VAWC.
wrong.3: A fair grade is not abuse.

subject: Family Life and Child Development
stem: The Early Years Act treats which age range as the first crucial stage of educational development?

explanation.correct: The Early Years Act covers ages 0 to 8.

subject: Family Life and Child Development
stem: The family a person is born into is called the family of:

explanation.correct: The family of orientation is the one you are born into.

wrong.1: The family of procreation is formed through marriage.
wrong.2: Affinity refers to relatives by marriage, not this definition.
wrong.3: Adoption is a way of forming a family, not this term.

subject: Family Life and Child Development
stem: A married couple and the children they raise together form, for the parents, their family of:

explanation.correct: The family of procreation is the family formed through marriage.

wrong.1: The family of orientation is the one a person is born into.
wrong.2: That is not a sociological term for this.
wrong.3: "Family of origin" is the family one was born into.

subject: Family Life and Child Development
stem: Lola Nena, her daughter, her son-in-law and their two children all live in one house. This household is best described as:

explanation.correct: A household with parent and child plus other relatives such as grandparents is an extended family.

wrong.1: A nuclear family has only parents and children.
wrong.2: A blended family joins parts of earlier families through remarriage.
wrong.3: That term names the family one is born into, not the household type.

subject: Family Life and Child Development
stem: Being married to only one person at a time is called:

explanation.correct: Monogamy is marriage to one person at a time.

wrong.1: Polygamy is marriage to more than one person at a time.
wrong.2: Endogamy is marrying within one's group, not this definition.
wrong.3: Cohabitation is living together without marriage.

subject: Family Life and Child Development
stem: From the functionalist view, which statement best describes the family?
options: It performs vital roles for its members and for society, such as socializing children
It mainly reproduces social inequality between classes
It is only a unit of meaning built through daily interaction
It has no role once children reach school age

explanation.correct: The functionalist view says families provide for members' well-being and socialize children.

wrong.3: Functionalists stress lifelong roles, including caring for elderly parents.

subject: Family Life and Child Development
stem: Who first introduced the idea of the family life cycle, in 1955?

explanation.correct: Glick (1955) described growing up, forming families, rearing and launching children, and the empty nest.

wrong.1: Duvall later described classic stages; the idea began with Glick.

subject: Family Life and Child Development
stem: In Evelyn Duvall's stages, the "preschooler family" has its oldest child aged about:

explanation.correct: Duvall's preschooler family covers children about 2.5 to 6.

subject: Family Life and Child Development
stem: The Reyes couple's eldest child has just left home to work in Manila, while the younger ones are still in school. Which Duvall stage fits best?

explanation.correct: The launching family stage begins as children start to leave home.

wrong.1: The empty nest comes after all children have left.
wrong.2: That stage is about children aged 13–20 still at home.
wrong.3: That is the childless first stage.

wrong.1: The meter stick is a measuring tool.
wrong.2: The tape measure is a measuring tool.
wrong.3: The L-square is listed among measuring tools.

subject: Clothing Construction
stem: A dressmaker takes a client's measurements in a random order and writes nothing down. Which TR requirement is being broken?
options: Measurements must be taken in sequence and recorded
Measurements may only be taken by two persons together
Measurements must be taken only after cutting the fabric
Measurements must be taken in inches, never centimeters

explanation.correct: The TR says measurements are taken in sequence, following standard measurement, and recorded.

wrong.2: Measuring comes before drafting and cutting.
wrong.3: The TR does not fix the unit this way.

subject: Clothing Construction
stem: In the Dressmaking NC II TR, when are the client's special needs (pocket, collar, sleeve, cut) incorporated?
options: When the garment design is planned with the client
Only after the garment is finished and pressed
When the final pattern is filed away
Never; casual apparel uses one standard design only

explanation.correct: Element 1 discusses design and fabric with the client and incorporates special needs.

wrong.1: Special needs are planned at the start.
wrong.2: Filing is the end of the pattern unit.

subject: Clothing Construction
stem: A custom-fitted basic pattern from which many styles can be developed is called a:
options: Graded pattern made in several sizes for the market
Draped muslin mock-up pinned on a dress form
Final cut pattern with seam allowances added

explanation.correct: A sloper or block is the custom-fitted basic pattern.

wrong.1: Grading changes the size of a finished pattern.
wrong.2: Draping is a different method of making patterns.
wrong.3: The final pattern is developed from the block.

subject: Clothing Construction
stem: Changing the size of a finished pattern up or down is called:

explanation.correct: Changing a finished pattern's size is grading.

wrong.1: Draping makes a pattern by pinning fabric on a form.
wrong.2: Drafting creates the pattern from measurements.

subject: Clothing Construction
stem: On a commercial pattern, what do circular holes usually mark?
options: Dart apex, pocket and buttonhole placement
Where to lengthen or shorten the pattern piece
The direction of the straight grain on the fabric
Where the seam allowance ends at the cut edge

explanation.correct: Circular holes mark these points.

wrong.2: The long arrow is the grainline.
wrong.3: Notches mark seam allowances and matching points.

subject: Clothing Construction
stem: On a pattern piece, what do double parallel lines indicate?
options: Where to lengthen or shorten the piece
The center front fold of the garment

explanation.correct: Double lines show where to lengthen or shorten.

subject: Clothing Construction
stem: What is the difference between the flat-pattern method and draping?
options: Flat-pattern drafts on a flat surface from measurements; draping pins fabric on a form
Flat-pattern uses a dress form; draping uses rulers and curves on paper
Flat-pattern is only for knits; draping is only for woven fabric
They are two names for exactly the same method

explanation.correct: The source describes them this way.

wrong.2: The source does not divide them by fabric.

subject: Clothing Construction
stem: According to the TR, how is the final pattern handled after cutting?
options: It is labeled, filed and secured
It is thrown away once the garment is cut
It is given to the fabric supplier
It is sewn into the garment lining

explanation.correct: The final pattern is labeled, filed and secured.
