wrong.1: The TR says it is filed and secured.
wrong.2: That is not in the TR.
wrong.3: That is not in the TR.

subject: Clothing Construction
stem: The straight grain of a woven fabric runs:
options: Parallel to the warp threads and the selvedge
Perpendicular to the selvedge along the weft
At 45 degrees to the selvedge in every case
In any direction the cutter prefers

explanation.correct: Straight grain runs along the warp and selvedge.

subject: Clothing Construction
stem: Which direction of woven fabric has the LEAST stretch?

explanation.correct: Straight grain has the least stretch.

wrong.3: Diagonals are bias, with more stretch.

subject: Clothing Construction
stem: A designer wants a dress that drapes and clings to the body's curves. How should the fabric be cut?
options: On the straight grain from top to bottom
With the selvedge running across the hips

explanation.correct: Woven fabric is most elastic and fluid on the bias, so bias-cut garments drape and cling.

wrong.1: Straight grain gives the least stretch.
wrong.2: Cross grain stretches more than straight grain but less than bias.

subject: Clothing Construction
stem: "True bias" is at what angle to the grain?

explanation.correct: True bias is 45°.

wrong.1: 90° is the cross grain relative to the straight grain.

subject: Clothing Construction
stem: What seam allowance is common on home-sewing patterns?

explanation.correct: Home-sewing patterns use 1/4 to 5/8 inch; 5/8 in is common.

wrong.1: That is much wider than usual.
wrong.3: That is much wider than usual.

subject: Clothing Construction
stem: Why are narrower seam allowances used at necklines and armholes?
options: Curved areas need narrower allowances to lie smoothly
These areas never need to be finished
Fabric there is always cut on the bias

explanation.correct: The source says curved areas get narrower allowances.

wrong.2: That is not the reason given.
wrong.3: That is not the reason given.

subject: Clothing Construction
stem: Before cutting, the TR says patterns are pinned:
options: Along the grain line, with seam allowances marked
Across the selvedge to save fabric
Only on the wrong side after sewing
Without checking the fabric for faults

explanation.correct: Patterns are pinned along the grain line and seam allowances are marked.

wrong.3: Fabric is checked for quality and faults first.

subject: Clothing Construction
stem: According to the TR, what is done to fabric before the pattern is laid out?
options: It is checked for faults, width and selvedges, then soaked or drip-dried and pressed
It is sewn into a tube to test the seams first
It is cut into strips to measure its stretch
It is bleached to remove all color first

explanation.correct: These preparation steps come before cutting.

wrong.1: That is not a preparation step.
wrong.2: That is not in the TR.
wrong.3: That is not in the TR.

subject: Clothing Construction
stem: Which sleeve types are listed in the Dressmaking NC II TR?

explanation.correct: The TR lists puff, tailored and cup sleeves.

wrong.1: These are not the listed types.
wrong.2: These are not the listed types.
wrong.3: The TR lists three sleeve types.

subject: Clothing Construction
stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the faults the TR says must be corrected before a garment is released?

explanation.correct: The listed faults are grease/oil spots, puckering, loose threads, missing buttons and uneven stitches.

wrong.2: Loose threads are a listed fault.
wrong.3: Uneven stitches are a listed fault.

subject: Clothing Construction
stem: Which items are listed in the TR as accessories and accents?
options: Zipper, buttons, bias tape, hook and eye

explanation.correct: These are the listed accessories.

wrong.1: These are sewing supplies, not the listed accents.
wrong.2: These are not the listed accents.
wrong.3: These are not the listed accents.

subject: Clothing Construction
stem: Which underpinning knowledge does the TR list for preparing and cutting materials?
options: Fabric weight, shrinkage, pile, grain and pattern shapes
Retail prices of fabrics in different markets
The history of the sewing machine

explanation.correct: These fabric properties are listed.

subject: Clothing Construction
stem: On a European-style care label, what does the number inside the washtub symbol show?
options: The number of washes the garment can survive

explanation.correct: The number is the maximum washing temperature in °C.

wrong.2: Size is not shown in the tub.
wrong.3: Fiber content is written in words.

subject: Clothing Construction
stem: A triangle with two oblique lines inside it means:
options: Only non-chlorine bleach may be used
Do not bleach at all, in any form
Any bleach may be used freely
Tumble dry on low heat only

explanation.correct: Two oblique lines mean no chlorine bleach.

subject: Clothing Construction
stem: A square with a circle inside it on a care label refers to:

explanation.correct: A circle inside a square is tumble drying.

subject: Clothing Construction
stem: An iron symbol with three dots means a maximum sole-plate temperature of about:

explanation.correct: 1, 2 and 3 dots mean about 110, 150 and 200 °C.

wrong.3: That is not on the scale.

subject: Clothing Construction
stem: A blouse is pure silk. Which ironing setting fits best?
options: Two dots, the same as denim
Any setting, because silk does not scorch

explanation.correct: Silk takes the lowest heat level (Level 1); one dot is about 110 °C.

wrong.1: Three dots is for heat-tolerant fabrics such as cotton.
wrong.2: Denim is the highest level in the TR.

subject: Clothing Construction
stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the elements of design listed in our source?

explanation.correct: Emphasis is a principle of design, not one of the listed elements (line, shape, form, color, space, texture, value).

subject: Clothing Construction
stem: What are the three properties of color?

explanation.correct: Color has hue, intensity and value.

wrong.1: These are other elements of design.
wrong.2: These are color groupings, not the three properties.

subject: Clothing Construction
stem: A color scheme that uses tints and shades of a single hue is:

explanation.correct: Monochromatic uses one hue's tints and shades.

wrong.1: Analogous uses neighbors on the wheel.
wrong.3: Triadic uses three evenly spaced hues.

subject: Clothing Construction
stem: A student pairs a blue skirt with an orange blouse for maximum contrast. Which scheme is this?

explanation.correct: Blue and orange sit opposite on the wheel, giving maximum contrast.

wrong.1: Analogous colors are side by side.
wrong.3: That uses a base color plus the two beside its complement.

subject: Clothing Construction
stem: A triadic color scheme uses:
options: Three hues evenly spaced, 120 degrees apart

explanation.correct: Triadic means three evenly spaced hues.

subject: Clothing Construction
stem: A split-complementary scheme consists of:
options: A base color plus the two colors beside its complement
A base color plus its exact opposite only
Two pairs of complements forming a rectangle
Tints of one color split by white

explanation.correct: That is the definition.

wrong.2: That is a tetradic scheme, not split-complementary.

subject: Clothing Construction
stem: A blouse is loose around the bust and does not follow the body's shape. Which construction detail is used to fix this?

explanation.correct: Darts take in ease and give shape, especially at the bust.

wrong.1: A hem finishes the edge and sets length.
wrong.2: Buttons close the garment but do not shape it.
wrong.3: Gathering adds fullness at an edge.

subject: Clothing Construction
stem: What happens to the length of a fabric edge when it is gathered?
options: It becomes shorter where it is stitched
It stays the same but becomes stiffer
It is cut away and removed

explanation.correct: Gathering makes the fabric shorter where stitched and flares beyond.

subject: Clothing Construction
stem: A hem serves which TWO purposes?
options: Prevents unravelling and adjusts the length
Adds fullness and shapes the bust
Joins two pieces and marks the grain
Decorates the collar and closes the front

explanation.correct: A hem prevents unravelling and adjusts the length of the piece.

wrong.2: Seams join pieces; arrows mark grain.

subject: Clothing Construction
stem: Which of the following is NOT listed as a basic/block pattern in the Dressmaking TR?

explanation.correct: The listed blocks are blouse, skirt, trouser, shorts, culottes and shirt.

subject: Clothing Construction
stem: According to the TR, the final pattern may be cut:

explanation.correct: The TR says with or without seam allowance.

subject: Clothing Construction
stem: On a pattern, notches mark:
options: Seam allowances, centerlines, zipper placement and matching points
Only the brand of the pattern
Where to lengthen or shorten the piece

explanation.correct: The source lists these uses.

subject: Clothing Construction
stem: Which is NOT among the standard body measurements listed in the Dressmaking TR?

explanation.correct: The listed measurements include shoulder, neck, bust, waistline, hips, lengths and armhole.

subject: Clothing Construction
stem: Most garments are cut with which grain running from top to bottom?
options: Any grain, since it does not matter

explanation.correct: Most garments are cut with the straight grain running top to bottom.

wrong.2: Bias is used for drape, not most garments.

subject: Clothing Construction
stem: The cross grain runs:
options: Perpendicular to the selvedge, along the weft
Parallel to the selvedge, along the warp

explanation.correct: That is the cross grain.

wrong.3: That is not a grain direction.

subject: Clothing Construction
stem: A wider seam allowance such as 5/8 inch helps especially with fabrics that:

explanation.correct: The source notes 5/8 in helps with fabrics that ravel.

subject: Clothing Construction
stem: After sewing, a dressmaker finds a grease spot and a missing button. What does the TR require before releasing the garment?
options: Release it and let the client fix them
Charge extra for the missing button
Hide the spot under a label

explanation.correct: The TR lists grease spots and missing buttons as faults to correct.

wrong.2: That is not the TR rule.
wrong.3: That does not correct the fault.

subject: Clothing Construction
stem: On US care labels, washing temperature is shown by:

explanation.correct: The source notes US labels use dots instead of numbers.

subject: Clothing Construction
stem: A care label carries pictograms for which five kinds of care?
options: Washing, bleaching, drying, ironing and professional cleaning
Cutting, sewing, pressing, folding and selling
Dyeing, weaving, knitting, felting and spinning
Storing, packing, shipping, pricing and displaying

explanation.correct: These are the five categories.

subject: Clothing Construction
stem: The color property that refers to brightness or dullness (chroma) is:
options: Hue, the name of the color

explanation.correct: Intensity is also called chroma.

wrong.3: Texture is not a color property.

subject: Clothing Construction
stem: A designer pairs red with the two colors on either side of green. Which scheme is this?

explanation.correct: A base plus the two colors beside its complement is split-complementary.

wrong.1: That would pair red with green only.
wrong.3: That uses only red tints and shades.

subject: Clothing Construction
stem: A skirt waistband is drawn up so the fabric below flares into soft, irregular folds. Which technique was used?

explanation.correct: Gathering makes small irregular folds held by a thread.

wrong.1: Darts are pointed folds for fit.

subject: Clothing Construction
stem: A tracing wheel is also known as a:
options: Pattern wheel, pounce wheel or dart wheel

explanation.correct: The source lists these names.

wrong.2: That is not in our source.

subject: Workplace Safety in HE
stem: Under RA 11058, who chairs the workplace OSH committee?
options: The employer or the employer's representative
A DOLE inspector assigned to the region

explanation.correct: The employer or representative is chairperson.

wrong.1: The safety officer is the secretary.

subject: Workplace Safety in HE
stem: In the OSH committee under RA 11058, the safety officer serves as:

explanation.correct: The safety officer is the secretary.

subject: Workplace Safety in HE
stem: How long is the mandatory safety and health seminar for all workers under RA 11058?

explanation.correct: Sec. 16(b) requires an eight-hour seminar.

subject: Workplace Safety in HE
stem: A safety officer sees workers on a broken scaffold that may collapse at any moment. What may the officer do under RA 11058?
options: Wait for the monthly committee meeting
Ignore it if the employer objects

explanation.correct: Safety officers may issue work stoppage orders when necessary.

wrong.2: Fines are imposed on violators by DOLE, not by the officer on workers.
wrong.3: The officer's duty is to act.

subject: Workplace Safety in HE
stem: Work stops for two days because of an imminent danger caused by the employer's violation. Who pays the workers' wages for those days?

explanation.correct: Sec. 23 makes the employer pay wages during such stoppage.

subject: Workplace Safety in HE
stem: Under RA 11058, the fine for willful non-compliance is up to:
options: ₱1,000,000 per worker, payable once a year

explanation.correct: Sec. 28(a) sets this fine.

wrong.1: The fine is per day and much higher.

subject: Workplace Safety in HE
stem: Under RA 11058, who are jointly and solidarily liable for OSH compliance?
options: Employer, project owner, contractor and those who manage or supervise the work
Only the workers who were injured
Only the safety officer who signed the program, and no one else

explanation.correct: Sec. 21 lists them.

wrong.1: Workers are protected, not made solely liable.
wrong.3: Liability is shared by the listed parties.

subject: Workplace Safety in HE
stem: The workplace safety and health program is prepared by the employer:
options: In consultation with workers, then submitted to DOLE
Alone and kept secret from workers
Only after an accident happens and DOLE orders one

explanation.correct: Sec. 12 requires consultation and submission to DOLE.

wrong.1: It must be available to everyone.

subject: Workplace Safety in HE
stem: Which is NOT listed as part of a workplace safety and health program under RA 11058?
options: A rule that workers buy their own fire extinguishers

explanation.correct: The program includes compliance, drug-free workplace, disease prevention, PPE, signage, toolbox meetings, accident reporting and emergency preparedness.

subject: Workplace Safety in HE
stem: Under RA 11058, what must welfare facilities include where applicable?
options: Separate sanitary, washing and sleeping facilities for men and women
Air-conditioned offices for all workers and visitors

explanation.correct: Sec. 19 requires these.

subject: Workplace Safety in HE
stem: Under PD 856, what must a food establishment have before operating for public patronage?
options: A sanitary permit from the local health office
A health certificate for the building from the city engineer
A permit from the Department of Education

explanation.correct: Sec. 14 requires a sanitary permit.

subject: Workplace Safety in HE
stem: Under PD 856, what document must each food establishment employee have?
options: A health certificate from the local health authority
A sanitary permit in their own name
A barangay clearance and a police clearance only

explanation.correct: Sec. 15 requires a health certificate.

wrong.1: The sanitary permit is for the establishment.

subject: Workplace Safety in HE
stem: A carinderia changes owners. Within how many days must the new owner have the change noted on the sanitary permit?
options: No need; the old permit still applies

explanation.correct: Sec. 14(d) requires noting within 14 days.

subject: Workplace Safety in HE
stem: Where must the sanitary permit be displayed?
options: In a conspicuous place in the establishment
Only on the city hall bulletin board for the public

explanation.correct: Sec. 14 says post it conspicuously.

wrong.3: It is posted in the establishment.

subject: Workplace Safety in HE
stem: Under PD 856, when must food handlers wash their hands with soap and water?
options: Immediately before working and after using the toilet
Only at the end of the shift
Only when the hands look dirty
Once a week, during the sanitary inspector's visit

explanation.correct: Sec. 19(b)(iii) requires this.

subject: Workplace Safety in HE
stem: Under PD 856, what headwear is required in a food establishment?
options: The cook wears a prescribed cap; female employees wear caps or hairnets
Only the owner wears a cap when visiting the kitchen

explanation.correct: Sec. 19(b) sets these rules.

wrong.3: The rule names the cook and female employees.

subject: Workplace Safety in HE
stem: A salon worker notices cut hair and a spilled solution on the floor near a client's chair. What does the Beauty Care TR require?
options: Remove spills, hair and other hazards from floors promptly
Ask the client to step around it until the shift ends

explanation.correct: The TR requires prompt removal.

wrong.3: That does not remove the hazard.

subject: Workplace Safety in HE
stem: According to the Beauty Care TR, what is done with salon linen?
options: It is stored, cleaned and disinfected
It is thrown away after one use to save time
It is kept on the floor

explanation.correct: The TR requires storing, cleaning and disinfecting linen.

wrong.2: The TR describes cleaning and disinfecting.

subject: Workplace Safety in HE
stem: When a salon tool needs repair, the Beauty Care TR says the worker should:
options: Throw it in the waste bin with hair

explanation.correct: The TR says check maintenance needs and refer for repair.

wrong.1: Faulty tools are referred for repair.
wrong.2: That is not the TR procedure.

subject: Workplace Safety in HE
stem: Which stock practice does the Beauty Care TR require?
options: Stock rotation and recording of stock levels
Buying stock only when a client asks for a product

explanation.correct: The TR requires these.

wrong.1: That is not the practice named.

subject: Workplace Safety in HE
stem: Which are the three elements of the TESDA unit "Practice career professionalism"?
options: Integrate personal and organizational goals; set and meet priorities; maintain professional growth
Buy tools; sell products; pay taxes
Plan the design, take measurements, draft the pattern

explanation.correct: These are the three elements.

subject: Workplace Safety in HE
stem: Under "Practice career professionalism", maintaining professional growth includes:
options: Obtaining and renewing licenses and certifications
Changing jobs every month to gain new experiences

explanation.correct: The unit lists NCs, COCs and professional licenses.

subject: Workplace Safety in HE
stem: Setting and meeting work priorities, under the TESDA unit, includes:
options: Using resources efficiently and maintaining equipment economically
Doing the easiest tasks first regardless of deadlines
Leaving the care of equipment to customers and suppliers

explanation.correct: The unit lists these practices.

subject: Workplace Safety in HE
stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the emergency-related drills listed in the Cookery NC II OHS unit?

explanation.correct: The drills are fire, earthquake, BLS/CPR, first aid, spillage control and disaster preparedness.

subject: Workplace Safety in HE
stem: A worker gave information to a DOLE inspector and was then demoted by the employer for it. Under RA 11058, what penalty applies?
options: No penalty, since demotion is the employer's right
Only a verbal warning from the barangay
The worker pays a fine for reporting

explanation.correct: Sec. 28(b) adds a fine for retaliation.

subject: Workplace Safety in HE
stem: In an OSH committee where there is no union, workers' representatives are chosen by:
options: Election by simple majority of the workers

explanation.correct: The source states this.

subject: Workplace Safety in HE
stem: A health certificate for a food handler is issued after:
options: Physical and medical exams and required immunizations
Paying a fee only, with no examination
One week of working without problems

explanation.correct: Sec. 15 describes this.

wrong.2: The certificate is required before employment.

subject: Workplace Safety in HE
stem: Under PD 856, food handlers dry their hands with:
options: A clean or disposable towel or a hand dryer
The same cloth used to wipe tables

explanation.correct: Sec. 19 lists these.

subject: Workplace Safety in HE
stem: Which lifting practice does the Beauty Care TR require?
options: Lifting heavy stock with a bent back to save time
Carrying everything at once in one trip
Asking clients to carry salon supplies

explanation.correct: The TR requires them.

subject: Workplace Safety in HE
stem: Under the Beauty Care TR, salon walkways should be kept:
options: Stacked with extra stock for quick access
Covered with cut hair until closing

explanation.correct: The TR says keep walkways uncluttered.

subject: Workplace Safety in HE
stem: A cook renews her National Certificate and takes a new short course on food safety. Which element of "Practice career professionalism" is this?
options: Set and meet work priorities only
Integrate personal objectives with organizational goals

explanation.correct: Renewing certifications is part of professional growth.

subject: Tools and Equipment in HE
stem: Which are the three elements of the Cookery NC II unit "Clean and maintain kitchen premises"?
options: Clean, sanitize and store equipment; clean and sanitize premises; dispose of waste
Buy supplies; cook meals; serve guests at tables
Plan menus; cost recipes; set selling prices for dishes
Greet guests; seat guests; take orders from guests

explanation.correct: These are the three elements.

subject: Tools and Equipment in HE
stem: According to the Cookery TR, equipment and utensils are cleaned and sanitized using:
options: Chemicals and clean potable water, following manufacturer's instructions
Only hot water, with no chemicals of any kind
Any liquid on hand, including used cooking oil
Sand and ash, as in traditional practice

explanation.correct: Element 1 states this.

wrong.1: The TR names chemicals and potable water.
wrong.2: Potable water and proper chemicals are required.
wrong.3: That is not in the TR.

subject: Tools and Equipment in HE
stem: How are kitchen premises cleaned according to the TR?
options: On a cleaning schedule, without damage to health or property
Only when an inspector is expected to visit
Once a year, during the long holiday break
Only by the head chef, never by staff

explanation.correct: Element 2 requires a cleaning schedule.

wrong.3: The TR does not limit it this way.

subject: Tools and Equipment in HE
stem: What does the TR require about kitchen waste?
options: It is sorted and disposed of per sanitary regulations
It is mixed together in one open drum
It is buried behind the kitchen every evening
It is left for the next shift to handle

explanation.correct: Element 3 requires sorting and proper disposal.

wrong.3: Disposal is part of the unit.

subject: Tools and Equipment in HE
stem: According to the Bread and Pastry TR, ingredients are:
options: Selected, measured and weighed according to the recipe
Estimated by eye to save time during busy hours
Chosen only by their price at the market
Mixed first and measured after baking

explanation.correct: Element 1.1 states this.

wrong.1: The TR requires measuring and weighing.

subject: Tools and Equipment in HE
stem: Rolling butter into dough in layers, as in croissants, is which technique listed in the TR?
options: Proofing the dough in a warm, humid cabinet
Panning the dough into greased molds
Scaling the dough into equal weights

explanation.correct: Laminating is listed among the techniques; rolled-in dough is laminated.

subject: Tools and Equipment in HE
stem: Letting shaped yeast dough rise before baking is called:
options: Creaming butter and sugar until fluffy
Folding a light mixture into a heavy one
Laminating dough with layers of fat

explanation.correct: Proofing is listed among the techniques.

subject: Tools and Equipment in HE
stem: Muffins and shortcakes belong to which bakery product type in the TR?
options: Lean-yeast dough breads such as sourdough
Rich-yeast sweet dough and rolled-in dough
Soft dough loaves and buns made with yeast

explanation.correct: The TR lists muffins and shortcakes as quick breads.

subject: Tools and Equipment in HE
stem: Which is NOT one of the quality criteria for bakery products in the TR?

explanation.correct: The criteria are color, consistency and texture, moisture, mouth feel and appearance.

subject: Tools and Equipment in HE
stem: In storing bakery products, which factors does the TR say to consider?
options: Temperature, light and air exposure, containers and labeling
Only the color of the box the bread is placed in
The baker's favorite music while storing
Only the time of day the product was sold

explanation.correct: The range of variables lists these.

wrong.3: That is not the listed factor.

subject: Tools and Equipment in HE
stem: According to the TR, the oven temperature is chosen based on:
options: The desired characteristics of the product
The color of the oven door
The number of bakers on duty

explanation.correct: Element 1.5 links oven temperature to product characteristics.

subject: Tools and Equipment in HE
stem: Which machine is used to finish raw edges in the Dressmaking TR's list?

explanation.correct: The TR lists the edging machine among machine types.

subject: Tools and Equipment in HE
stem: A sewing machine's needle breaks during work. Under the TR, this is classified as:
options: A major fault, like a defective motor
Not a fault at all, so it is ignored
A reason to scrap the whole machine

explanation.correct: Broken needle is listed as a minor fault.

wrong.1: Major faults include motor defects and timing problems.

subject: Tools and Equipment in HE
stem: A machine's needle and hook timing is not synchronized. Under the TR, this is:
options: A minor fault, like loose threads
Normal for a new machine and safe to use
A matter for the client to fix

explanation.correct: Timing not synchronized is a major fault.

wrong.3: Faults are reported to the supervisor.

subject: Tools and Equipment in HE
stem: Basic machine maintenance in the Dressmaking TR includes:
options: Cleaning and lubricating per the manufacturer and reporting problems
Repainting the machine body every week
Replacing the motor at every use
Taking the machine apart after each garment

explanation.correct: The maintenance elements include these.

subject: Tools and Equipment in HE
stem: According to Housekeeping NC II, cleaning equipment should be checked:
options: For cleanliness and safety before use
Only after it breaks down during work
Once a year by the hotel owner
Never, as long as it looks new

explanation.correct: Element 1 requires checking equipment before use.

subject: Tools and Equipment in HE
stem: In Housekeeping NC II, cleaning chemicals are chosen according to:
options: The type of material being cleaned
The color of the cleaning bottle
Whatever chemical is cheapest that day

explanation.correct: Element 2 says choose by material such as glass, leather, wood or carpet.

subject: Tools and Equipment in HE
stem: Which is NOT listed as a hazard to watch for when cleaning public areas?

explanation.correct: The hazards listed include spills, slippery floors, fumes, blood, needles, broken glass and hot surfaces.

subject: Tools and Equipment in HE
stem: Which of the following is NOT protective clothing listed in Housekeeping NC II?

explanation.correct: The list includes overalls, aprons, goggles, masks, waterproof clothing and footwear, and headwear.

subject: Tools and Equipment in HE
stem: Which is NOT listed as baking equipment in the Bread and Pastry TR?

explanation.correct: Baking equipment includes mixers, scales, ovens, moulds and baking pans.

subject: Tools and Equipment in HE
stem: Sweet dough and rolled-in (laminated) dough belong to which product type in the TR?

explanation.correct: The TR lists these under rich-yeast dough.

wrong.1: Quick breads do not use yeast.

subject: Tools and Equipment in HE
stem: If an accident happens while cleaning kitchen premises, the TR says to:
options: Continue cleaning and report it next month
Hide the incident from the supervisor

explanation.correct: Element 2 requires first aid procedures.

subject: Tools and Equipment in HE
stem: In Housekeeping NC II, cleaning agents may be:
options: Dry or wet, chosen per the manufacturer and OSH rules
Any liquid found in the guest room

explanation.correct: Element 1 describes this.

subject: Tools and Equipment in HE
stem: In the Dressmaking TR, a defective electric motor in a sewing machine is a:

explanation.correct: Electric motor defects are major faults.

subject: Assessment in HE
stem: In TESDA's "Conduct competency assessment" unit, which sequence of elements is correct?
options: Organize, prepare candidate, gather evidence, decide, record, give feedback
Gather evidence, organize, decide, prepare candidate, give feedback, record
Prepare candidate, decide, gather evidence, organize, record, give feedback
Organize, gather evidence, give feedback, prepare candidate, record, decide

explanation.correct: These are the six elements in order.

wrong.1: Organizing and preparing come before gathering evidence.
wrong.2: The decision comes after evidence is gathered.
wrong.3: Preparing the candidate comes before evidence.

subject: Assessment in HE
stem: Before a cookery assessment begins, the assessor explains its purpose, the competency standards and the evidence to be collected. Which element is this?

explanation.correct: Element 2 explains context, purpose, standards, evidence and procedure.

wrong.1: The decision comes after evidence is gathered.

subject: Assessment in HE
stem: When making the assessment decision, the assessor evaluates evidence against:
options: The rules of evidence and the dimensions of competency
The candidate's grades in previous school years
The trainer's personal preferences in style

explanation.correct: Element 4 uses the rules of evidence, dimensions of competency and the unit requirements.

wrong.1: Past grades are not the criterion.
wrong.2: Competency assessment is not a race against others.
wrong.3: Decisions follow the standards, not preference.

subject: Assessment in HE
stem: In the feedback element, what should the assessor do if a candidate is not yet competent?
options: Explore the gaps and advise the candidate about reassessment
Keep the result secret from the candidate
Change the result to competent to avoid disputes

explanation.correct: Element 6 says gaps are explored and reassessment is advised.

wrong.1: Feedback must be clear and constructive.
wrong.3: Disputed decisions are recorded and reported, not changed.

subject: Assessment in HE
stem: What does the TR require about assessment records?
options: They are kept per policy and outcomes are confidential
They are posted publicly on the classroom wall
They are discarded after the candidate leaves
They are given only to the candidate's parents

explanation.correct: Element 5 requires records and confidentiality.

wrong.3: Records follow policy, not this rule.

subject: Assessment in HE
stem: A candidate with a hearing impairment is about to be assessed. Which TR step addresses this?
options: Lowering the competency standard for this candidate

explanation.correct: Preparing the candidate includes determining allowable adjustments.

wrong.1: Adjustments change methods, not the standard.

subject: Assessment in HE
stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the purposes of assessment listed in the TESDA TR?
options: Ranking trainees from best to worst for a prize

explanation.correct: The listed purposes include certification, recruitment, monitoring, training needs, skills audit, RPL, classification and feedback.

subject: Assessment in HE
stem: A cook with 15 years' restaurant experience but no certificate asks to be assessed without first taking the full course. Which purpose of assessment applies?
options: Recruitment and selection for a job opening

explanation.correct: RPL assesses competencies already gained through experience.

wrong.2: He has not been in training.
wrong.3: That is not the purpose here.

subject: Assessment in HE
stem: According to the TR, evidence in competency assessment may be:

explanation.correct: The range of variables lists direct and indirect evidence.

wrong.1: Many kinds of evidence are allowed.
wrong.2: Evidence must be gathered by set methods.
wrong.3: Photographs are one possible form, not the only one.

subject: Assessment in HE
stem: When planning a session, trainers check assessment instruments for which qualities?
options: Length, color, font size and paper quality

explanation.correct: The plan-training-session unit lists these.

wrong.1: These are not the qualities listed.
wrong.2: These are not the qualities listed.
wrong.3: Popularity is not a quality listed.

subject: Assessment in HE
stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the assessment methods named across the TM units?

explanation.correct: The named methods are demonstration with oral questioning, written tests, interviews, third-party reports and portfolios.

subject: Assessment in HE
stem: Assigning numbers to answer "how much?" is called:

explanation.correct: Measurement assigns numbers.

wrong.2: Assessment is the broader process of gathering information.
wrong.3: Reflection is thinking about one's practice.

subject: Assessment in HE
stem: Making a value judgment about the information collected is called:

explanation.correct: Evaluation makes judgments about information.

wrong.3: Observation is one way of gathering information.

subject: Assessment in HE
stem: While students practice sewing a seam, the teacher walks around and asks quick questions to spot problems and adjust the lesson. This is:

explanation.correct: Spontaneous observation during seatwork is informal formative assessment.

wrong.1: Summative comes after instruction and grades it.

subject: Assessment in HE
stem: "Assessment for learning" is usually:

explanation.correct: Assessment for learning is usually formative, during instruction.

wrong.2: Reference type is a different issue.
wrong.3: Formative assessment can be formal and recorded.

subject: Assessment in HE
stem: Which statement about formal formative assessment is correct?
options: It is planned, systematic gathering of data during instruction
It happens only at the end of the term
It is always a spontaneous remark by the teacher
It is used only to certify competency

explanation.correct: Formal formative assessment is planned and systematic.

subject: Assessment in HE
stem: In a performance assessment, what does the teacher observe?
options: Both the process (procedure) and the product
Only the final written answer sheet
Only the time the task took

explanation.correct: Performance assessment observes process and product.

wrong.1: That would be a pencil-and-paper test.
wrong.2: Time alone is not the focus.

subject: Assessment in HE
stem: What is the difference between alternative and authentic assessment?
options: Alternative means not pencil-and-paper; authentic means similar to real-world tasks
Alternative is always graded; authentic is never graded
They are identical terms with no difference
Authentic means multiple-choice; alternative means essay

explanation.correct: The source defines them this way.

wrong.2: They overlap but are defined differently.

subject: Assessment in HE
stem: Which is a recognized DISADVANTAGE of performance assessment?
options: It is time-consuming and hard to score reliably
It hides the learning goals from students

explanation.correct: The source lists these disadvantages.

wrong.1: Assessing complex outcomes is an advantage.
wrong.2: It usually has good content validity.

subject: Assessment in HE
stem: Performance assessments usually have good:
options: Coverage of many tasks in one hour

explanation.correct: The source says they usually have good content validity.

wrong.2: They are hard to score reliably.

subject: Assessment in HE
stem: Students plan, cook and serve a three-course meal to invited guests in the school canteen. This assessment is best described as:

explanation.correct: It is a complex, real-world task observed for process and product.

subject: Assessment in HE
stem: A rubric that gives one overall score from general descriptions is:

explanation.correct: A holistic rubric gives one overall score.

wrong.1: An analytic rubric scores each criterion separately.
wrong.2: A checklist marks presence, not levels.

subject: Assessment in HE
stem: A teacher wants to give students separate feedback on cutting accuracy, seam quality and finishing. Which rubric fits best?
options: No rubric, only a letter grade

explanation.correct: Analytic rubrics describe levels for each characteristic separately, giving more specific feedback.

wrong.1: A holistic rubric gives only one overall score.

subject: Assessment in HE
stem: What is an advantage of a holistic rubric compared with an analytic one?
options: It gives more specific feedback on each trait
It always has more score levels
It removes all need for teacher judgment

explanation.correct: The source notes holistic rubrics are quicker to develop.

wrong.1: That is the analytic rubric's strength.
wrong.2: The number of levels is not the difference.

subject: Assessment in HE
stem: Our source defines a portfolio as:
options: A purposeful collection of work that tells the story of achievement or growth
A folder that keeps every paper the student ever made
A single final exam with a cover page
A list of grades from all subjects

explanation.correct: A portfolio is a meaningful, purposeful collection.

wrong.1: The source says it is purposeful, not everything.

subject: Assessment in HE
stem: Which portfolio holds the student's best work, usually chosen by the student?

explanation.correct: Showcase portfolios hold best work.

wrong.3: That is not one of the student portfolio types.

subject: Assessment in HE
stem: A working portfolio is:
options: Day-to-day work not meant for assessment of learning
The best finished pieces for a final grade
A complete record used to certify competence
A file kept only by the parents

explanation.correct: Working portfolios hold ongoing work.

wrong.2: That would be a documentation use.

subject: Assessment in HE
stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the four dimensions of portfolio purpose in our source?
options: Assessment for learning versus of learning

explanation.correct: The dimensions are for vs of learning, current vs progress, showcase vs documentation, finished vs working.

subject: Assessment in HE
stem: Which law established the Philippine Qualifications Framework (PQF)?

explanation.correct: RA 10968 institutionalized the PQF.

wrong.2: RA 10533 is the K to 12 law.
wrong.3: RA 7836 is the teachers' professionalization law.

subject: Assessment in HE
stem: PQF level descriptors are defined by which three domains?
options: Knowledge, skills and values; application; degree of independence

explanation.correct: Sec. 8 lists these.

wrong.2: These are Bloom-style domains, not the PQF's.

subject: Assessment in HE
stem: The PQF harmonizes qualification levels across which sectors?

explanation.correct: The PQF covers all three.

wrong.1: It also covers basic and TVET.
wrong.2: It is not limited to private schools.

subject: Assessment in HE
stem: Under RA 7796, who sets national occupational skills standards?

explanation.correct: Sec. 22 assigns this to accredited industry committees.

wrong.1: Principals do not set national standards.
wrong.2: DepEd does not set these standards.

subject: Assessment in HE
stem: Before a Bread and Pastry assessment, the assessor checks the venue, tools and ingredients and confirms the schedule. Which element is this?

explanation.correct: Element 1 is organizing the assessment.

subject: Assessment in HE
stem: During the assessment, the assessor observes the candidate kneading and shaping dough and asks oral questions, recording what she sees. Which element is this?

explanation.correct: Observing and questioning to collect evidence is element 3.

wrong.3: That is explaining the process beforehand.

subject: Assessment in HE
stem: A candidate disagrees with the "not yet competent" decision. What does the TR say about this?
options: Disputed decisions are recorded and reported
The assessor must change the decision immediately
The candidate may never be reassessed

explanation.correct: Element 6 requires this.

wrong.1: The TR does not say this.
wrong.3: It must be recorded and reported.

subject: Assessment in HE
stem: In competency assessment, evidence is gathered using the methods specified in the:

explanation.correct: Element 3 uses the Evidence Guide's methods.

wrong.2: That is not the specified source.
wrong.3: That is not the specified source.

subject: Assessment in HE
stem: After the decision and records, what does the assessor organize for competent candidates?

explanation.correct: Element 5 includes organizing the issuing of certificates.

wrong.1: That is not in the element.
wrong.2: That is not in the element.
wrong.3: That is not in the element.

subject: Assessment in HE
stem: A hotel tests applicants' housekeeping skills before hiring. Which purpose of assessment in the TR is this?

explanation.correct: Assessment can be used to recruit and select.

wrong.1: RPL credits past learning toward certification.

subject: Assessment in HE
stem: Midway through a cookery course, the trainer assesses trainees to tell them what they still need to improve. Which purpose is this?
options: Giving feedback on progress during training

explanation.correct: This is a listed purpose.

subject: Assessment in HE
stem: A resort assesses all its kitchen staff to find out which skills the team has and lacks. This purpose is a:
options: Recognition of prior learning for one person

explanation.correct: Checking the skills of current staff is a skills audit.

wrong.2: That is not the main purpose described.

subject: Assessment in HE
stem: An assessor accepts a signed report from a candidate's restaurant supervisor describing her work. This is an example of:

explanation.correct: Third-party reports are a named assessment method.

wrong.2: The candidate did not perform it in front of the assessor.
wrong.3: The assessor did not interview the candidate.

subject: Assessment in HE
stem: At the end of the quarter, a teacher gives a test to grade and certify what learners learned in the sewing unit. This is:

explanation.correct: Assessment after instruction to grade is summative.

subject: Assessment in HE
stem: Assessment is defined in our source as:
options: Gathering information about learning and making value judgments

explanation.correct: The source defines assessment this way.

subject: Assessment in HE
stem: A teacher counts how many stitches per inch each learner made. This is mainly:

explanation.correct: Assigning numbers is measurement.

subject: Assessment in HE
stem: Learners repair a sewing machine while the teacher watches the steps and checks the result. This is:
options: Performance assessment of process and product

explanation.correct: Repairing a machine is a source example of performance assessment.

subject: Assessment in HE
stem: Authenticity of an assessment task is:
options: Either fully present or fully absent

explanation.correct: The source says authenticity is a matter of degree.

subject: Assessment in HE
stem: Which is NOT an advantage of performance assessment in our source?
options: It is quick to score reliably

explanation.correct: It is hard to score reliably and time-consuming.

subject: Assessment in HE
stem: Because performance tasks take time, a teacher can give only two in a quarter. What drawback does this show?
options: Fewer tasks can be done because they are time-consuming
They always have poor content validity

explanation.correct: The source names this drawback.

wrong.1: They usually have good content validity.

subject: Assessment in HE
stem: A teacher scores a dressmaking project with one overall rating of 1 to 4 based on a general description. This rubric is:

explanation.correct: One overall score from general descriptions is holistic.

wrong.2: A checklist marks presence or absence.

subject: Assessment in HE
stem: An analytic rubric describes levels for each characteristic separately, which gives:

explanation.correct: Analytic rubrics give more specific feedback.

wrong.1: Holistic rubrics are quicker to develop.

subject: Assessment in HE
stem: A learner keeps all drafts, recipes and sketches from the term in one folder to show how her skills grew. This portfolio mainly shows:
options: Nothing, because it is not graded

explanation.correct: A collection of all work showing growth fits progress and documentation.

wrong.1: A showcase holds selected best work.

subject: Assessment in HE
stem: Who usually chooses the work in a showcase portfolio, according to our source?

explanation.correct: Showcase work is usually chosen by the student.

subject: Assessment in HE
stem: The PQF supports which practice that credits learning gained outside formal schooling?

explanation.correct: The PQF supports RPL.

subject: Assessment in HE
stem: Under RA 7796, who conducts trade tests for certification?
options: Accredited bodies, under TESDA's certification and accreditation program
No one; certificates are free for all

explanation.correct: Sec. 22 describes this.

subject: Assessment in HE
stem: Under RA 10968, the PQF describes:
options: Levels of qualifications and standards for learning outcomes
Only the design of school uniforms

explanation.correct: Sec. 4 describes this.

subject: Research in HE
stem: What does IMRaD stand for?

explanation.correct: IMRaD names the four main parts of a research article.

wrong.1: Methods, Results and Discussion are the correct parts.

subject: Research in HE
stem: A section of a study reports that 78% of learners improved and states whether the hypothesis was supported. Which IMRaD section is this?

explanation.correct: Results report the answer found and whether the hypothesis was supported.

wrong.1: The introduction explains why the study was done.
wrong.2: Methods describe who, when, where and how.
wrong.3: The discussion interprets implications and links to other research.

subject: Research in HE
stem: A section describes the 35 Grade 9 participants, the materials used and when the data were gathered. Which section is this?

explanation.correct: Methods describe participants, materials and procedures.

wrong.3: The introduction states the problem and question.

subject: Research in HE
stem: In which IMRaD section does the researcher explain how the findings fit with other research and suggest future studies?

explanation.correct: The discussion covers implications, fit with other research and future research.

wrong.2: Results report findings without interpreting them broadly.
wrong.3: The title page does not discuss findings.

subject: Research in HE
stem: The "wine glass" (hourglass) model of IMRaD describes a paper that moves:
options: From general to specific and back to general
From results first to introduction last
In a straight line with no change in scope from start to end

explanation.correct: Introduction is general, methods and results specific, discussion general again.

wrong.1: The model returns to general at the end.
wrong.3: The model shows a change in scope.

subject: Research in HE
stem: Which of the following is an element of research papers that lies OUTSIDE the IMRaD acronym?
options: Disclosure statement on funding and conflicts of interest

explanation.correct: Disclosure and ethics statements are other common elements.

subject: Research in HE
stem: A number that describes a property of a SAMPLE is called a:

explanation.correct: A statistic describes a sample.

wrong.2: A variable is a characteristic measured.
wrong.3: A datum is a single value.

subject: Research in HE
stem: A researcher knows the average height of ALL 1,200 learners in a school from official records. This number is a:

explanation.correct: A number describing the whole population is a parameter.

wrong.2: A lurking variable clouds a study.
wrong.3: That is the outcome in an experiment.

subject: Research in HE
stem: Which of the following is QUALITATIVE (categorical) data?
options: Students' favorite dish, recorded as words
The number of eggs used in each recipe tested
The weight of flour in grams

explanation.correct: Categorizing attributes gives qualitative data.

subject: Research in HE
stem: Which graphs are used to display qualitative data, according to our statistics source?
options: Box plots and dot plots only

explanation.correct: These display qualitative data.

wrong.2: Scatter plots show two quantitative variables.

subject: Research in HE
stem: Quantitative data can be:

explanation.correct: Quantitative data are counts (discrete) or measurements (continuous).

wrong.2: Opinions recorded as categories are qualitative.

subject: Research in HE
stem: A researcher divides learners by grade level and randomly selects a proportionate number from EACH grade. This is:

explanation.correct: Random samples from each stratum make a stratified sample.

wrong.1: A cluster sample takes all members of some groups.
wrong.2: A systematic sample takes every nth item.
wrong.3: A convenience sample uses whoever is available.

subject: Research in HE
stem: A division randomly picks 5 of its 40 schools and surveys every teacher in those 5 schools. This is:

explanation.correct: Randomly selecting some clusters and taking all their members is cluster sampling.

wrong.1: Stratified sampling takes some from every group.
wrong.2: Systematic sampling takes every nth item.

subject: Research in HE
stem: From an alphabetical class list, a teacher picks a random start and then every 5th name. This is:

explanation.correct: A random start then every nth item is systematic sampling.

subject: Research in HE
stem: A teacher surveys only the students who happen to pass by the canteen at noon. What is the main problem?
options: It is a non-random convenience sample that may be highly biased
It is a stratified sample with too many strata
It is a cluster sample of the whole school
It is too random to be useful, because anyone could pass by

explanation.correct: Convenience sampling is non-random and may be biased.

wrong.3: It is not random at all.

subject: Research in HE
stem: A teacher tests whether using video demonstrations improves sewing scores. The video demonstrations are the:

explanation.correct: The explanatory variable is the one expected to cause change.

wrong.1: The response is the sewing score.
wrong.2: A lurking variable is an unwanted outside influence.

subject: Research in HE
stem: In the same study, the learners' sewing scores are the:

explanation.correct: The outcome measured is the response variable.

wrong.2: A control group is a set of participants.
wrong.3: Scores are the outcome, not an outside influence.

subject: Research in HE
stem: The class using videos also had a more experienced teacher. In the study, the teacher's experience is a possible:
options: Control variable that removes bias automatically

explanation.correct: A variable other than the explanatory one that can cloud the result is a lurking variable.

wrong.3: A sampling frame is a list of the population.

subject: Research in HE
stem: Why does an experiment include a control group?
options: To balance the effects of simply being in an experiment
To make the treatment group larger
To guarantee that the hypothesis will be proven true

explanation.correct: A control group balances these effects.

subject: Research in HE
stem: In a double-blind experiment:
options: Both the subjects and the researchers dealing with them do not know who gets the treatment
Only the data analysts are blinded
No one, including the researchers, is told the purpose afterward

explanation.correct: Double-blinding blinds both.

subject: Research in HE
stem: Blinding in an experiment mainly counters:

explanation.correct: Blinding counters the power of suggestion.

subject: Research in HE
stem: Who coined the term "action research", and when?

explanation.correct: Lewin coined the term in 1944.

wrong.1: Dewey wrote on democracy and education, not this term.
wrong.2: Mertler later described a cycle used by teachers.
wrong.3: Schön wrote on the reflective practitioner.

subject: Research in HE
stem: Lewin described action research as a spiral of steps, each a circle of:
options: Planning, action and fact-finding about the result
Lecturing, assigning homework and collecting the papers

explanation.correct: Lewin's 1946 description uses these steps.

subject: Research in HE
stem: Which order matches Mertler's action research cycle?
options: Planning, acting, developing an action plan, communicating and reflecting
Acting, planning, reflecting, developing an action plan
Communicating and reflecting, planning, acting, developing an action plan
Developing an action plan, acting, planning, reflecting

explanation.correct: These are the four stages in order.

subject: Research in HE
stem: Which of the following belongs to the PLANNING stage of Mertler's cycle?

explanation.correct: Planning includes identifying the problem, reviewing literature and developing a plan.

wrong.2: That is developing an action plan.

subject: Research in HE
stem: Compared with ordinary good teaching, action research is:
options: Planned more thoughtfully, recorded more systematically and shared more openly
Done without any data, relying on the teacher's memory alone

explanation.correct: The source says so.

wrong.1: Action research is done by teachers.

subject: Research in HE
stem: A Home Economics teacher records her lessons on video and keeps a journal to study why learners struggle with pattern drafting. What is she doing?
options: Conducting a national census of all learners

explanation.correct: Videotaping one's lessons and keeping a journal are action research data sources.

subject: Research in HE
stem: A teacher wants to publish her classroom study in a journal. What must she obtain first?
options: Informed consent from parents or guardians and students
Nothing, since the data come from her own class

explanation.correct: Sharing outside the school needs informed consent.

wrong.2: All participants and guardians must consent.
wrong.3: Consent is needed when data are shared outside.

subject: Research in HE
stem: Which of the following is NOT usually part of an informed consent form for classroom research?
options: A promise of higher grades for those who join
A description of the study and data
A statement that participation is voluntary and may be stopped
A guarantee of confidentiality or anonymity

explanation.correct: The form describes the study, says participation is voluntary, and guarantees confidentiality.

subject: Research in HE
stem: How is taking part in research different from doing an ordinary class task?
options: Students may choose not to take part in research
Students must always join research projects
Research needs no permission from anyone at all

explanation.correct: Participation in research is voluntary.

wrong.1: Research participation should not be required for grades.

subject: Research in HE
stem: Under RA 10173, learners' education and health information is classified as:

explanation.correct: Sec. 3(l) lists education and health as sensitive.

subject: Research in HE
stem: A study's opening explains that many Grade 8 learners struggle with measuring ingredients and asks whether visual cards help. Which section is this?

explanation.correct: The introduction gives the reason and research question.

wrong.1: Methods describe who, when, where and how.

subject: Research in HE
stem: IMRaD is the most common structure for:

explanation.correct: The source says so.

subject: Research in HE
stem: A teacher records each learner's favorite cooking method (boil, fry, steam). This data is:

explanation.correct: Categories described in words are qualitative.

subject: Research in HE
stem: A teacher counts how many eggs each group used. This data is:

explanation.correct: Counts are discrete quantitative data.

subject: Research in HE
stem: In a cluster sample, the researcher:
options: Randomly selects some clusters and takes all their members
Takes a random sample from every stratum
Picks every nth item after a random start
Uses whoever is easiest to reach

explanation.correct: That is cluster sampling.

subject: Research in HE
stem: Why must the explanatory variable be isolated in an experiment?
options: So lurking variables do not cloud the results
So the sample becomes a convenience sample
So no data need to be collected
So the results always support the hypothesis

explanation.correct: Isolating the explanatory variable controls lurking variables.

subject: Research in HE
stem: Action research leads to:
options: Concrete decisions that improve teaching in a particular context
General laws for every school in the world

explanation.correct: The source defines action research this way.

wrong.1: It focuses on a particular context.

subject: Research in HE
stem: A teacher's consent form says participation is voluntary and names will be kept confidential. What else should it include?
options: A description of the study and the data to be collected
A promise of extra grades for joining
A requirement that all must join

explanation.correct: The form describes the research and data.

subject: Research in HE
stem: In a taste test, neither the learners nor the teacher serving the samples knows which cookie has less sugar. This is:

explanation.correct: Both subjects and the researchers dealing with them are blinded.

wrong.1: Only one side would be blinded.

subject: Foundations of Education
stem: In functionalist sociology, what is the difference between manifest and latent functions of education?
options: Manifest functions are intended and visible; latent functions are hidden and unintended
Manifest functions are hidden; latent functions are intended and visible
Manifest functions belong to private schools; latent ones to public schools
They are two names for the same function of schooling

explanation.correct: The source defines them this way.

wrong.2: The terms are not about school type.

subject: Foundations of Education
stem: Which sociologist called schools "socialization agencies"?
options: Karl Marx, writing about class conflict
George Herbert Mead, writing about the self

explanation.correct: Durkheim described schools as socialization agencies.

wrong.1: Marx is linked to conflict theory.

subject: Foundations of Education
stem: Two classmates in a college program later help each other find jobs through their school friendships. To a functionalist, this is a:

explanation.correct: Social networks that later help with jobs are a latent function.

wrong.1: Socialization is intended; job networks are an unintended effect.

subject: Foundations of Education
stem: Teaching students to respect authority and obey laws is which manifest function of education?

explanation.correct: Social control teaches conformity to law and respect for authority.

wrong.2: Tracking is a practice conflict theorists criticize.
wrong.3: That is not the function described.

subject: Foundations of Education
stem: A sociologist argues that grouping students into "fast" and "slow" sections keeps poor children in low tracks. Which perspective is this?
options: Symbolic interactionism only, about classroom talk

explanation.correct: Conflict theorists argue tracking perpetuates inequality.

wrong.1: Functionalists stress the positive functions of schooling.
wrong.2: Interactionists study interactions and labels; the inequality claim is conflict theory.

subject: Foundations of Education
stem: A teacher keeps calling a learner a "slow student," and the learner begins to perform poorly. Which concept explains this?

explanation.correct: Interactionists show how labels can become self-fulfilling prophecies.

wrong.1: Labeling is not an intended function.

subject: Foundations of Education
stem: According to conflict theorists, the hidden curriculum tends to favor students who have more:

explanation.correct: The hidden curriculum favors those with more cultural capital.

subject: Foundations of Education
stem: Which perspective studies the roots and effects of gender inequality in education?

explanation.correct: Feminist theory studies gender inequality in education.

subject: Foundations of Education
stem: Symbolic interactionists studying education focus mainly on:
options: Classroom dynamics and interactions between students and teachers
The four questions of curriculum planning

explanation.correct: The source describes this focus.

subject: Foundations of Education
stem: Under RA 11650, which schools are covered by the policy of inclusion?
options: All early and basic education schools, public and private
Only private schools with special programs

explanation.correct: Sec. 5 covers public and private schools.

wrong.1: SPED centers are converted to ILRCs; coverage is broader.

subject: Foundations of Education
stem: A private school refuses to admit a child solely because she uses a wheelchair. Under RA 11650 this is:
options: Not allowed; no learner may be denied admission on the basis of disability
Allowed, since private schools choose freely
Allowed if the school lacks ramps

explanation.correct: Sec. 5 bars denial of admission on the basis of disability.

wrong.2: Disability cannot be the basis for denial.

subject: Foundations of Education
stem: Under RA 11650, what happens to existing SPED Centers?
options: They are converted and renamed Inclusive Learning Resource Centers
They are closed and their teachers dismissed
They are merged with TESDA centers

explanation.correct: Sec. 6 converts them into ILRCs.

subject: Foundations of Education
stem: The Child Find System under RA 11650 is run by the ILRC to:
options: Identify, locate and evaluate learners with disabilities not receiving education services
Find children who skip classes and punish them

explanation.correct: Sec. 7 describes the Child Find System.

subject: Foundations of Education
stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the processes named in RA 11650's definition of inclusive education?

explanation.correct: Inclusive education involves accommodation, modification, adaptation and individualization.

subject: Foundations of Education
stem: Under RA 11106, what is the national sign language of the Filipino deaf?

explanation.correct: RA 11106 declares Filipino Sign Language the national sign language.

wrong.1: The law names Filipino Sign Language.
wrong.2: The law names Filipino Sign Language.
wrong.3: Braille is a tactile writing system.

subject: Foundations of Education
stem: RA 11510 institutionalizes which program?

explanation.correct: RA 11510 is the ALS Act.

subject: Foundations of Education
stem: Under Art. XIV Sec. 2(2) of the 1987 Constitution, which level of education is compulsory for all children of school age?

explanation.correct: The Constitution makes elementary education compulsory.

subject: Foundations of Education
stem: Under the 1987 Constitution, free public education is maintained at which levels?

explanation.correct: Art. XIV Sec. 2(2) maintains free public education in elementary and high school.

wrong.1: The provision names elementary and high school.
wrong.2: The provision names elementary and high school.
wrong.3: The provision names elementary and high school.

subject: Foundations of Education
stem: Art. XIV Sec. 2(4) of the Constitution directs the State to encourage:
options: Non-formal, informal and indigenous learning systems
Only formal schooling in public schools

explanation.correct: The provision names these.

subject: Foundations of Education
stem: Act No. 74 (1901) established which body?
options: The Department of Education, Culture and Sports

explanation.correct: Act No. 74 created the Department of Public Instruction.

subject: Foundations of Education
stem: Under Act No. 74, which language was to become the basis of public school instruction "as soon as practicable"?

explanation.correct: Sec. 14 made English the basis of instruction.

wrong.1: Spanish had been the colonial language; Act 74 chose English.

subject: Foundations of Education
stem: Under Act No. 74, primary instruction in the public schools was:
options: Open only to children of officials

explanation.correct: Sec. 1 made all primary instruction free.

subject: Foundations of Education
stem: A school teaches children to take turns, cooperate and prepare for future jobs. To Durkheim and the functionalists, this mainly shows which manifest function?

explanation.correct: Socialization is the first manifest function.

subject: Foundations of Education
stem: Students learn to work with others in small groups even though no lesson aims to teach this. A functionalist would call this a:

explanation.correct: Unintended benefits such as small-group skills are latent functions.

subject: Foundations of Education
stem: Functionalists view education as:
options: One of the most important social institutions
A tool only for keeping the poor down
Only a matter of classroom talk

explanation.correct: The source says so.

subject: Foundations of Education
stem: A sociologist notes that children from wealthy homes already know the "rules" of school behavior and do better. Which concept fits?
options: The hidden curriculum favors those with more cultural capital

explanation.correct: Conflict theorists argue this.

subject: Foundations of Education
stem: A researcher studies how teachers' praise and seating choices shape students' views of themselves. Which perspective is this?

explanation.correct: Interactionists study classroom interactions and labels.

wrong.2: Conflict theory focuses on inequality between groups.

subject: Foundations of Education
stem: Conflict theorists argue that tracking students into advanced and low tracks:
options: Perpetuates inequality and leads to self-fulfilling prophecies

explanation.correct: The source states this.

subject: Foundations of Education
stem: Under RA 11650, an IEP includes:
options: The services, their duration and frequency, and the learner's present level
Only the learner's grades from last year
Only a list of school rules

explanation.correct: Sec. 4 lists these.

subject: Foundations of Education
stem: Under RA 11650, how many Inclusive Learning Resource Centers must be established, at least?
options: At least one in every city and municipality

explanation.correct: Sec. 6 requires at least one per city and municipality.

wrong.1: The law requires one per city and municipality.

subject: Foundations of Education
stem: An ILRC team visits homes to find children with disabilities who are not in school. Which system are they running?

explanation.correct: Identifying and locating unserved learners is Child Find.

wrong.1: ALS serves out-of-school youth and adults.

subject: Foundations of Education
stem: RA 11650 aims to give learners with disabilities:
options: Free and appropriate public early and basic education and access to general education
Separate schools only, away from other learners
Private tutoring paid by parents only

explanation.correct: Sec. 3 states these objectives.

wrong.2: The law covers early and basic education.
wrong.3: The law aims at free public education.

subject: Foundations of Education
stem: A 25-year-old who left school in Grade 6 wants to continue learning. Which program, institutionalized by law, fits?

explanation.correct: ALS serves out-of-school youth and adults.

subject: Foundations of Education
stem: A parent argues that the State may not stop her from choosing how to rear her child even though elementary schooling is compulsory. Which constitutional phrase supports her?
options: Without limiting the natural right of parents to rear their children

explanation.correct: Art. XIV Sec. 2(2) includes this phrase.

subject: Foundations of Education
stem: Art. XIV Sec. 1 directs the State to make quality education:
options: Available only to those who pay

explanation.correct: Sec. 1 says take steps to make education accessible to all.

subject: Foundations of Education
stem: Act No. 74 of 1901 was passed during which period of Philippine history?

explanation.correct: Act No. 74 was passed under American rule.

subject: Foundations of Education
stem: Courtship among classmates is classified by functionalists as a:
options: Manifest function intended by the curriculum
Form of social control by teachers

explanation.correct: The source lists courtship as a latent function.

wrong.2: That is a manifest function about authority.

subject: Foundations of Education
stem: The hidden curriculum, as used by conflict theorists, is:
options: Nonacademic knowledge learned through informal learning and cultural transmission
The official list of subjects in the curriculum guide
A secret exam given at the end of the year
Lessons taught only in private schools

explanation.correct: The source defines it this way.

subject: Foundations of Education
stem: A researcher studies why fewer girls take electrical installation courses and what this means for gender equality. Which perspective is this?

explanation.correct: Studying gender inequality in education is feminist theory.

subject: Foundations of Education
stem: A school modifies test formats and lesson materials so a learner with low vision can take part fully. Under RA 11650 this is part of:
options: Inclusive education through accommodation and modification

explanation.correct: The law's definition includes these processes.

subject: Foundations of Education
stem: Under RA 11650, inclusive education aims at learners' full:

explanation.correct: The definition names these three.

subject: Foundations of Education
stem: Under the 1987 Constitution, the State's duty regarding education is to protect and promote the right of all citizens to:
options: Private schooling paid by the State

explanation.correct: Art. XIV Sec. 1 states this.

wrong.1: The Constitution names free elementary and high school.

subject: Foundations of Education
stem: A history teacher says Act No. 74 made Tagalog the language of instruction. What is the correction?
options: Act No. 74 made English the basis of public school instruction
Act No. 74 made Spanish the only language
Act No. 74 banned all languages in schools
Act No. 74 did not mention language

explanation.correct: Sec. 14 named English.

subject: The Teaching Profession
stem: How many members compose the Board for Professional Teachers under RA 7836?
options: Three, chosen by the PRC chairperson
Nine, one from each regional office

explanation.correct: Sec. 5 sets 5 members appointed by the President.

wrong.1: The Board has five members appointed by the President.
wrong.2: The Board has five appointed members.

subject: The Teaching Profession
stem: What is the term of office of a member of the Board for Professional Teachers?
options: Three years, with no reappointment after two consecutive terms
Six years, with one term only

explanation.correct: Sec. 7 sets 3-year terms and bars a third consecutive term.

subject: The Teaching Profession
stem: What is the minimum age to be appointed to the Board for Professional Teachers?

explanation.correct: Sec. 8 requires at least 35 years of age.

wrong.3: 18 is the minimum age for LET applicants.

subject: The Teaching Profession
stem: Under RA 7836, how often must the written licensure examination be given?
options: At least once every two years
Only when there are enough applicants

explanation.correct: Sec. 13 requires at least once a year.

wrong.1: The law says once a year.
wrong.2: The law sets at least once a year.

subject: The Teaching Profession
stem: Under RA 7836, the LET for secondary teachers has how many parts?
options: Three: professional education, general education and specialization
Two: professional education and general education

explanation.correct: Sec. 14 sets three parts for secondary.

wrong.3: The law sets three parts for secondary.

subject: The Teaching Profession
stem: What is the minimum age for an LET applicant under RA 7836?

explanation.correct: Sec. 15 requires at least 18.

subject: The Teaching Profession
stem: Within how many days after the exam must the Board report ratings to the PRC?

explanation.correct: Sec. 16 sets 120 days.

subject: The Teaching Profession
stem: Under RA 7836, registration as a professional teacher begins when:
options: The name is entered in the roster of professional teachers
The applicant pays the exam fee
The applicant passes the general education part only
The school principal signs the appointment

explanation.correct: Sec. 17 says registration starts with entry in the roster.

wrong.1: Paying the fee does not register a teacher.
wrong.2: All required parts must be passed.
wrong.3: Registration is with the Board and PRC.

subject: The Teaching Profession
stem: Under RA 7836, how often may a teacher take the optional merit examination for promotion?
options: At least once in five years, free of charge

explanation.correct: Sec. 19 provides this.

wrong.1: The law says at least once in 5 years, free.
wrong.2: The law says at least once in 5 years.

subject: The Teaching Profession
stem: A person teaches in a high school without a valid certificate of registration. What penalty does RA 7836 provide?
options: A fine of ₱5,000–₱20,000, or 6 months to 5 years' imprisonment, or both
A warning only, for a first offense
A fine of ₱100 per day of teaching

explanation.correct: Sec. 28 sets this penalty.

wrong.1: The law provides a fine or imprisonment.
wrong.3: That is not a penalty in the law.

subject: The Teaching Profession
stem: A registered teacher is convicted by final judgment of a crime. What may the Board do?
options: Suspend or revoke the certificate after notice and hearing
Nothing, since the license is for life
Revoke it immediately with no hearing
Transfer the teacher to another region

explanation.correct: Sec. 23 allows this after notice and hearing.

wrong.1: The Board may suspend or revoke.
wrong.3: The Board's power concerns the certificate.

subject: The Teaching Profession
stem: A BS Biology graduate wants to take the LET for secondary teachers. Under RA 9293, how many professional education units are needed?

explanation.correct: RA 9293 requires at least 18 units for arts and sciences graduates.

subject: The Teaching Profession
stem: A licensed teacher who has not taught for six years wants to return to teaching. What does RA 9293 require?
options: At least 12 units of education courses
At least 18 units of professional education
Nothing; a license is valid forever

explanation.correct: Sec. 2 requires 12 units after 5 years without practice.

wrong.2: That is for non-education graduates taking the LET.
wrong.3: The law sets a refresher requirement.

subject: The Teaching Profession
stem: Under the PRC Modernization Act, LET questions must stay within:
options: The syllabi or TOS prepared by the professional board
Only the topics in the previous year's exam

explanation.correct: Sec. 9(h) requires questions to stay strictly within the syllabi or TOS.

wrong.2: The rule is the board's syllabi or TOS.
wrong.3: The rule is the board's syllabi or TOS.

subject: The Teaching Profession
stem: Under RA 4670, a provisional teacher becomes permanent after at least how many years of continuous, efficient and faithful service?

explanation.correct: Sec. 5 sets at least 10 years.

wrong.1: One year is the probation period for provisional status.

subject: The Teaching Profession
stem: A superintendent wants to transfer a teacher to a far school without stating reasons. What does RA 4670 require?
options: The teacher's consent, or notice of reasons with a right to appeal if the service requires it
Nothing; superintendents may transfer at will
Only the school head's verbal approval
A court order before any transfer

explanation.correct: Sec. 6 requires consent except for cause, with notice and appeal.

wrong.2: The law requires notice of reasons.
wrong.3: The law does not require a court order.

subject: The Teaching Profession
stem: Under RA 4670, who chairs the committee that first hears administrative charges against a public school teacher?
options: The Schools Division Superintendent or a representative of at least division-supervisor rank
A judge of the regional trial court

explanation.correct: Sec. 9 sets this composition.

wrong.1: The principal does not chair it.
wrong.3: The mayor does not chair it.

subject: The Teaching Profession
stem: Who sits on the RA 4670 committee hearing charges against a teacher, besides the superintendent's side?
options: A teachers' organization representative and a division supervisor
Two parents chosen by the PTA
The barangay captain and a police officer
Two students from the teacher's class

explanation.correct: Sec. 9 lists them.

subject: The Teaching Profession
stem: While a case against a teacher is pending, the school posts the charges on social media. Under RA 4670 this is:
options: Not allowed; there should be no publicity while the case is pending
Allowed if the charge is serious
Required by the Data Privacy Act

explanation.correct: Sec. 8 forbids publicity during a pending case.

subject: The Teaching Profession
stem: Under RA 4670, what is the normal maximum of actual classroom teaching per day?

explanation.correct: Sec. 13 sets at most 6 hours.

wrong.1: 8 hours is allowed only when the service requires it, with extra pay.
wrong.3: The law says 6, up to 8 with extra pay.

subject: The Teaching Profession
stem: A teacher is required to teach 8 hours a day because of a shortage. What extra pay does RA 4670 provide?
options: Regular pay plus at least 25% of basic pay
Double pay for the extra hours
No extra pay; it is part of the job

explanation.correct: Sec. 13 adds at least 25%.

subject: The Teaching Profession
stem: Under RA 4670, how often must public school teachers have a free medical examination after hiring?
options: Only when the teacher is sick

explanation.correct: Sec. 22 requires it at least once a year.

wrong.1: The law says at least once a year.
wrong.2: It is required before starting and yearly.

subject: The Teaching Profession
stem: A teacher with 8 years of service wants a study leave. Under RA 4670, what may she receive?
options: Up to one school year of leave at no less than 60% of monthly salary
Up to five years of leave at full pay

explanation.correct: Sec. 24 allows this after 7 years of service.

wrong.1: The law says up to one school year.
wrong.2: The law gives at least 60% pay.

subject: The Teaching Profession
stem: What does RA 4670 provide when a teacher's illness needs treatment for more than one year?

explanation.correct: Sec. 25 provides indefinite sick leave.

subject: The Teaching Profession
stem: Under RA 4670, what is the basis for computing a retiring teacher's benefits?
options: A one-range salary raise upon retirement
The average salary of all teachers
A fixed ₱1,000 per year of service
