explanation.correct: Sec. 26 provides a one-range raise as the basis.

subject: The Teaching Profession
stem: A school head tells an applicant she will be hired only if she does not join a teachers' union. Under RA 4670 this is:
options: Allowed if written in the contract

explanation.correct: Secs. 27–28 protect the right to join organizations.

subject: The Teaching Profession
stem: Under RA 4670, which deductions from salary are allowed with the teacher's written authority?
options: Teachers' association dues and insurance premiums
Fines for late submission of reports

explanation.correct: Sec. 21 allows these with written authority.

wrong.1: Deductions must be authorized by law.

subject: The Teaching Profession
stem: RA 4670 recognizes which condition as a compensable occupational disease of teachers?
options: Physical and nervous strain on the teacher's health

explanation.correct: Sec. 23 recognizes this.

wrong.1: That is not the condition named.
wrong.2: The law names physical and nervous strain.
wrong.3: That is not the condition named.

subject: The Teaching Profession
stem: Under RA 10912, CPD is:
options: A mandatory requirement for renewing the professional ID card
Optional, for teachers who want promotion only

explanation.correct: Sec. 10 makes CPD mandatory for renewal.

wrong.2: It applies to all PRC-regulated professionals.

subject: The Teaching Profession
stem: RA 10912 aligns CPD programs with which frameworks?
options: The PQF, the ASEAN Qualifications Reference Framework and ASEAN mutual recognition arrangements
Only the K to 12 curriculum guide

explanation.correct: Sec. 4 names these.

wrong.1: The law names the PQF and ASEAN frameworks.
wrong.2: That is not a qualifications framework.

subject: The Teaching Profession
stem: Under RA 10627, school anti-bullying policies must prohibit bullying in which setting?
options: All of the listed settings: near school grounds, at school activities and through school technology
Only inside classrooms during class hours

explanation.correct: Sec. 3 lists these settings and bans retaliation.

subject: The Teaching Profession
stem: Under RA 10627, who is responsible for implementing the school's anti-bullying policy?

explanation.correct: Sec. 4 assigns this to the principal.

wrong.1: Students report, but the principal implements.
wrong.2: The barangay is not assigned this.

subject: The Teaching Profession
stem: A student reports bullying and is later threatened for "snitching." Under RA 10627, the threat is:
options: Retaliation, which school policies must prohibit
Allowed as part of student discipline
Not bullying because it happened once
Only a matter for the parents

explanation.correct: Sec. 3 requires a ban on retaliation against those who report.

subject: The Teaching Profession
stem: Under RA 10627, schools report bullying statistics to the division superintendent:
options: Every first week of the school year
Only when a case reaches the court

explanation.correct: Sec. 5 sets this schedule.

subject: The Teaching Profession
stem: A coach asks an athlete for a sexual favor in exchange for a spot on the team. The athlete refuses. Under RA 7877, has sexual harassment been committed?
options: Yes; it is committed whether or not the demand is accepted
No, because coaches are not teachers
Only if the athlete is a minor

explanation.correct: Sec. 3 says so.

subject: The Teaching Profession
stem: Under the Safe Spaces Act (RA 11313), what must every school designate?
options: An officer to receive complaints, with published grievance procedures
A school nurse for each class
A security guard at every room

explanation.correct: Sec. 21 requires this.

wrong.1: That is not the requirement named.
wrong.2: That is not the requirement named.
wrong.3: That is not the requirement named.

subject: The Teaching Profession
stem: Under RA 7610, which of the following is NOT listed as child abuse?
options: Giving fair, explained consequences for breaking a class rule
Acts that demean a child's dignity

explanation.correct: Child abuse covers psychological and physical abuse, neglect, cruelty, sexual abuse and acts that debase a child's dignity.

subject: The Teaching Profession
stem: A 20-year-old learner with a severe intellectual disability is abused. Can RA 7610's protection for "children" apply?
options: Yes; it covers persons over 18 unable to protect themselves because of a disability
No; it covers only persons below 12
Only if a court first declares her a minor

explanation.correct: Sec. 3(a) includes such persons.

wrong.1: The age limit is 18, with this exception.

subject: The Teaching Profession
stem: Article XIV Sec. 5(5) of the 1987 Constitution directs the State to give education:

explanation.correct: Sec. 5(5) states this and aims to attract the best talents to teaching.

subject: The Teaching Profession
stem: Under RA 7836, the Board for Professional Teachers is under the general supervision and administrative control of:
options: The Department of Education's regional offices
The Commission on Higher Education alone
The Office of the Ombudsman for teachers

explanation.correct: Sec. 5 places the Board under the PRC.

wrong.1: The Board is under the PRC.
wrong.2: The Board is under the PRC.

subject: The Teaching Profession
stem: Members of the Board for Professional Teachers are appointed by:
options: The President, from PRC recommendees nominated by the accredited teachers' association
The Senate, by majority vote of its members
The teachers of each region, by election
The DepEd Secretary alone, without nominations

explanation.correct: Sec. 5 describes this.

subject: The Teaching Profession
stem: Before practicing, every registered professional teacher must:
options: Pass a second LET after one year of teaching
Teach for free for six months
Obtain a barangay certificate of good conduct only

explanation.correct: Sec. 18 requires the oath.

subject: The Teaching Profession
stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the Board's duties under RA 7836 Sec. 6?
options: Setting the salaries of public school teachers
Fixing the dates and places of the exam
Adopting a code of ethical and professional standards

explanation.correct: The duties include issuing or revoking certificates, fixing exam dates and adopting a code of ethics.

subject: The Teaching Profession
stem: Under RA 4670, a teacher hired on provisional status for lack of eligibility serves a probation of at least:

explanation.correct: Sec. 4 sets at least one year.

wrong.1: The law says at least one year.
wrong.2: Ten years is for becoming permanent.
wrong.3: The law says at least one year.

subject: The Teaching Profession
stem: Under RA 4670, what is the policy on discrimination against teachers?
options: No discrimination in entering, practicing or leaving the profession on non-professional grounds
Discrimination is allowed in private schools only
Only married teachers may be hired
Teachers may be dismissed for their religion

explanation.correct: Sec. 10 states this.

wrong.1: RA 4670 covers public school teachers and bars discrimination.

subject: The Teaching Profession
stem: A teacher couple both work in public schools but are assigned to towns far apart. What does RA 4670 say?
options: Whenever possible, they should be employed in the same locality
They must always teach in the same school
Nothing; the law does not address married teachers

explanation.correct: Sec. 11 states this.

wrong.1: The law does not require this.
wrong.2: The law says same locality whenever possible.

subject: The Teaching Profession
stem: Under RA 4670, teachers enjoy academic freedom especially in:

explanation.correct: Sec. 12 states this.

subject: The Teaching Profession
stem: After teaching six hours, a teacher coaches the school's cooking contest team for two more hours. What does RA 4670 provide?
options: At least 25% additional compensation for the extra co-curricular work
No pay, since coaching is volunteer work
Double pay for the whole day
A day off the next month instead of pay

explanation.correct: Sec. 14 provides this.

subject: The Teaching Profession
stem: A teacher's professional ID card is due for renewal, but she has taken no CPD programs. Under RA 10912:
options: She must meet the CPD requirement to renew
She may renew freely, since CPD is optional
She must retake the whole LET
She loses her license permanently with no remedy

explanation.correct: CPD is mandatory for renewal.

wrong.2: The law requires CPD, not a new LET.
wrong.3: The requirement is CPD for renewal.

subject: The Teaching Profession
stem: Under RA 10627, bullying is committed by:
options: One or more students against another student

explanation.correct: The law defines bullying between students.

subject: The Teaching Profession
stem: Under RA 10627, who must report bullying they witness?
options: School staff, students, parents and volunteers

explanation.correct: Sec. 4 lists them.

subject: The Teaching Profession
stem: Under the Safe Spaces Act, school heads must:
options: Post the Act, run prevention measures and create an independent mechanism to investigate complaints
Settle all complaints privately without records
Refer all complaints to the barangay only
Ignore complaints unless the police file them

explanation.correct: Sec. 22 lists these duties.

wrong.2: Schools must have their own mechanism.

subject: The Teaching Profession
stem: A teacher repeatedly calls a pupil "stupid" in front of the class to humiliate him. Under RA 7610, this could be:
options: Child abuse, as an act that debases or demeans a child's dignity
Allowed as a form of discipline
Only a matter of school etiquette
Bullying under RA 10627, since a teacher did it

explanation.correct: Sec. 3(b) includes such acts and emotional maltreatment.

wrong.2: The law treats it as possible abuse.

subject: Curriculum
stem: Which question comes FIRST in Tyler's rationale?
options: What educational purposes should the school seek to attain?
How can learning experiences be organized?
How can learning experiences be selected?

explanation.correct: Tyler starts with purposes (objectives).

subject: Curriculum
stem: Ralph Tyler is often called the father of:

explanation.correct: Tyler headed evaluation for the Eight-Year Study and is called the father of educational evaluation.

subject: Curriculum
stem: Tyler's statement "It is what he does that he learns, not what the teacher does" stresses:
options: The learner's own experiences as the source of learning
The teacher's lecture as the main source of learning
Testing as the only goal of school

explanation.correct: Tyler emphasized learning experiences.

subject: Curriculum
stem: Tyler's book Basic Principles of Curriculum and Instruction was published in:

explanation.correct: The book appeared in 1949.

wrong.1: 1998 is when Understanding by Design appeared.

subject: Curriculum
stem: Which order follows the three stages of Understanding by Design (backward design)?
options: Identify desired results, determine assessment evidence, plan learning activities
Plan activities, determine evidence, identify results
Determine evidence, plan activities, identify results
Identify results, plan activities, determine evidence

explanation.correct: These are the three stages.

subject: Curriculum
stem: A teacher starts planning a unit by choosing fun activities from the textbook, then decides later what students should learn. What habit does backward design respond to?
options: Starting planning with activities and textbooks instead of goals
Writing objectives that are too specific

explanation.correct: Backward design responds to this habit.

wrong.1: The problem is starting with activities.
wrong.2: That is not the habit described.
wrong.3: That is not the habit described.

subject: Curriculum
stem: Who developed Understanding by Design?

explanation.correct: They developed UbD in 1998.

wrong.2: They are linked to the taxonomy.

subject: Curriculum
stem: Fractions appear in Grade 3, again in Grade 5 with operations, and again in Grade 7 in algebra. Which design principle is this?

explanation.correct: Revisiting a topic at a more sophisticated level is a spiral curriculum.

wrong.1: Backward design is a planning sequence.
wrong.2: The hidden curriculum is unintended learning.

subject: Curriculum
stem: Students learn from daily routines that boys carry chairs and girls sweep the floor, though no lesson says so. This is:

explanation.correct: Lessons learned but not openly intended form the hidden curriculum.

subject: Curriculum
stem: Under RA 10533, secondary education consists of:
options: Four years of junior high school and two years of senior high school
Six years of junior high school only
Two years of junior high and four years of senior high
Four years of high school, as before 2013

explanation.correct: Sec. 4 sets 4 + 2 years.

subject: Curriculum
stem: Under RA 10533, the typical entrant age to senior high school is:

explanation.correct: Typical entrant ages are 6 (Grade 1), 12 (JHS) and 16 (SHS).

subject: Curriculum
stem: Under RA 10533, which agency formulates the basic education curriculum?
options: DepEd, working with CHED and TESDA

explanation.correct: Sec. 5 assigns this to DepEd with CHED and TESDA.

subject: Curriculum
stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the curriculum standards and principles in RA 10533 Sec. 5?
options: Exclusive and fixed for all regions

explanation.correct: The law calls for learner-centered, inclusive, relevant, culture-sensitive, contextualized and global curricula.

subject: Curriculum
stem: Under RA 10533, who chairs the Curriculum Consultative Committee?

explanation.correct: Sec. 6 makes the DepEd Secretary chair.

wrong.3: The President does not chair it.

subject: Curriculum
stem: Under RA 10533, approval of locally produced teaching materials is devolved to:

explanation.correct: Sec. 5(h) devolves approval to regional and division offices.

wrong.2: Approval is at regional and division levels.

subject: Curriculum
stem: What did RA 12027 (2024) do to the mother tongue as medium of instruction in kindergarten to Grade 3?
options: Discontinued it; instruction reverts to Filipino and English
Made it compulsory in all private schools
Replaced English with the mother tongue in college

explanation.correct: RA 12027 discontinued mother tongue as medium of instruction.

wrong.3: That is not what it did.

subject: Curriculum
stem: Under RA 12027, regional languages may still be used as:
options: The sole medium of all examinations
The only language for science classes

explanation.correct: Regional languages remain auxiliary media.

subject: Curriculum
stem: Under RA 12027, MTB-MLE may still be used in which classes?
options: Monolingual classes that meet requirements such as KWF orthography and trained teachers
All classes in every region, without conditions

explanation.correct: Sec. 2 allows this.

subject: Curriculum
stem: Which document organizes standards into specific skills (the scope and sequence) and names observable behaviors?
options: A standards statement, which is very general

explanation.correct: A curriculum framework organizes standards into skills and behaviors.

wrong.2: Neither standards nor frameworks are daily plans.

subject: Curriculum
stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the three features of a Mager behavioral objective?

explanation.correct: Mager's features are observable behavior, conditions, and a minimum acceptable level.

subject: Curriculum
stem: Which objective best follows Mager's format?
options: Given a recipe, the learner will measure dry ingredients with no errors within 5 minutes.
The teacher will demonstrate measuring dry ingredients.
The learner will appreciate the value of baking.

explanation.correct: It has a condition, an observable behavior and a criterion.

subject: Curriculum
stem: How do Gronlund's cognitive approach and Mager's behavioral approach to objectives differ?
options: Gronlund goes from general goals to specific indicators; Mager starts with specific behaviors
They are the same approach with different names

explanation.correct: The source contrasts them this way.

subject: Curriculum
stem: In the 2001 revision of Bloom's taxonomy, which original level was renamed "Create" and moved to the top?

explanation.correct: Synthesis became Create and was moved above Evaluate.

subject: Curriculum
stem: Bloom's original 1956 taxonomy was developed by:
options: A committee chaired by Benjamin Bloom

explanation.correct: The taxonomy came from a committee chaired by Bloom.

wrong.1: Simpson proposed a psychomotor taxonomy in 1972.
wrong.3: Bruner is linked to the spiral curriculum.

subject: Curriculum
stem: Who proposed a seven-level psychomotor taxonomy in 1972?

explanation.correct: Simpson proposed the psychomotor taxonomy.

subject: Curriculum
stem: Students judge which of three meal plans best meets a family's nutrient needs and defend their choice. Which revised Bloom level is this?

explanation.correct: Judging against criteria and defending a choice is Evaluate.

subject: Curriculum
stem: A curriculum team asks, "How will we know whether these cooking activities actually achieved our goals?" Which Tyler question is this?
options: How can the effectiveness of learning experiences be evaluated?
What educational purposes should the school seek?
How can learning experiences be selected?
How can learning experiences be organized?

explanation.correct: This is Tyler's fourth question.

subject: Curriculum
stem: A team lists possible field trips, demonstrations and lab tasks that could help reach its objectives. Which Tyler question are they answering?
options: How can learning experiences be selected?
What purposes should the school seek?

explanation.correct: Choosing experiences is the second question.

wrong.3: That is not a Tyler question.

subject: Curriculum
stem: Tyler led evaluation for which famous study (1933–1941)?

explanation.correct: Tyler headed evaluation for the Eight-Year Study.

wrong.3: That is not in our source.

subject: Curriculum
stem: Before planning any activity, a teacher writes the essential question "Why do foods spoil?" and decides students will show understanding by designing a storage guide. Which approach is this?

explanation.correct: Starting with desired results and evidence is backward design.

wrong.1: Tyler starts with purposes but UbD puts evidence before activities.
wrong.2: That is the habit UbD responds to.
wrong.3: That concerns revisiting topics across grades.

subject: Curriculum
stem: What is the key difference between Tyler's rationale and backward design?
options: Backward design plans assessment evidence before learning activities
Tyler plans evaluation first, before purposes

explanation.correct: UbD puts assessment before activities.

wrong.3: Tyler's evaluation is the fourth question.

subject: Curriculum
stem: In Stage 1 of Understanding by Design, teachers identify desired results such as:

explanation.correct: Stage 1 names understandings and essential questions.

subject: Curriculum
stem: Which theorist is associated with the spiral curriculum?

explanation.correct: Bruner proposed the spiral curriculum.

wrong.3: Dale proposed the Cone of Experience.

subject: Curriculum
stem: RA 10533 says the K to 12 curriculum uses which approach to sequence content across grades?

explanation.correct: The law names the spiral progression approach.

wrong.1: That is not a curriculum approach in the law.
wrong.2: That is not in the law.
wrong.3: That is not in the law.

subject: Curriculum
stem: Learners notice that only students with expensive uniforms are chosen to greet visitors, and they learn that appearance matters more than effort. This is:

explanation.correct: Unintended lessons from the school environment form the hidden curriculum.

subject: Curriculum
stem: According to our source, the hidden curriculum can:
options: Replace the official curriculum by law

explanation.correct: The source notes it can reinforce inequality.

wrong.1: It conveys norms, values and beliefs.

subject: Curriculum
stem: Under RA 10533, kindergarten entrants are at least how old?

explanation.correct: Kindergarten entrants are at least 5.

wrong.2: That is the typical Grade 1 entrant age.

subject: Curriculum
stem: Under RA 10533, the typical entrant age to Grade 1 is:

explanation.correct: The typical Grade 1 entrant age is 6.

subject: Curriculum
stem: A curriculum that uses local foods, dialects and community examples while connecting to global issues follows which K to 12 principle?

explanation.correct: Sec. 5 lists contextualized and global curricula.

subject: Curriculum
stem: Which agency is NOT named in RA 10533 Sec. 5 as working with or consulted by DepEd on the curriculum?

explanation.correct: DepEd works with CHED and TESDA and consults DOLE, PRC, schools, teachers, parents and industry.

subject: Curriculum
stem: Under RA 12027, which agency develops a language-mapping policy with DepEd?

explanation.correct: DepEd and KWF develop language mapping.

subject: Curriculum
stem: Which document is MORE detailed than a curriculum framework?

explanation.correct: A curriculum guide is more detailed still.

wrong.2: That is not a curriculum document.
wrong.3: That is not a curriculum document.

subject: Curriculum
stem: According to Seifert and Sutton, standards and curriculum frameworks:
options: Do not lay out daily activity plans

explanation.correct: Neither lays out daily plans.

subject: Curriculum
stem: In the objective "Given a pattern, the learner will cut the fabric within 3 mm of the line," which part is the criterion?

explanation.correct: The criterion is the minimum acceptable level.

subject: Curriculum
stem: In the objective "Given a recipe, the learner will measure flour accurately," which part is the condition?

explanation.correct: The condition states the circumstances of performance.

subject: Curriculum
stem: Good learning objectives describe:

explanation.correct: Objectives describe student actions, not teacher actions.

wrong.3: That is content, not an objective.

subject: Curriculum
stem: Learners classify given foods by their main nutrient class and explain why. Which revised Bloom level is mainly targeted?

explanation.correct: Classifying and explaining fit Understand.

subject: Curriculum
stem: Learners use a given formula to compute the cost per serving of a recipe. Which revised Bloom level is this?

explanation.correct: Using a procedure in a situation is Apply.

subject: Curriculum
stem: Which three domains does Bloom's taxonomy cover?

explanation.correct: These are the three domains.

subject: Curriculum
stem: In which year did the affective-domain handbook appear?

explanation.correct: The affective handbook appeared in 1964.

subject: Curriculum
stem: Which order follows Tyler's four questions?
options: Purposes, selecting experiences, organizing experiences, evaluating
Evaluating, purposes, organizing experiences, selecting experiences
Selecting experiences, evaluating, purposes, organizing experiences
Organizing experiences, selecting experiences, evaluating, purposes

explanation.correct: These are Tyler's questions in order.

subject: Curriculum
stem: In Stage 2 of backward design, teachers determine:
options: The textbook chapters to cover first, before goals
The seating plan for the classroom
The final grades of the previous class

explanation.correct: Stage 2 is assessment evidence.

wrong.1: That is the habit UbD avoids.
wrong.2: That is not a UbD stage.
wrong.3: That is not a UbD stage.

subject: Curriculum
stem: Understanding by Design was first published in:

explanation.correct: Wiggins and McTighe published UbD in 1998.

subject: Curriculum
stem: A spiral curriculum links later learning to:
options: Earlier learning of the same topic
Nothing, since each year starts fresh

explanation.correct: Each revisit builds on earlier learning.

subject: Curriculum
stem: The hidden curriculum is conveyed through:
options: Only textbooks approved by the region

explanation.correct: Norms, values and beliefs come through the environment.

subject: Curriculum
stem: Under RA 10533, kindergarten education is a prerequisite for:

explanation.correct: Kindergarten is a prerequisite for Grade 1.

subject: Curriculum
stem: A curriculum unit includes learners with disabilities and adjusts to their developmental level. Which K to 12 standard does this follow?
options: Exclusive and fixed for all learners regardless of need

explanation.correct: Sec. 5(a) lists this.

subject: Curriculum
stem: The Curriculum Consultative Committee under RA 10533 includes representatives of:
options: CHED, TESDA, DOLE, PRC, DOST and business
Only parents and students of one school

explanation.correct: Sec. 6 lists these.

subject: Curriculum
stem: Which requirement must monolingual classes meet to keep using MTB-MLE under RA 12027?
options: Use of KWF orthography, documented vocabulary, materials and trained teachers
A class size of at least 100 learners
No teachers trained in the language

explanation.correct: Sec. 2 lists these.

subject: Curriculum
stem: Which objective is NOT observable, and so does not fit Mager's format?
options: The learner will appreciate Filipino cuisine.
The learner will list five Filipino dishes.
The learner will slice onions into even rings.
The learner will plate a dish within 3 minutes.

explanation.correct: "Appreciate" cannot be directly observed.

subject: Curriculum
stem: Planning, per Seifert and Sutton, needs both:
options: Only daily activities with no goals
Only national standards, no classroom objectives

explanation.correct: The source says both are needed.

subject: Curriculum
stem: Learners design an original healthy snack recipe for a school fair. Which revised Bloom level is this?

explanation.correct: Producing an original product is Create.

subject: Curriculum
stem: Learners compare two brands of canned tuna by price per gram and ingredients to find differences. Which revised Bloom level is this?

explanation.correct: Breaking information into parts and comparing is Analyze.

subject: Curriculum
stem: Under RA 10533, junior high school's typical entrant age is:

explanation.correct: Typical entrant ages are 6, 12 and 16.

subject: Curriculum
stem: In the original 1956 taxonomy, which level was at the top?

explanation.correct: The original top level was Evaluation, above Synthesis.

wrong.1: Create is the top level of the 2001 revision.

subject: Curriculum
stem: The "scope and sequence" of skills is found in a:

explanation.correct: A framework organizes standards into a scope and sequence.

subject: Methods and Strategies
stem: Before a lesson on food preservation, a teacher shows a one-slide chart grouping methods into "heat", "cold", "drying" and "chemical". This is:
options: A summative test given at the start of the unit

explanation.correct: A brief overview that partly organizes the material before it is presented is an advance organizer (Ausubel).

subject: Methods and Strategies
stem: Who proposed advance organizers?
options: Madeline Hunter, in her lesson-design model

explanation.correct: Ausubel (1978) proposed advance organizers.

wrong.1: Hunter uses advance organizers but did not propose them.
wrong.2: Engelmann is linked to direct instruction.

subject: Methods and Strategies
stem: A concept map is usually:
options: A diagram of relationships among concepts, made by the student
A list of class rules posted on the wall at the start of the year
A test blueprint showing the number of items per topic
A seating chart drawn by the principal

explanation.correct: Concept maps are usually student-made diagrams of relationships.

wrong.2: That is a table of specifications.
wrong.3: That is not a concept map.

subject: Methods and Strategies
stem: What is the central assumption of mastery learning?
options: All students can learn to the same high level, though some need more time
Only gifted students can master difficult content, so others are grouped apart
Students should be ranked after one test only
Time for learning must be identical for everyone

explanation.correct: Mastery learning assumes all can reach a high level.

wrong.2: Mastery learning uses ungraded tests and retests.
wrong.3: Time varies; the level is fixed.

subject: Methods and Strategies
stem: Which sequence matches the typical mastery-learning cycle?
options: Brief lesson, ungraded test, enrichment or tutoring, retest
Graded final exam, then the lesson, then tutoring, then promotion to the next unit

explanation.correct: This is the typical cycle.

wrong.1: The test after the lesson is ungraded.

subject: Methods and Strategies
stem: Direct instruction (Engelmann) combines which ideas?
options: Behaviorist praise with cognitive features such as stated objectives and frequent review
Free play with no stated objectives and no review, so children set their own pace
Psychoanalytic dream analysis with group therapy

explanation.correct: The source describes this mix.

wrong.3: Discovery is the opposite of scripted instruction.

subject: Methods and Strategies
stem: In Madeline Hunter's model, using the start of the lesson, an advance organizer and an explicit objective belong to which step?
options: Checking for understanding during the lesson

explanation.correct: These are listed under preparing students to learn.

wrong.3: That is not a Hunter step.

subject: Methods and Strategies
stem: In a group project, two members do all the work while others coast, and all get the same grade. Which problem of cooperative learning is this?

explanation.correct: A single group grade for everyone can allow freeloading.

wrong.1: That happens when only individual contributions are graded.

subject: Methods and Strategies
stem: A teacher grades only each member's own part of a group report. Students then refuse to learn anything outside their own section. Which problem is this?

explanation.correct: Grading only individual contributions can lead to overspecialization.

wrong.1: Freeloading arises from a single group grade.
wrong.2: That is a loss of perceived control.

subject: Methods and Strategies
stem: Each home-group member studies one food group in an "expert group" and then teaches it back to the home group. Which strategy is this?
options: STAD, with individual tests and team points

explanation.correct: Experts on one part teach it to the home group in jigsaw.

wrong.1: STAD teams study together, then take individual tests.

subject: Methods and Strategies
stem: In STAD (Student Teams–Achievement Divisions), how are students tested?
options: Individually, with team scores based on improvement
Only as a group, with one shared answer sheet for the whole team
Only by the principal at the end of the year

explanation.correct: STAD tests individuals and builds team scores.

subject: Methods and Strategies
stem: Over three weeks, groups investigate "How can our barangay reduce food waste?" and present a report to the barangay council. Which strategy is this?

explanation.correct: An extended investigation ending in a presentation or product is project-based learning.

wrong.2: Jigsaw is a short cooperative format.

subject: Methods and Strategies
stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the factors Seifert and Sutton name for choosing an instructional strategy?
options: The color of the classroom walls
The forms of thinking to encourage
How much ideas must be organized by the teacher
How much responsibility students take for their learning

explanation.correct: The factors are the forms of thinking to encourage, how much the teacher organizes ideas, and how much responsibility students take.

subject: Methods and Strategies
stem: Under RA 10533, the K to 12 curriculum proceeds:
options: From the known to the unknown
From the abstract to the concrete
From the hardest topics to the easiest
In random order to build flexibility

explanation.correct: Sec. 5 says the curriculum proceeds from the known to the unknown.

subject: Methods and Strategies
stem: Media literacy is the ability to:
options: Access, analyze, evaluate and create media, and act ethically
Memorize the names and channel numbers of TV and radio stations

explanation.correct: The source defines media literacy this way.

wrong.3: Media literacy engages with media critically.

subject: Methods and Strategies
stem: Who first defined digital literacy, in 1997?

explanation.correct: Gilster defined digital literacy in 1997.

wrong.2: Banks described dimensions of multicultural education.

subject: Methods and Strategies
stem: Henry Jenkins distinguished which gap from the digital divide?

explanation.correct: Jenkins described the participation gap.

subject: Methods and Strategies
stem: Ecological literacy (ecoliteracy) was developed by:

explanation.correct: The source credits Orr and Capra in the 1990s.

wrong.1: They are linked to digital literacy.

subject: Methods and Strategies
stem: A unit teaches learners to compare loan offers and plan a monthly allowance. Which new literacy does this build?

explanation.correct: Making informed decisions about money is financial literacy.

wrong.3: That is literacy learned through interaction.

subject: Methods and Strategies
stem: Which of the following is NOT one of James Banks's dimensions of multicultural education?
options: Prejudice reduction among students of different groups

explanation.correct: Banks's dimensions are content integration, knowledge construction, prejudice reduction, equity pedagogy and empowering school culture.

subject: Methods and Strategies
stem: After a short lesson on knife cuts, a teacher gives an ungraded quiz, tutors those who did not reach the standard, gives enrichment to the rest, then retests. This is:

explanation.correct: The cycle of lesson, ungraded test, tutoring or enrichment, and retest is mastery learning.

wrong.1: Jigsaw uses expert and home groups.
wrong.3: Inquiry has learners investigate open questions.

subject: Methods and Strategies
stem: Which is a challenge of mastery learning named by Seifert and Sutton?
options: Fairness between enrichment and remediation, and the need for a detailed curriculum of small units
It cannot be used with any tests
It only works for college students

explanation.correct: The source names these challenges.

wrong.1: It uses ungraded tests and retests.
wrong.2: It needs a detailed, organized curriculum.

subject: Methods and Strategies
stem: For which learners is direct instruction described as very effective?
options: Basic skills such as early reading and arithmetic, especially in K–3
Only learners in open-ended art projects
Only learners who already mastered the content

explanation.correct: The source says so.

subject: Methods and Strategies
stem: A Grade 1 teacher follows a scripted lesson, praises correct answers immediately, states the objective, and reviews often in small steps. This is:

explanation.correct: A highly scripted approach with praise, stated objectives and frequent review is direct instruction.

subject: Methods and Strategies
stem: Midway through a lesson, a teacher asks a question every learner answers on mini-boards, then samples a few individuals. Which Hunter step is this?
options: Checking for understanding and guided practice

explanation.correct: Questions everyone answers and sampling individuals are listed here.

subject: Methods and Strategies
stem: A teacher does the first two practice items together with the class, then lets learners finish a short set with feedback. Which Hunter step is this?

explanation.correct: The source says do the first few together and keep practice brief with feedback.

wrong.3: That is not a Hunter step.

subject: Methods and Strategies
stem: In Hunter's model, presenting information clearly includes:
options: A set structure, familiar examples and concise explanation
Long, unplanned stories to fill time

explanation.correct: The source lists these.

wrong.1: That is the opposite of concise.

subject: Methods and Strategies
stem: Besides concept maps, which strategies help learners organize expository material, per our source?
options: Copying the textbook word for word

explanation.correct: The source names outlining and note-taking.

subject: Methods and Strategies
stem: During a lecture, students may look passive, but our source says they must:
options: Make an effort to listen in order to learn
Do nothing at all to learn

explanation.correct: Learning from exposition requires active listening.

wrong.1: The source says effort is needed.

subject: Methods and Strategies
stem: A teacher asks, "Why does bread rise more in a warm place?" and lets groups test it without telling them the answer. This is:

explanation.correct: The teacher poses questions and does not answer directly.

wrong.2: That is about reaching a standard before moving on.

subject: Methods and Strategies
stem: Which thinkers are linked with inquiry learning in our source?

explanation.correct: The source names both.

subject: Methods and Strategies
stem: What do students need for cooperative learning to work, per our source?
options: Time and a place to work together
Individual grades only, never group rewards
No guidance from the teacher at all

explanation.correct: The source names time and place.

wrong.2: Group success is part of the definition.

subject: Methods and Strategies
stem: Which researchers are linked with the jigsaw classroom in our source?

explanation.correct: The source names them.

subject: Methods and Strategies
stem: Teams of four study a nutrition unit together; each member then takes a quiz alone, and the team earns points based on members' improvement. This is:

explanation.correct: STAD tests individuals and scores partly on improvement.

wrong.3: That is a collection of work.

subject: Methods and Strategies
stem: How large are STAD teams in our source?

explanation.correct: STAD teams have 4–5 members.

subject: Methods and Strategies
stem: Student-centered strategies such as inquiry and projects differ from teacher-directed ones mainly in that:
options: Learners direct more of their own work
The teacher explains everything in a lecture

explanation.correct: Student-centered strategies give learners more responsibility.

subject: Methods and Strategies
stem: Under RA 10533, which kinds of pedagogy should the K to 12 curriculum use?
options: Constructivist, inquiry-based, reflective, collaborative and integrative
Only lecture with no student activity

explanation.correct: Sec. 5 lists these.

subject: Methods and Strategies
stem: Learners analyze a TV advertisement for a sugary drink, identify its target audience and techniques, and create their own honest ad. Which literacy is developed?

explanation.correct: Accessing, analyzing, evaluating and creating media is media literacy.

wrong.3: That is about learning through interaction.

subject: Methods and Strategies
stem: Digital literacy is the ability to:
options: Find, evaluate and communicate information using digital devices

explanation.correct: The source defines it this way.

subject: Methods and Strategies
stem: A class studies how a mangrove ecosystem supports fisherfolk and plans ways to keep the community sustainable. Which literacy is this?

explanation.correct: Ecoliteracy uses ecological principles to build sustainable communities.

subject: Methods and Strategies
stem: In the sociocultural view, social literacy is learned through:
options: Social interaction with peers and adults, using books, games, conversations and stories

explanation.correct: The source describes it this way.

subject: Methods and Strategies
stem: A teacher adds Maranao, Ifugao and Tausug dishes to the cookery unit and explains their cultural meanings. Which Banks dimension is this?

explanation.correct: Using examples from diverse cultures is content integration.

wrong.1: That adjusts teaching to help diverse learners achieve.
wrong.3: That changes the whole school's culture.

subject: Methods and Strategies
stem: Before reading a chapter on fabrics, learners draw a diagram linking "fiber", "yarn", "weave" and "fabric" with labeled arrows. This is a:
options: Rubric with criteria and performance levels for grading
Table of specifications for a unit test
Behavioral objective with a condition and criterion

explanation.correct: A student-made diagram of relationships among concepts is a concept map.

wrong.1: A rubric is a scoring guide.

subject: Methods and Strategies
stem: In mastery learning, the test given right after the first brief lesson is:
options: The final graded exam that decides promotion to the next year
Skipped entirely so learners are not stressed
Given only to the top learners in the class

explanation.correct: The first test is ungraded; it decides who needs tutoring or enrichment.

wrong.2: The test is part of the cycle.

subject: Methods and Strategies
stem: Which order follows Madeline Hunter's effective teaching model?
options: Prepare students, present information, check understanding with guided practice, independent practice
Independent practice, present information, prepare students, check understanding at the end
Check understanding, prepare students, independent practice, present information last
Present information, independent practice, prepare students, guided practice at the end

explanation.correct: These are the steps in order.

subject: Methods and Strategies
stem: In cooperative learning, groups are rewarded:
options: Partly or wholly for group success
Only for beating every other group in a contest
Never, since rewards spoil cooperation in every case
Only by the principal at the end of the year

explanation.correct: That is the source's definition.

wrong.1: That is competition, not the definition.

subject: Methods and Strategies
stem: In a jigsaw lesson on food preservation, Marco joins the "drying" expert group. What does he do next?
options: Return to his home group and teach the drying method to them
Stay in the expert group and take a separate test only on drying
Present drying to the whole school assembly
Skip the other parts because he already knows drying well

explanation.correct: Experts teach their part back to the home group.

wrong.3: He learns the other parts from teammates.

subject: Methods and Strategies
stem: A teacher wants learners to take more responsibility for directing their own learning. Which kind of strategy fits best?
options: A student-centered strategy such as inquiry or a project
A tightly scripted direct-instruction lesson led by the teacher
A long lecture with notes copied from the board
A silent drill with answers given by the teacher

explanation.correct: Student-centered strategies give learners more responsibility.

wrong.1: That keeps control with the teacher.

subject: Methods and Strategies
stem: Which term did Henry Jenkins use to say that access to technology alone is not enough?

explanation.correct: Jenkins distinguished the participation gap from the digital divide.

subject: Methods and Strategies
stem: Financial literacy includes which components, per our source?
options: Skills, knowledge, behavior and attitude for informed money decisions
Only the ability to count coins quickly at a store
Only knowing the names of all banks in the country
Only memorizing tax rates set by the government

explanation.correct: The source defines it this way.

subject: Methods and Strategies
stem: A teacher changes her methods so learners from different cultural and social backgrounds can all achieve well. Which Banks dimension is this?
options: Content integration of examples from many cultures
Knowledge construction about how knowledge is made

explanation.correct: Modifying teaching to help diverse students achieve is equity pedagogy.

subject: Methods and Strategies
stem: A teacher uses materials and activities aimed at changing negative racial attitudes among learners. Which Banks dimension is this?
options: Content integration of cultural examples into lessons
Equity pedagogy that changes methods for achievement
Empowering the whole school culture and structure

explanation.correct: That dimension focuses on modifying attitudes through methods and materials.

subject: Methods and Strategies
stem: Lecture or exposition is defined as:
options: Telling or explaining previously organized information
Students investigating questions without any teacher input
Students teaching each other in expert groups
A long-term project ending in a product

explanation.correct: That is the source's definition.

subject: Methods and Strategies
stem: In a mastery-learning class, some learners pass the first quiz. What do they receive while others are tutored?
options: A failing grade for finishing early

explanation.correct: Those who master it get enrichment.

wrong.3: Tutoring is for those who did not master it.

subject: Methods and Strategies
stem: Madeline Hunter's model is also called:

explanation.correct: The source calls it mastery teaching.

subject: Methods and Strategies
stem: Inquiry learning is also called discovery learning, a term associated with:

explanation.correct: The source links discovery learning to Bruner.

wrong.2: Canter is linked to assertive discipline.

subject: Methods and Strategies
stem: Project-based learning, as described by Katz, ends with:
options: A presentation, report or other product

explanation.correct: Projects end in a product or presentation.

wrong.1: That is not the defining end.

subject: Methods and Strategies
stem: According to Seifert and Sutton, good teachers:
options: Use only lectures for every lesson
Use only projects and never explain anything

explanation.correct: The source says good teachers mix them.

subject: Methods and Strategies
stem: Media literacy includes the ability to reflect critically and to:
options: Avoid all forms of media forever

explanation.correct: Media literacy includes acting ethically.

subject: Methods and Strategies
stem: Multicultural education is defined in our source as strategies that:
options: Teach the histories, cultures and contributions of diverse groups
Replace all subjects with cultural studies

explanation.correct: That is the definition.

subject: Educational Technology and Classroom Management
stem: Edgar Dale's Cone of Experience was meant to show:
options: How concrete or abstract different audiovisual media are
Exact percentages of what learners remember from each medium
The order of Piaget's cognitive stages
The cost of each kind of teaching material

explanation.correct: Dale's cone is an intuitive model of the concreteness of media.

subject: Educational Technology and Classroom Management
stem: In which year did Dale first introduce the Cone of Experience?
options: 1969, the year of its final revision
2001, the year of the revised taxonomy

explanation.correct: Dale introduced it in 1946 and revised it in 1954 and 1969.

subject: Educational Technology and Classroom Management
stem: What is the difference between classroom procedures and rules in Seifert and Sutton?
options: Procedures are routines for repeated tasks; rules are standards of behavior students take responsibility for
Procedures are punishments for breaking rules; rules are rewards for following procedures
Rules are for teachers; procedures are for parents
They are the same thing under two names

explanation.correct: The source distinguishes them this way.

subject: Educational Technology and Classroom Management
stem: A teacher wants students to help write class guidelines. According to the source, students' involvement is MORE justified for:
options: Rules, because they concern personal responsibility
Procedures such as how papers are passed forward and collected each day
Bell schedules set by the division office
Seating charts for fire drills only

explanation.correct: There is a stronger case for student input on rules than on procedures.

wrong.1: Procedures are like conventions; input matters less.

subject: Educational Technology and Classroom Management
stem: What does the source advise about classroom displays?
options: Reinforce curriculum and student work, but avoid making the room too busy
Cover every wall completely on the first day so the room looks finished and lively
Avoid displaying student work at all

explanation.correct: Too many displays make a room busy.

subject: Educational Technology and Classroom Management
stem: Why should teachers plan classroom transitions carefully?
options: Transitions waste time and invite misbehavior
Transitions are the best time to give tests
Transitions never cause problems if rules exist

explanation.correct: The source names lost time and misbehavior.

wrong.2: That law does not regulate transitions.

subject: Educational Technology and Classroom Management
stem: While helping one group, a teacher notices two students passing notes across the room and signals them to stop without leaving the group. This shows:
options: The ripple effect of ignored misbehavior

explanation.correct: Awareness of everything (withitness) lets the teacher respond to several events at once (overlapping).

wrong.1: The teacher acted; the ripple effect follows ignored misbehavior.
wrong.2: No consequence followed on its own.

subject: Educational Technology and Classroom Management
stem: Kounin's "ripple effect" refers to:
options: Misbehavior that spreads to others when left alone
Good behavior that spreads and improves the test scores of the class
A wave of applause after a lesson
Feedback that is delayed by a week

explanation.correct: The ripple effect is contagious misbehavior.

subject: Educational Technology and Classroom Management
stem: A student taps a pencil quietly once during seatwork; no one else notices. What response does the source suggest may be wise?
options: Sending the student to the principal
Stopping the class for a long lecture on rules

explanation.correct: Ignoring may be wise when behavior is minor and unlikely to disrupt others.
